translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Lu Yi was demoted to Prince of Yi lecturer.

sentences.zh: 己丑，上宴全忠於壽春殿。

translations.literal: On jichou the emperor feasted Quanzhong at Shouchun Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou he feasted Quanzhong at Shouchun Hall.

sentences.zh: 又令全忠與茂貞書，取平原公主。

translations.literal: He again ordered Quanzhong write Maozhen for Princess Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Quanzhong write Maozhen for Princess Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 同州節度使趙翊、陝州節度使朱友謙來朝。

translations.literal: Tongzhou Commissioner Zhao Yi and Shanzhou Commissioner Zhu Youqian came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi and Zhu Youqian came to audience.

sentences.zh: 制以朱友裕為華州刺史，充感化軍節度使。

translations.literal: An edict made Zhu Youyu Hua Prefect and Commissioner of Ganhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Zhu Youyu Ganhua commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乙未，會鞠于保甯殿，全忠得頭籌，令內弟子送酒，仍面賜副元帥官告。

translations.literal: On yiwei, a ball game was held at Baoning Hall; Quanzhong won the lead token, ordered inner consorts' sons bring wine, and face-to-face granted the vice commander-in-chief's commission.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei at Baoning Hall Quanzhong won the lead token and granted Pei Shu's commission.

sentences.zh: 以新除廣州節度使裴樞為門下侍郎、吏部尚書、平章事、監修國史；

translations.literal: Newly appointed Guangzhou Commissioner Pei Shu was made Vice Director, Minister of Personnel, Grand Councilor, Commissioner for Editing the National History;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu was made vice director and grand councilor;

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎王溥同平章事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Pu was made Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu was made grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，全忠歸大梁，上宴之內殿，置酒於延喜門。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Quanzhong returned to Daliang; the emperor feasted him in the inner hall and set wine at Yanxi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Quanzhong returned to Daliang; the emperor feasted him at Yanxi Gate.

sentences.zh: 是日，全忠與四鎮判官皆預席，上臨軒泣別，又令中使走送御製《楊柳枝》詞五首賜之。

translations.literal: That day Quanzhong and the four commands' judges all attended; the emperor faced the hall weeping farewell and ordered inner envoys gallop to send five composed "Willow Branch" lyrics as gift.
translations.idiomatic: That day judges attended; the emperor wept farewell and sent five "Willow Branch" lyrics.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，平原公主至京師。

translations.literal: On xinchou Princess Pingyuan reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Princess Pingyuan arrived.

sentences.zh: 三月壬寅朔，全忠引四鎮之兵征王師範。

translations.literal: In the third month, on renyin, the first day, Quanzhong led four commands' troops against Wang Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, renyin new moon: Quanzhong led four commands against Wang Shifan.

sentences.zh: 先是，大將朱友甯、楊師厚前軍臨淄、青，師範求援于淮南，楊行密遣將王景仁帥眾萬人赴之。

translations.literal: Before this, generals Zhu Youning and Yang Shihou's vanguard reached Linzi and Qing; Shifan begged Huainan aid; Yang Xingmi sent Wang Jingren with ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Before this Youning and Yang Shihou reached Linzi; Shifan begged Huainan aid.

sentences.zh: 四月辛未朔，西川王建以兵攻秦、隴，乘茂貞之弱也，仍遣判官韋莊入貢，修好于全忠。

translations.literal: On the fourth month, xinwei, the first day, Sichuan Wang Jian attacked Qin and Long, seizing Maozhen's weakness, and sent Judge Wei Zhuang to present tribute and seek good relations with Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, xinwei new moon: Wang Jian attacked Qin and Long and sent Wei Zhuang to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 五月，制鳳翔隴右四鎮北庭行軍、彰義軍節度、涇原渭武觀察處置押蕃落等使、開府儀同三司、守尚書令、兼侍中、鳳翔尹、上柱國、秦王李茂貞可檢校太師、守中書令。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict: Fengxiang Longyou Four Commands Northern Court Campaign, Zhangyi Commissioner Li Maozhen could be Acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: Maozhen was made acting grand preceptor—he had feared Quanzhong's grand guardian rank.

sentences.zh: 初，茂貞淩弱王室，朝廷姑息，加尚書令，及是全忠方守太尉，茂貞懼，乞罷尚書令故也。

translations.literal: At first Maozhen had bullied the royal house; the court indulged him and added Director of the Department of State Affairs; now Quanzhong held Grand Guardian and Maozhen feared and begged leave the directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen had bullied the court; now he begged leave the directorate.

sentences.zh: 崔胤奏：「六軍十二衛名額空存，實無兵士。

translations.literal: Cui Yin memorialized: "The Six Armies and Twelve Guards exist in name only with no soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin wrote: "Six Armies and Twelve Guards are names without soldiers.

sentences.zh: 京師侍衛，亦藉親軍。

translations.literal: Capital guard also relies on personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: Capital guard relies on personal troops.

sentences.zh: 請每軍量召募一千一百人，共置六千六百人。

translations.literal: I beg each army recruit one thousand one hundred men, altogether six thousand six hundred."
translations.idiomatic: He begged six thousand six hundred recruits."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The edict was assented to.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 乃令六軍諸衛副使、京兆尹鄭元規立格招收於市。

translations.literal: Six Armies and Guards vice commissioners and Jingzhao Magistrate Zheng Yuangui set standards to recruit in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuangui recruited in the market.

sentences.zh: 制以潁州刺史朱友恭檢校司空，兼徐州刺史，充武甯軍節度使，從全忠奏也。

translations.literal: An edict made Yingzhou Prefect Zhu Yougong Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Xuzhou Prefect, Commissioner of Wuning Army—following Quanzhong's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yougong was made Wuning commissioner—per Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 六月，青州、淮南軍與汴人戰於臨淄，汴軍大敗，朱友甯戰死，傳首淮南。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Qing and Huainan armies fought Bian at Linzi; Bian troops were greatly defeated; Zhu Youning died in battle; his head was sent to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: at Linzi Bian was defeated; Zhu Youning died; his head went to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 九月，汴將楊師厚大敗青州軍於臨朐。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Bian general Yang Shihou greatly defeated Qing troops at Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Yang Shihou defeated Qing at Linqu.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使成汭以舟師赴援鄂州，澧朗雷彥恭承虛襲陷江陵。

translations.literal: Jingnan Commissioner Cheng Run led a fleet to aid Ezhou; Li Lang's Lei Yanxi seized the opening and took Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Run sailed to aid Ezhou; Lei Yanxi took Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 汭軍士聞之潰歸，汭憤怒投水而死。

translations.literal: Run's soldiers heard and fled back; Run in rage threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Run's troops fled; Run drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 趙匡凝遂以兵襲荊州，據之。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangning thereupon led troops to attack Jingzhou and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangning then marched on Jingzhou, took it, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，汴州護駕都將朱友倫擊鞠墜馬卒，全忠怒，殺同鞠將校數人。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Zhu Youlun, the Bianzhou escort commander, fell from his horse while playing cuju and died; Quanzhong in rage killed several fellow players and officers.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Zhu Youlun, Bianzhou’s commander of the imperial escort, fell from his horse playing cuju and died. Quanzhong flew into a rage and executed several of the players and their officers.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁酉朔，王師範以青州降楊師厚，全忠復令師範知青州事。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, dingyou, Wang Shifan surrendered Qingzhou to Yang Shihou; Quanzhong again ordered Shifan to know Qingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the first day of the eleventh month, Wang Shifan surrendered Qingzhou to Yang Shihou. Quanzhong restored him to govern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 邠州、鳳翔兵士逼京畿。

translations.literal: Bingzhou and Fengxiang soldiers pressed the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from Bing and Fengxiang closed in on the capital.

sentences.zh: 汴軍屯河中。

translations.literal: Bian armies encamped at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu’s Bian armies camped at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 青州牙將劉鄩以兗州降葛從周，稟師範命也。

translations.literal: Qingzhou staff officer Liu Ye with Yanzhou surrendered to Ge Congzhou, reporting Shifan’s command.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye, a Qingzhou staff officer, surrendered Yanzhou to Ge Congzhou on Wang Shifan’s orders.

sentences.zh: 全忠嘉之，署為元帥府都押衙，權知鄜州留後事。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was pleased and appointed him chief adjutant of the marshal’s headquarters, acting military governor of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong rewarded him with the post of chief adjutant at headquarters and acting military governor of Bin.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁卯朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, dingmao.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the first day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，制以禮部尚書獨孤損為兵部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict appointed Minister of Rites Dugu Sun as Vice Minister of War and co–Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Dugu Sun, Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of War and co–Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 丙申，制守司徒、侍中、太清宮使、弘文館大學士、延資庫使、判六軍十二衛事、諸道鹽鐵轉運使、判度支、上柱國、魏國公、食邑四千五百戶崔胤責授太子賓客，守刑部尚書、兼京兆尹、六軍諸衛副使鄭元規責授循州司戶。

translations.literal: On bingshen, an edict demoted Cui Yin, Grand Mentor, Palace Minister of the Supreme Ultimate, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, commissioner of the Extended Treasury, controller of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards, transport commissioner for salt and iron, controller of the budget, Pillar of the State, Duke of Wei with 4,500 households, to Crown Prince Mentor; Zheng Yuangui, Minister of Justice and acting Jingzhao governor and deputy controller of the Six Armies, to Xunzhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Cui Yin—Grand Mentor, Palace Minister, Hongwen Grand Academician, Extended Treasury commissioner, controller of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards, salt-and-iron transport commissioner, budget controller, Pillar of the State, Duke of Wei—was demoted to Crown Prince Mentor. Zheng Yuangui, Minister of Justice and acting Jingzhao governor, was demoted to registrar of Xun.

sentences.zh: 是日，汴州扈駕指揮使朱友諒殺胤及元規、皇城使王建勳、飛龍使陳班、閣門使王建襲、客省使王建乂、前左僕射上柱國河間郡公張浚。

translations.literal: That day, Zhu Youliang, Bianzhou escort commander, killed Yin and Yuangui, Imperial City commissioner Wang Jianxun, Flying Dragon commissioner Chen Ban, Gate commissioner Wang Jianxi, Guest Reception commissioner Wang Jianyi, and former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun, Duke of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Zhu Youliang, the Bianzhou escort commander, murdered Yin, Yuangui, the Imperial City commissioner Wang Jianxun, Flying Dragon commissioner Chen Ban, Gate commissioner Wang Jianxi, Guest Reception commissioner Wang Jianyi, and the former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun, Duke of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 全忠將逼車駕幸洛陽，懼胤、浚立異也。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was about to force the imperial carriage to Luoyang and feared Yin and Jun would set up a rival court.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong meant to drag the court to Luoyang and feared Yin and Jun might rally opposition.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年春正月丁酉朔，以翰林學士、左拾遺柳璨為右諫議大夫、同平章事，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: On the first day of spring in Tianyou year 1, dingyou, Hanlin academician and Left Reminder Liu Can was made Right Remonstrator, co–Grand Councillor, and granted the purple-gold fish bag.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, New Year’s Day of Tianyou 1, Hanlin academician Liu Can was promoted to Right Remonstrator and co–Grand Councillor and given the purple-gold fish bag.

sentences.zh: 己亥，制以兵部尚書崔遠為中書侍郎、同平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: On jihai, an edict made Minister of War Cui Yuan Central Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, and Academician of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Cui Yuan, Minister of War, was named Central Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, and Jixian Academician.

sentences.zh: 己酉，全忠率師屯河中，遣牙將寇彥卿奉表請車駕遷都洛陽。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Quanzhong led troops to encamp at Hezhong and sent staff officer Kou Yanqing to present a memorial requesting the court move to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Quanzhong marched to Hezhong and sent Kou Yanqing with a memorial begging the emperor to relocate to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 全忠令長安居人按籍遷居，徹屋木，自渭浮河而下，連甍號哭，月餘不息。

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered Chang’an residents moved by household register, dismantled houses for timber, floated them down the Wei and Yellow rivers; linked roofs wailed for more than a month without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong forced Chang’an’s people to relocate by registry, stripped their houses for lumber, and rafted the timbers down the Wei and Yellow rivers. For more than a month the river was a chain of weeping roofs.

sentences.zh: 秦人大罵于路曰：「國賊崔胤，召朱溫傾覆社稷，俾我及此，天乎！

translations.literal: Qin people cursed on the road: “State traitor Cui Yin summoned Zhu Wen to overturn the altars of state, bringing us to this—Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Along the roads the people of Qin cursed: “The traitor Cui Yin called in Zhu Wen to wreck the realm and ruin us—O Heaven!”

sentences.zh: 天乎！

translations.literal: Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: O Heaven!”

sentences.zh: 」丁巳，車駕發京師。

translations.literal: ” On dingsi, the imperial carriage departed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the imperial procession left Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，次陝州，全忠迎謁于路。

translations.literal: On guihai, it halted at Shaan Prefecture; Quanzhong met and bowed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai it reached Shaanzhou, where Quanzhong met the emperor on the road and performed obeisance.

sentences.zh: 二月丙寅朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month, bingyin.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the first day of the second month.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，全忠辭赴洛陽，親督工作。

translations.literal: On yihai, Quanzhong took leave for Luoyang to supervise construction in person.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Quanzhong went to Luoyang to oversee the building work himself.

sentences.zh: 四月丙寅朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, bingyin.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the first day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝遣晉國夫人可證傳詔諭全忠，言中宮誕蓐未安，取十月入洛陽宮。

translations.literal: On guisi, the emperor sent the Jin State Lady Kezheng to transmit an edict to Quanzhong, saying the inner palace’s lying-in was unsettled and entry to the Luoyang palace should wait until the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the emperor sent Lady Kezheng of Jin with an edict: the empress was not yet safely delivered; the court should enter Luoyang palace only in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 全忠意上遲留俟變，怒甚，謂牙將寇彥卿曰：「亟往陝州，到日便促官家發來！

translations.literal: Quanzhong thought the sovereign delayed awaiting trouble and was greatly angry, telling staff officer Kou Yanqing: “Go quickly to Shaanzhou; the day you arrive, hurry the Son of Heaven onward!
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong decided the emperor was stalling for a chance to rebel. Furious, he told Kou Yanqing: “Get to Shaanzhou at once. The day you arrive, drive the Son of Heaven forward!”

translations.literal: closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: (end of command)

sentences.zh: 閏四月乙未朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the intercalary fourth month, yiwei.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the first day of the intercalary fourth month.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，車駕發陝州。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the imperial carriage departed Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the court left Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，次谷水行宮。

translations.literal: On renyin, it halted at the Gushui traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin it stopped at the Gushui traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤所募六軍兵士，胤死後亡散並盡，從上東遷者，唯諸王、小黃門十數，打球代奉內園小兒共二百餘人。

translations.literal: At that time the Six Armies soldiers Yin had recruited, after Yin’s death, scattered and were gone; those who followed east were only several dozen princes and junior yellow-gate eunuchs, ball-players and inner-garden boys substituting for attendants—over two hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies troops Cui Yin had raised had melted away after his death. What still followed the emperor east were a few dozen princes, junior eunuchs, ball-players, and inner-garden boys standing in for attendants—barely two hundred souls.

sentences.zh: 全忠在陝，仍慮此輩為變，欲盡去之，以汴卒為侍衛。

translations.literal: Quanzhong at Shaan still feared they might stir trouble and wished to remove them all, using Bian troops as guards.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong, still at Shaan, feared this remnant might turn on him and meant to purge them and replace them with Bian guards.

sentences.zh: 至谷水頓，全忠令醫官許昭遠告內園等謀變，因會設幄，酒食次並坑之，乃以謀逆聞。

translations.literal: At the Gushui halt, Quanzhong had medical officer Xu Zhaoyuan report that the inner garden and others plotted mutiny; he then convened them under tents and, after food and drink, buried them in a pit, then announced a plot of treason.
translations.idiomatic: At Gushui he had the physician Xu Zhaoyuan accuse the inner-garden staff of conspiracy, summoned them to a feast in the tents, and buried them alive in a pit afterward, then announced a treason plot.

sentences.zh: 由是帝左右前後侍衛職掌，皆汴人也。

translations.literal: Henceforth all attendants before and behind and on duty were Bian men.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every attendant around the emperor was a Bian soldier.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，車駕由徽安門入，朱全忠、張全義、宰相裴樞獨孤損前導。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the imperial carriage entered by the Hui’an Gate; Zhu Quanzhong, Zhang Quanyi, and Grand Councillors Pei Shu and Dugu Sun went before as guides.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the procession entered through Hui’an Gate with Quanzhong, Zhang Quanyi, and councillors Pei Shu and Dugu Sun leading the way.

sentences.zh: 是日大風雨土，跬步不辨物色，日暝稍止。

translations.literal: That day great wind and rain of dust; a pace’s distance could not distinguish objects; at dusk it slightly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: That day a sandstorm blotted out the world at arm’s length; only at dusk did it ease.

sentences.zh: 上謁太廟，禮畢還宮，御正殿宣勞從官衛士，受駕。

translations.literal: The sovereign visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple; when rites were done he returned to the palace, took the main hall to announce rewards to attendant officials and guards, and received the carriage escort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worshipped at the ancestral temple, returned to the palace, took the main hall to reward the escort, and accepted their homage.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，上御光政門，大赦，制曰：

translations.literal: On yisi, the sovereign took the Guangzheng Gate, proclaimed a great amnesty, and an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he appeared at Guangzheng Gate and proclaimed a general amnesty. The edict read:

sentences.zh: 戊申，敕今後除留宣徽兩院、小馬坊、豐德廟、御廚、客省、閣門、飛龍、莊宅九使外，其餘並停。

translations.literal: On wushen, an edict: hereafter except retain the Xuanhui two courts, small horse stable, Fengde shrine, imperial kitchen, guest reception, gate office, flying dragon, and manor nine commissions; the rest are all stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen an edict abolished every inner office except the Xuanhui courts, horse stable, Fengde shrine, imperial kitchen, guest reception, gate office, flying dragon bureau, and manor commission.

sentences.zh: 內園冰井公事委河南尹，仍不差內夫人傳宣。

translations.literal: Inner-garden and ice-well affairs are entrusted to the Henan governor; inner ladies are still not to transmit edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-garden and ice-well duties went to the Henan governor; inner ladies were barred from relaying edicts.

sentences.zh: 殺醫官閻祐之、國子博士歐陽特，言星讖也。

translations.literal: Medical officer Yan Youzhi and National University doctor Ouyang Te were killed, on grounds of star omens.
translations.idiomatic: The physician Yan Youzhi and National University lecturer Ouyang Te were executed for alleged star omens.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴樞兼右僕射、諸道鹽鐵轉運等使、監修國史，戶部尚書、門下侍郎、平章事獨孤損判度支，中書侍郎、平章事柳璨判戶部事。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Pei Shu also took Right Vice Director, salt-and-iron transport commissioner, and supervisor of national history; Households Minister and Vice Director Dugu Sun controlled the budget; Central Vice Director Liu Can controlled household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu added Right Vice Director, salt-and-iron transport, and historiography; Dugu Sun took the budget; Liu Can took household affairs.

sentences.zh: 五月乙丑朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, yichou.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, the first day of the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，制河陽節度使張漢瑜同平章事。

translations.literal: On bingyin, an edict made Heyang military governor Zhang Hanyu co–Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Zhang Hanyu, military governor of Heyang, was made co–Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 宴百僚於崇勳殿，上贊述全忠之功業，因言御樓前一日所司亡失赦書，賴元帥府收得副本施行，幾失事矣，中書不得無過。

translations.literal: A banquet for the hundred officials was held in Chongxun Hall; the sovereign praised Quanzhong’s achievements and said that the day before ascending the tower the office had lost the amnesty text and only the marshal’s headquarters recovered a copy to implement—nearly a disaster; the Secretariat could not be without fault.
translations.idiomatic: At Chongxun Hall the emperor lauded Quanzhong’s deeds, then noted that the amnesty scroll had vanished the day before the tower ceremony and only a copy from headquarters saved the day—almost a catastrophe—and the Secretariat was not blameless.

sentences.zh: 裴樞等起待罪。

translations.literal: Pei Shu and others rose to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu and the others rose to await punishment.

sentences.zh: 中飲，帝更衣，召全忠曲宴閣中，全忠懇辭。

translations.literal: Mid-feast, the emperor changed clothes and summoned Quanzhong to a private banquet in the pavilion; Quanzhong earnestly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-banquet the emperor withdrew to summon Quanzhong to a private pavilion feast; Quanzhong pleaded off.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕以全忠功業崇高，欲齋中款曲，以表庇賴耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “I wished, because Quanzhong’s achievements are lofty, to fast and receive him intimately, to show reliance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “Your service is so great I meant to fast and receive you privately—to show how I lean on you.

sentences.zh: 全忠既不欲來，即令敬翔來，朕與之言。

translations.literal: Since Quanzhong does not wish to come, then let Jing Xiang come; I will speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not come, send Jing Xiang; I will speak with him.”

sentences.zh: 」全忠令敬翔私退，奏曰：「敬翔亦醉而出矣。

translations.literal: ” Quanzhong had Jing Xiang withdraw privately and memorialized: “Jing Xiang also came out drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong had Jing Xiang slip away and reported, “Jing Xiang left drunk as well.”

sentences.zh: 」己巳，全忠辭赴大梁，宴於崇勳殿，是日雨甚。

translations.literal: ” On jisi, Quanzhong took leave for Daliang; a banquet was held in Chongxun Hall; that day rain was heavy.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Quanzhong left for Daliang after another Chongxun banquet in pouring rain.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，翰林學士、左諫議大夫、知制誥沈棲遠守本官，以病陳乞故也。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Hanlin academician, Left Remonstrator, and drafter of edicts Shen Qiyuan kept his original office, because he had submitted illness.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Shen Qiyuan, Hanlin academician and Left Remonstrator, kept his post after pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，敕河南府畿縣先減尉一員，可准京兆府例，復置縣尉一員。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict: Henan metropolitan counties had first reduced one assistant magistrate; they may follow Jingzhao’s precedent and restore one county assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai an edict restored one assistant magistrate per county in the Henan capital districts, matching Jingzhao’s practice.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，中書奏：准今年四月十一日赦文，陝州都督府改為興唐府，其都督府長史宜改為尹，左右司馬為少尹，錄事為司錄，陝縣為次赤，餘為次畿。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Secretariat memorialized: per this year’s fourth-month eleventh-day amnesty, Shaanzhou superior prefecture is changed to Xingtang Prefecture; its superior prefect becomes governor, left and right aides become junior governors, registrar becomes recorder, Shaan county becomes secondary red, the rest secondary metropolitan.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Secretariat proposed renaming Shaan superior prefecture Xingtang, its chief magistrate “governor,” his deputies “junior governors,” and adjusting county ranks per the April amnesty.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The edict was assented to.
translations.idiomatic: Assent was given.

sentences.zh: 六月甲午朔，邠州楊崇本侵掠關內，全忠遣朱友裕屯軍於百仁村。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, jiawu; Yang Chongben of Bin raided within the passes; Quanzhong sent Zhu Youyu to encamp at Bairen Village.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, sixth month’s first day, Yang Chongben raided Guanzhong; Quanzhong sent Zhu Youyu to camp at Bairen Village.

sentences.zh: 丙申，通議大夫、中書舍人、賜紫金魚袋楊注可充翰林學士。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Tongyi Grand Master, Secretariat drafter, bearer of purple-gold fish Yang Zhu may serve as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Yang Zhu was approved as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 庚子，三佛齊國入朝使薄訶粟可甯遠將軍。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Srivijaya envoy Bohe Su may be General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Srivijayan envoy Bohe Su was made General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 丁未，制金紫光祿大夫、太子少傅盧紹可太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: On dingwei, an edict: Jinzi-guanglu Grand Master, Junior Tutor of the Heir Lu Shao may retire as Junior Mentor of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Lu Shao, Junior Tutor of the Heir, was permitted to retire as Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 銀青光祿大夫、太子少師、天水男、食邑三百戶趙崇可檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: Yinguanglu Grand Master, Junior Preceptor of the Heir, Baron of Tianshui with 300 households Zhao Chong may be acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chong, Junior Preceptor of the Heir, was made acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以京兆少尹鄭韜光為太常少卿，前侍御史韋說為右司員外郎，前進士姚顗為校書郎，前進士趙頎、劉明濟、竇專並可秘書省校書郎正字，從柳璨奏也。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Jingzhao junior governor Zheng Taoguang was made Vice Minister of Rites; former attendant censor Wei Yue Right Division aide; former presented scholars Yao Hao and Zhao Qi, Liu Mingji, and Dou Zhuan may be regular secretaries of the Secretariat—all on Liu Can’s memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Zheng Taoguang became Vice Minister of Rites; Wei Yue, Yao Hao, Zhao Qi, Liu Mingji, and Dou Zhuan received Secretariat posts at Liu Can’s request.

sentences.zh: 荊南襄州忠義軍節度、開府儀同三司、檢校太師、中書令、江陵尹、襄州刺史、上柱國、楚王、食邑六千戶趙匡凝宜備禮冊命。

translations.literal: Jingnan Xiangzhou Loyalty Army military governor, Kaifu, acting Grand Preceptor, Central Director, Jiangling governor, Xiangzhou prefect, Pillar, King of Chu with 6,000 households Zhao Kuangning should receive full investiture rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangning, King of Chu and military governor at Xiangyang, was ordered invested with full rites.

sentences.zh: 七月癸亥朔，全忠率師討邠、鳳。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, guihai; Quanzhong led troops to campaign against Bin and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, seventh month’s first day, Quanzhong marched against Bin and Feng.

sentences.zh: 甲子，自汴至洛陽，宴于文思球場。

translations.literal: On jiazi, from Bian to Luoyang, banquet at the Wensi ball ground.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he came from Bian to Luoyang and feasted at the Wensi ball court.

sentences.zh: 全忠入，百官或坐於廊下，全忠怒，笞通引官何凝。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong entered, some hundred officials sat in the corridor; Quanzhong was angry and flogged usher He Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong found officials lounging in the corridor and had the usher He Ning beaten.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，制金紫光祿大夫、行御史中丞、上柱國韓儀責授棣州司馬，侍御史歸藹責授登州司戶，坐百官傲全忠也。

translations.literal: On bingyin, an edict demoted acting Censor-in-Chief Han Yi to Bianzhou aide and attendant censor Gui Ai to Dengzhou registrar, for the hundred officials’ arrogance toward Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Han Yi and Gui Ai were demoted for slighting Quanzhong at court.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，制以中大夫、中書舍人、上柱國、賜紫金魚袋杜彥林為太中大夫、守御史中丞。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, an edict made Zhongdaifu, Secretariat drafter, Pillar Du Yanlin Grand Master and acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Du Yanlin was promoted to Grand Master and acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，制以兵部郎中蕭頎為吏部郎中，戶部郎中徐綰為兵部郎中，司勳員外郎張茂樞為禮部郎中，監察御史郤殷象為右補闕。

translations.literal: On dingchou, an edict: Personnel Director Xiao Qi to Personnel Director; Households Director Xu Wan to War Director; Merit Vice Director Zhang Maoshu to Rites Director; investigating censor Xi Yinxiang to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou a slate of bureau promotions moved Xiao Qi, Xu Wan, Zhang Maoshu, and Xi Yinxiang up the ladder.

sentences.zh: 己卯，制武昌軍節度、鄂岳蘄黃等州觀察處置兼三司水陸發運淮南西面行營招討等使、開府儀同三司、檢校太師、中書令、西平王、食邑三千戶杜洪加食邑一千戶，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: On jimao, an edict: Wuchang military governor Du Hong, Kaifu, acting Grand Preceptor, Central Director, Western Peace King with 3,000 households, added 1,000 households and 200 actual fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Du Hong, King of Western Peace at Wuchang, received an added thousand households and two hundred fiefs.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，中書奏：「西京舊有淩煙閣，圖畫功臣，今遷都洛陽，合議修建。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the Secretariat memorialized: “The western capital once had the Lingyan Pavilion picturing meritorious ministers; now with the move to Luoyang, it is fitting to discuss rebuilding.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the Secretariat urged rebuilding Luoyang’s Lingyan Pavilion of meritorious portraits, as in the old western capital.

sentences.zh: 副元帥梁王勳庸冠世，請淩煙閣之側別創一閣，以表殊勳。

translations.literal: Deputy Marshal Prince of Liang’s merit crowns the age; request a separate pavilion beside Lingyan to display extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: They asked a second pavilion beside Lingyan for the Prince of Liang, whose merit outshone all others.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 八月壬辰朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, renchen.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the first day of the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 壬寅夜，朱全忠令左龍武統軍朱友恭、右龍武統軍氏叔琮、樞密使蔣玄暉弑昭宗於椒殿。

translations.literal: On renyin night, Zhu Quanzhong ordered Left Dragon Martial commander Zhu Yougong, Right Dragon Martial commander Shi Shuzong, and Privy Councilor Jiang Xuanhui to assassinate Zhaozong in the Jiao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin night Zhu Quanzhong had Zhu Yougong, Shi Shuzong, and Jiang Xuanhui murder Emperor Zhaozong in the Jiao Hall.

sentences.zh: 自帝遷洛，李克用、李茂貞、西川王建、襄陽趙匡凝知全忠篡奪之謀，連盟舉義，以興復為辭。

translations.literal: Since the emperor moved to Luoyang, Li Keyong, Li Maozhen, Wang Jian of Xichuan, and Zhao Kuangning of Xiangyang knew Quanzhong’s usurpation plan and allied in arms under the banner of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang, Li Keyong, Li Maozhen, Wang Jian in the west, and Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang—all seeing Quanzhong’s coup—joined arms claiming restoration.

sentences.zh: 而帝英傑不群，全忠方事西討，慮變起於中，故害帝以絕人望。

translations.literal: But the emperor was outstanding; Quanzhong was campaigning west and feared trouble arising within, so he killed the emperor to cut off hope.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong was too formidable; Quanzhong, campaigning west, feared a palace revolt and killed him to kill hope.

sentences.zh: 帝自離長安、日憂不測，與皇后、內人唯沉飲自寬。

translations.literal: Since leaving Chang’an the emperor daily feared the unforeseen; with the empress and inner persons he only drowned worry in drink.
translations.idiomatic: From Chang’an onward he lived in dread; he, the empress, and the palace women drank away their fear.

sentences.zh: 是月壬寅，全忠令判官李振自河中至洛陽，與友恭等圖之。

translations.literal: That month on renyin, Quanzhong ordered judge Li Zhen from Hezhong to Luoyang to plot with Yougong and others.
translations.idiomatic: That renyin, Quanzhong sent Li Zhen from Hezhong to Luoyang to plot with Yougong and the rest.

sentences.zh: 是夜二鼓，蔣玄暉選龍武衙官史太等百人叩內門，言軍前有急奏面見上。

translations.literal: At the second watch that night, Jiang Xuanhui chose Dragon Martial officer Shi Tai and a hundred men to knock at the inner gate, saying urgent memorials from the army required audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch Jiang Xuanhui led a hundred Dragon Martial officers to the inner gate claiming urgent army memorials.

sentences.zh: 內門開，玄暉每門留卒十人，至椒殿院，貞一夫人啟關，謂玄暉曰：「急奏不應以卒來。

translations.literal: The inner gate opened; Xuanhui left ten soldiers at each gate; reaching the Jiao Hall court, Lady Zhenyi of Hedong opened the gate and said to Xuanhui: “Urgent memorials should not come with soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They entered; Xuanhui left ten men per gate. At the Jiao courtyard Lady Zhenyi opened the door and said, “Soldiers do not belong on urgent memorials.”

sentences.zh: 」史太執貞一殺之，急趨殿下。

translations.literal: ” Shi Tai seized Zhenyi and killed her, rushing to the hall steps.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tai seized her, killed her, and ran for the hall.

sentences.zh: 玄暉曰：「至尊何在？

translations.literal: Xuanhui said: “Where is the Supreme One?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xuanhui shouted, “Where is His Majesty?”

sentences.zh: 」昭儀李漸榮臨軒謂玄暉曰：「院使莫傷官家，寧殺我輩。

translations.literal: ” Zhaoyi Li Jianrong leaned from the balustrade and said to Xuanhui: “Commissioner, do not harm the Son of Heaven; better kill us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi Li Jianrong leaned from the rail: “Commissioner, spare the Son of Heaven—kill us instead.”

sentences.zh: 」帝方醉，聞之遽起。

translations.literal: ” The emperor, drunk, hearing this, rose hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, the emperor heard and lurched up.

sentences.zh: 史太持劍入椒殿，帝單衣旋柱而走，太追而弑之。

translations.literal: Shi Tai with sword entered the Jiao Hall; the emperor in single garment ran pillar to pillar; Tai pursued and assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tai strode in with a sword. The emperor, in his night clothes, dodged pillar to pillar until Tai ran him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 漸榮以身護帝，亦為太所殺。

translations.literal: Jianrong shielded the emperor with her body and was also killed by Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Jianrong threw herself over him and died with him.

sentences.zh: 復執何皇后，將害之。

translations.literal: They again seized Empress He and were about to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Empress He next.

sentences.zh: 後求哀于玄暉，玄暉以全忠止令害帝，釋後而去。

translations.literal: The empress begged Xuanhui; Xuanhui said Quanzhong had ordered only the emperor killed and released the empress and left.
translations.idiomatic: She begged Jiang Xuanhui, who said Quanzhong had ordered only the emperor’s death and let her go.

sentences.zh: 帝殂，年三十八，群臣上諡曰聖穆景文孝皇帝，廟號昭宗。

translations.literal: The emperor died at thirty-eight; the hundred officials posthumous title Sagely Solemn, Cultured in Filial Piety; temple name Zhaozong.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-eight. The court gave him the posthumous title Sagely Solemn, Cultured in Filial Piety and the temple name Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 二年二月二十日，葬於和陵。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the second month of year 2, buried at He Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth of the second month, year 2, he was buried at He Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 哀皇帝諱柷，昭宗第九子，母曰積善太后何氏。

translations.literal: The Lamented Emperor’s taboo is Zhu, ninth son of Zhaozong; mother the Accumulated Goodness Empress Dowager He.
translations.idiomatic: The Lamented Emperor, taboo Zhu, was Zhaozong’s ninth son; his mother was Empress Dowager He of Accumulated Goodness.

sentences.zh: 九月三日，生於大內。

translations.literal: On the third day of the ninth month, born in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the inner palace on the third day of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 二月，封輝王，名祚。

translations.literal: In the second month, enfeoffed Prince of Hui, name Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was enfeoffed Prince of Hui under the name Zuo.

sentences.zh: 二月，拜開府儀同三司，充諸道兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: In the second month, appointed Kaifu and commander-in-chief of all circuits’ armies.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was made Kaifu and commander-in-chief of all armies.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年八月十二日，昭宗遇弑。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the eighth month, Tianyou year 1, Zhaozong met assassination.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth of the eighth month, Tianyou 1, Zhaozong was murdered.

sentences.zh: 翌日，蔣玄暉矯宣遺詔，曰：「我國家化隋為唐，奄有天下，三百年之睹兵戈之屢起，賴勳賢協力，宗社再安。

translations.literal: The next day, Jiang Xuanhui forged and proclaimed the testamentary edict, saying: “Our state transformed Sui into Tang and possessed All Under Heaven; for three hundred years we have seen arms repeatedly rise, relying on meritorious worthies in concert to settle the altars again.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Jiang Xuanhui forged a death edict: “Our house turned Sui into Tang and held the realm three hundred years; again and again war came, yet worthy men restored the throne.

sentences.zh: 豈意宮闈之間，禍亂忽作，昭儀李漸榮、河東夫人裴貞一潛懷逆節，輒肆狂謀，傷疻既深，已及危革。

translations.literal: Who would have thought within the palace quarters sudden calamity—Zhaoyi Li Jianrong and Lady Zhenyi of Hedong secretly harbored treason and wildly plotted, wounding the ruler deep, already at death’s door.
translations.idiomatic: Who imagined palace women would strike—Zhaoyi Li Jianrong and Lady Zhenyi plotting treason, wounding the sovereign past saving?”

sentences.zh: 萬機不可以久曠，四海不可以乏君，神鼎所歸，須有纘繼。

translations.literal: The myriad affairs cannot long be vacant; the four seas cannot lack a lord; where the sacred tripod goes, succession is required.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad affairs cannot stand empty; the realm cannot lack a ruler; the sacred vessel must pass on.

sentences.zh: 輝王祚幼彰岐嶷，長實端良，裒然不群，予所鍾愛，必能克奉丕訓，以安兆人。

translations.literal: Prince of Hui Zuo in youth showed precocious intelligence, grown truly upright and good, outstanding among others, my cherished choice—surely able to uphold the great instruction and settle the million people.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hui Zuo is young but keen, grown upright and rare—the heir I trust to keep the great charter and calm the people.”

sentences.zh: 宜立為皇太子，仍改名柷，監軍國事。

translations.literal: He should be established Crown Prince, still rename Zhu, and oversee state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be Crown Prince, renamed Zhu, to oversee state affairs.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!”

sentences.zh: 孝愛可以承九廟，恭儉可以安萬邦，無樂逸游，志康寰宇。

translations.literal: Filial love can inherit the nine temples; respectful thrift can settle the myriad states; do not delight in roaming pleasure—will to heal the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Let filial piety sustain the ancestral shrines and thrift steady the realm; shun idle pleasure and heal the world.

sentences.zh: 百辟卿士，佑茲沖人，載揚我高祖、太宗之休烈。

translations.literal: Hundred ministers and scholars, aid this young lord, and raise the glorious achievements of our High Ancestor and Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, uphold this boy and carry forward the glory of Gaozu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 」是日遷神柩于西宮，文武百僚班慰於延和門外。

translations.literal: ” That day the spirit coffin was moved to the Western Palace; civil and military hundred officials in ranks offered condolence outside Yanhe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: That day the coffin went to the Western Palace; officials lined up in mourning outside Yanhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 其日午時，又矯宣皇太后令曰：「予遭家不造，急變爰臻，禍生女職之徒，事起宮奚之輩。

translations.literal: At the noon hour that day, again forged and proclaimed the Empress Dowager’s order: “I meet an ill-starred house; sudden change has come; calamity rose from women’s quarters, the affair began among palace servants.
translations.idiomatic: At noon they forged the Empress Dowager’s order: “Misfortune has struck the house; calamity rose from the women’s quarters and palace servants.”

sentences.zh: 皇帝自罹鋒刃，已至彌留，不及顧遺，號慟徒切。

translations.literal: The emperor himself met the blade, already at the final hour, unable to leave testament; wailing is vainly keen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell by the blade, past speech—tears avail nothing.”

sentences.zh: 定大計者安社稷，纂丕圖者擇賢明，議屬未亡人，須示建長策。

translations.literal: He who fixes the great plan secures the altars; he who continues the great design chooses the worthy and bright; deliberation falls to the widow—must show a founding long policy.
translations.idiomatic: Great plans secure the state; great designs need worthy men; the widow must show the way forward.”

sentences.zh: 承高祖之寶運，醫元勳之忠規，伏示股肱，以匡沖昧。

translations.literal: Inheriting the High Ancestor’s precious mandate, trusting the loyal rules of founding ministers, I reveal this to the limbs and trunk to correct the young and dim.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting the founders’ loyal counsel, I turn to you ministers to guide this child.”

sentences.zh: 皇太子柷宜於柩前即皇帝位，其哀制並依祖宗故事，中書門下准前處分。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhu should at once before the coffin take the imperial throne; mourning rites follow ancestral precedent; Secretariat and Chancellery act as before.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhu shall ascend before the coffin; mourning follows precedent; the Secretariat and Chancellery shall proceed as before.”

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!”

sentences.zh: 送往事居，古人令范，行今報舊，前哲格言。

translations.literal: Sending off the dead and serving the living—ancients’ model; acting now to repay the old—sages’ maxim.
translations.idiomatic: Honor the dead and serve the living—that is the ancients’ model; repay old debts with present duty—that is the sages’ maxim.”

sentences.zh: 抆淚敷宣，言不能喻。

translations.literal: Wiping tears I proclaim; words cannot express.
translations.idiomatic: I wipe my tears and cannot say enough.”

sentences.zh: 」帝時年十三，乞且監國，柩前即位，宜差太常卿王溥充禮儀使，又令太子家令李能告哀於十六宅。

translations.literal: ” The emperor was then thirteen, begged to oversee the state for the moment, and at the coffin took the throne; Director of Rites Wang Pu should be ritual commissioner; Crown Prince’s household intendant Li Neng should announce mourning at the Sixteen Mansions.
translations.idiomatic: The boy was thirteen; he begged to govern provisionally and took the throne at the coffin. Wang Pu was named ritual commissioner; Li Neng was sent to announce mourning at the princes’ mansions.

sentences.zh: 丙午，大行皇帝大殮，皇太子柩前即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the late emperor’s great encoffinment; the crown prince at the coffin took the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the late emperor was encoffined and the crown prince formally ascended at the bier.

sentences.zh: 己酉，矯制曰：「昭儀李漸榮、河東夫人裴貞一，今月十一日夜持刃謀逆，懼罪投井而死，宜追削為悖逆庶人。

translations.literal: On jiyou, forged edict: “Zhaoyi Li Jianrong and Lady Zhenyi of Hedong on the eleventh night of this month held blades in treason, fearing guilt and threw themselves into a well and died; they should be posthumously stripped as rebellious common women.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou a forged edict branded Li Jianrong and Lady Zhenyi traitors who stabbed the emperor on the eleventh, then drowned themselves in a well.

sentences.zh: 」蔣玄暉夜既弑逆，詰旦宣言於外曰：「夜來帝與昭儀博戲，帝醉，為昭儀所害。

translations.literal: ” After Jiang Xuanhui’s night assassination, at dawn he proclaimed outside: “Last night the emperor and the zhaoyi gambled; the emperor drunk, the zhaoyi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Jiang Xuanhui told the city the emperor had been drunk gambling with the zhaoyi and she had killed him.

sentences.zh: 」歸罪宮人，以掩弑逆之跡。

translations.literal: ” Blame was placed on palace women to cover the regicide.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women took the blame to hide regicide.

sentences.zh: 然龍武軍官健備傳二夫人之言于市人。

translations.literal: Yet Dragon Martial officers and soldiers widely passed the two ladies’ words among townspeople.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Dragon Martial troops spread the two ladies’ dying words through the markets.

sentences.zh: 尋用史太為棣州刺史，以酬弑逆之功。

translations.literal: Soon Shi Tai was used as Bian prefectural governor to reward regicide merit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Tai was made prefect of Bin to reward the killers.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，群臣上表請聽政。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the hundred officials memorialized requesting audience on government.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the officials asked him to take up government.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，中書奏：「皇帝九月三日降誕，請以其日為乾和節。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Secretariat memorialized: “The emperor’s birth on the third day of the ninth month—request that day as the Qianhe festival.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the Secretariat proposed the emperor’s birthday, ninth month third day, as the Qianhe festival.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，百僚赴西宮，殮訖，釋服。

translations.literal: On yichou, the hundred officials went to the Western Palace; encoffinment finished, mourning garments released.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou officials went to the Western Palace; when encoffinment ended they left mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 皇帝見群臣於崇勳殿西廊下。

translations.literal: The emperor received the hundred officials in the west corridor of Chongxun Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received them in Chongxun Hall’s west corridor.

sentences.zh: 中書帖：「今月二十四日釋服後，三日一度進名起居。

translations.literal: Secretariat note: “After releasing mourning garments on the twenty-fourth of this month, present names for routine audience every three days.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat ordered routine audiences every three days after mourning dress ended on the twenty-fourth.

sentences.zh: 」丙辰，敕：「朕奉太后慈旨，以兩司綱運未來，百官事力多闕，旦夕霜冷，深軫所懷。

translations.literal: ” On bingchen, edict: “I follow the Empress Dowager’s compassionate order: because the two departments’ transport funds have not come and officials’ salaries are much lacking, morning and evening frost is cold—deeply felt in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen an edict said the Empress Dowager, seeing salaries unpaid and frost biting, ordered relief.

sentences.zh: 令於內庫方圓銀二千一百七十二兩，充見任文武常參官救接，委御史台依品秩分俵。

translations.literal: Order from the inner treasury square round silver 2,172 taels to relieve present civil and military regular attendees; entrust the Censorate to distribute by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand one hundred seventy-two taels of silver from the inner treasury were to be split among attending officials by rank through the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 」是日，皇帝聽政。

translations.literal: ” That day, the emperor heard government.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor held court.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，敕：乾和節方在哀疚，其內道場宜停。

translations.literal: On dingsi, edict: Qianhe festival is still within mourning; inner Buddhist rites should stop.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi inner Buddhist rites for Qianhe were suspended for mourning.

sentences.zh: 戊午，遣刑部尚書張禕告哀於河中，全忠號哭盡哀。

translations.literal: On wuwu, sent Minister of Justice Zhang Yi to announce mourning at Hezhong; Quanzhong wailed with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Zhang Yi announced the death at Hezhong; Quanzhong wailed as if heartbroken.

sentences.zh: 庚申，敕：「乾和節文武百僚諸軍諸使諸道進奏官准故事於寺觀設齋，不得宰殺，只許酒果脯醢。

translations.literal: On gengshen, edict: “On Qianhe festival civil and military hundred officials, armies, commissioners, and circuit memorialists, per precedent set vegetarian feasts at temples—no slaughter, only wine, fruit, dried meat, and pickles allowed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Qianhe feasts at temples were ordered vegetarian—wine and preserves only, no slaughter.

sentences.zh: 」辛酉，敕：「三月二十三日嘉會節。

translations.literal: ” On xinyou, edict: “On the twenty-third day of the third month, the Jiahui festival.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Jiahui festival on the twenty-third of the third month was noted.

sentences.zh: 伏以大行皇帝仙駕上升，靈山將卜，神既游於天際，節宜輟於人間。

translations.literal: Considering the late emperor’s immortal carriage ascended, the spirit hill will be divined, the spirit already roams heaven’s edge—the festival should cease among men.
translations.idiomatic: With the late emperor’s spirit ascending and the tomb not yet chosen, human festivals should pause.

sentences.zh: 准故事，嘉會節宜停。

translations.literal: Per precedent, the Jiahui festival should stop.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent Jiahui was canceled.

translations.literal: closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: (end of edict)

sentences.zh: 九月壬戌朔，百官素服赴西內臨，進名奉慰。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, renxu; hundred officials in plain dress went to the western inner palace for audience, presenting names in condolence.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, ninth month’s first day, officials in white attended the western inner palace.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，大行皇帝大祥，百官素服赴西內臨。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the late emperor’s great felicity; hundred officials in plain dress attended the western inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, at the great felicity rite, they attended again in white.

sentences.zh: 己巳，敕右僕射、門下侍郎、禮部尚書、平章事裴樞宜充大行皇帝山陵禮儀使，門下侍郎、平章事獨孤損宜充大行皇帝山陵使，兵部侍郎李燕充鹵簿使，權知河南尹韋震充橋道使，宗正卿李克勤充按行使。

translations.literal: On jisi, edict: Right Vice Director, Vice Director, Minister of Rites, Grand Councillor Pei Shu should be late emperor tomb ritual commissioner; Vice Director Dugu Sun tomb commissioner; Vice Minister of War Li Yan chariot commissioner; acting Henan governor Wei Zhen bridge-and-road commissioner; Court of Imperial Sacrifices director Li Keqin procession commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, Li Yan, Wei Zhen, and Li Keqin were named to the tomb commission.

sentences.zh: 庚午，皇帝釋服從吉。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the emperor released mourning and followed auspicious day.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the emperor left mourning for an auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 中書門下奏：「伏以陛下光繼寶圖，纂承丕緒，教道克申於先訓，保任實自于慈顏。

translations.literal: Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: “Considering Your Majesty brightly continues the precious design, inherits the great succession, teaching and the Way extend the former instruction, protection and trust truly come from the compassionate countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat praised his succession and noted he had not yet honored the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 今則正位宸居，未崇徽號。

translations.literal: Now rightly occupying the imperial dwelling, the lofty title is not yet honored.
translations.idiomatic: He sat the throne but her title was still pending.

sentences.zh: 伏以大行皇帝皇后母臨四海，德冠六宮，推尊宜正於鴻名，敬上式光於睿孝，望上尊號曰皇太后。

translations.literal: Considering the late emperor’s empress mother oversaw the four seas, virtue crowned the six palaces—exalted respect should be corrected in a great name; reverent elevation should shine with sagely filial piety; we look up to honor as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: They urged the title Empress Dowager for the late emperor’s empress, virtue of the six palaces.

sentences.zh: 」奉敕宜依。

translations.literal: ” Edict: as ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 又敕輝王府官屬宜停。

translations.literal: Also edict: Prince of Hui mansion staff should stop.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hui’s household staff was dissolved.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，山陵橋道使改差權河南尹張廷範，其頓遞陵下應接等使，並令廷範兼之。

translations.literal: On xinsi, tomb bridge-and-road commissioner changed to acting Henan governor Zhang Tingfan; relay and tomb-base reception commissioners were also given to Tingfan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Zhang Tingfan replaced Wei Zhen on bridge, road, and tomb reception duties.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，中書奏：太常寺止鼓兩字「敔」上字犯禦名，請改曰「肇」。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Secretariat memorialized: Director of Rites stopped drum’s two graphs “敔” upper graph violates imperial taboo; request change to “肇.”
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the Rites Director asked to rename a drum character that violated the emperor’s taboo.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The edict was assented to.
translations.idiomatic: Assent was given.

sentences.zh: 十月辛卯朔，日有蝕之，在心初度。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, xinmao; eclipse of the sun, in the heart’s first degree.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, tenth month’s first day, the sun eclipsed in the Heart asterism.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，全忠自河中來朝，赴西內臨祭訖，對於崇勳殿。

translations.literal: On renchen, Quanzhong came from Hezhong to court, after western inner condolence rites finished faced audience in Chongxun Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Quanzhong came from Hezhong, mourned at the western palace, then met the emperor at Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 甲午，敕檢校太保、左龍武統軍朱友恭可復本姓名李彥威，貶崖州司戶同正。

translations.literal: On jiawu, edict: acting Grand Guardian, Left Dragon Martial commander Zhu Yougong may restore original name Li Yanwei, demoted to Yazhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Zhu Yougong, restored as Li Yanwei, was demoted to registrar of Ya.

sentences.zh: 檢校司徒、右龍武統軍氏叔琮可貶貝州司戶同正。

translations.literal: Acting Minister of Works, Right Dragon Martial commander Shi Shuzong may be demoted to Beizhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shuzong was demoted to registrar of Bei.

sentences.zh: 又敕：「彥威等主典禁兵，妄為扇動，既有彰於物論，兼亦系於軍情。

translations.literal: Also edict: “Yanwei and others commanded forbidden troops and rashly stirred them; already clear in public opinion and also tied to army sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said Yanwei and the rest had stirred the guards and must answer to army and public opinion.

sentences.zh: 謫掾遐方，安能塞責？

translations.literal: Demoted to distant prefectures—how can they fulfill responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: Exile was not enough.

sentences.zh: 宜配充本州長流百姓，仍令所在賜自盡。

translations.literal: They should be assigned as long exiles in their home prefectures and still ordered to commit suicide where they are.
translations.idiomatic: They were to be sent home as common exiles and ordered to kill themselves on arrival.

sentences.zh: 」河南尹張廷範收彥威等殺之。

translations.literal: ” Henan governor Zhang Tingfan seized Yanwei and others and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingfan seized them and killed them.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，大呼曰：「賣我性命，欲塞天下之謗，其如神理何！

translations.literal: Facing execution, he shouted: “Selling my life to stop the world’s slander—what of divine principle!
translations.idiomatic: At the block Yanwei shouted, “You buy my life to silence slander—what of heaven’s justice?”

sentences.zh: 操心若此，欲望子孫長世，可乎？

translations.literal: A heart like this—hoping descendants long endure—can it?
translations.idiomatic: With a heart like yours, do you think your line will last?”

sentences.zh: 」呼廷範，謂曰：「公行當及此，勉自圖之。

translations.literal: ” He called Tingfan and said: “Sir will soon reach this; strive to plan for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: He called to Tingfan, “You’ll be here soon—plan ahead.”

sentences.zh: 」是日，全忠歸大樑。

translations.literal: ” That day, Quanzhong returned to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: That day Quanzhong returned to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 丙申，制天平軍節度使、檢校太師、中書令，兼鄆州刺史、上柱國、東平王、食邑七千戶張全義本官兼河南尹、許州刺史、忠武軍節度觀察等使、判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: On bingshen, edict: Pingyi military governor, acting Grand Preceptor, Central Director, also Yanzhou prefect, Pillar, King of Dongping with 7,000 households Zhang Quanyi original office also Henan governor, Xuzhou prefect, Zhongwu military governor and observer, controller of Six Armies and Guards.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Zhang Quanyi, King of Dongping, added Henan governor, Xuzhou prefect, Zhongwu command, and control of the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 皇帝即位行事官、左丞楊涉進封開國伯，加食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor’s accession acting officer, Left Assistant Director Yang She advanced to Baron with 400 added households.
translations.idiomatic: Yang She, chief accession officer, was made a baron with four hundred added households.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎趙光逢進開國公，加食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Zhao Guangfeng advanced to Duke with 300 added households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guangfeng was made a duke with three hundred added households.

sentences.zh: 右散騎常侍竇回、給事中孫續、戶部郎中知制誥封舜卿等加勳階。

translations.literal: Right Regular Attendant Dou Hui, Giver of Affairs Sun Xu, Households Director and edict drafter Feng Shunqing and others added merit ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Hui, Sun Xu, Feng Shunqing, and others received merit promotions.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使、太常卿王溥與一子八品正員官。

translations.literal: Ritual commissioner, Director of Rites Wang Pu and one son eighth-rank regular office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu, ritual commissioner, won an eighth-rank post for a son.

sentences.zh: 書寶冊官吏部尚書陸扆、刑部尚書張禕，扆與一子八品正員官，禕加階。

translations.literal: Seal-and-register officers, Minister of Personnel Lu Yi and Minister of Justice Zhang Yi—Yi and one son eighth-rank regular office; Yi added rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi and Zhang Yi, seal officers, were rewarded; Yi’s son received rank.

sentences.zh: 太子太保盧紹卒。

translations.literal: Junior Guardian of the Heir Lu Shao died.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Guardian Lu Shao died.

sentences.zh: 魏博羅紹威進救接百官絹千匹、綿三千兩。

translations.literal: Weibo Luo Shaowei presented relief silk thousand bolts, cotton three thousand liang for the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei of Weibo sent a thousand bolts of silk and three thousand liang of cotton for officials’ relief.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛酉朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, xinyou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the first day of the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 癸酉午時，日有黃白暈，旁有青赤紉。

translations.literal: On guiyou at the noon hour, the sun had yellow-white halo, with blue-red cords at the side.
translations.idiomatic: At noon on guiyou the sun wore a yellow-white halo with blue-red cords beside it.

sentences.zh: 楊行密攻光州，又急攻鄂州，杜洪遣使求援，全忠率師五萬自潁州渡淮，至霍丘大掠以紓之，行密分兵來拒。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi attacked Guang Prefecture and pressed E Prefecture; Du Hong sent envoys begging aid; Quanzhong led fifty thousand from Yingzhou across the Huai, at Huoqiu greatly plundered to relieve it; Xingmi divided troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi besieged Guang and E; Du Hong begged help; Quanzhong crossed the Huai with fifty thousand, sacked Huoqiu, and met divided resistance.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，敕：「據太常禮院奏，於十二月內擇日冊太后者。

translations.literal: On yiyou, edict: “According to Director of Rites memorial, within the twelfth month choose a day to invest the empress.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou an edict cited the Rites Director: choose a day in the twelfth month to invest the empress.

sentences.zh: 朕近奉慈旨，以山陵未畢，哀感方纏。

translations.literal: I recently follow the compassionate order: because the mausoleum is not finished, grief still binds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said the tomb was unfinished and grief still bound him.

sentences.zh: 凡百有司，且虔充奉，吉凶之禮，難以並施。

translations.literal: All hundred offices for now devoutly fulfill service; auspicious and inauspicious rites are hard to perform together.
translations.idiomatic: Offices must serve the tomb; joy and mourning could not mix.

sentences.zh: 太后冊禮，宜俟山陵畢日，庶得橋山攀慕，彰盡節於群臣；

translations.literal: The empress investiture rites should wait until the mausoleum day is finished, so that at Qiaoshan clinging memory, ministers may show utmost node;
translations.idiomatic: Investiture should wait until the tomb was done—grief at Qiaoshan first, ceremony in the orchid hall after.

sentences.zh: 蘭殿承榮，展盛儀於朕志。

translations.literal: orchid hall receives glory, displaying full rites in my will.
translations.idiomatic: Then the orchid hall could receive its glory.

sentences.zh: 情既獲遂，禮實宜之。

translations.literal: Feeling obtained, rites truly fit.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling satisfied, ritual would be right.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrust the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: So ordered.

sentences.zh: 」己丑，嶺南東道辨州宜改為勳州。

translations.literal: ” On jichou, Lingnan East Circuit Bian Prefecture should be changed to Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Bian in Lingnan East was renamed Xun.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛卯朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, xinmao.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the first day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，權知河南府尹、和王傅張廷範宜復本官。

translations.literal: On guimao, acting Henan prefectural governor, Prince of He tutor Zhang Tingfan should restore original office.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Zhang Tingfan restored his former posts.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫、檢校司徒河東縣開國子、食邑五百戶、充山陵副使、權知河南尹、天平軍節度副使韋震權知鄆州軍州事。

translations.literal: Guanglu Grand Master, acting Minister of Works, Hedong County Viscount with 500 households, tomb deputy commissioner, acting Henan governor, Pingyi deputy military governor Wei Zhen acting military governor of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhen was made acting governor of Yan while keeping tomb and Henan duties.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年二年春正月庚申朔，楊行密陷鄂州，執節度使杜洪，斬於揚州市。

translations.literal: On the first day of spring in Tianyou year 2, gengshen; Yang Xingmi took E Prefecture, seized military governor Du Hong, beheaded at Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, New Year Tianyou 2, Yang Xingmi took Ezhou, captured Du Hong, and beheaded him at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄂、岳、蘄、黃等州入行密。

translations.literal: E, Yue, Qi, Huang and other prefectures entered Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: E, Yue, Qi, Huang, and neighboring prefectures fell to Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 全忠自霍丘還大樑。

translations.literal: Quanzhong from Huoqiu returned to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong returned to Daliang from Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 甲子，太常卿王溥上大行皇帝諡號、廟號，乃敕右僕射、平章事裴樞撰諡冊，中書侍郎柳璨撰哀冊。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Director of Rites Wang Pu presented the late emperor’s posthumous title and temple name; then edict Right Vice Director, Grand Councillor Pei Shu draft the investiture text; Central Vice Director Liu Can draft the lamentation text.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Wang Pu proposed posthumous name and temple name; Pei Shu was to draft the investiture, Liu Can the lament.

sentences.zh: 辛未，敕：「朕祗荷丕圖，仰惟元訓，方迫遺弓之痛，俯臨同軌之期。

translations.literal: On xinwei, edict: “I respectfully bear the great design, look up to the primal instruction, just pressed by the lost bow’s pain, looking down on the same-track period.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei an edict spoke of fresh grief for the late emperor and the coming tomb journey.

sentences.zh: 將展孝思，親扶護衛。

translations.literal: About to display filial thought, personally support the guard.
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor wished to escort the coffin himself.

sentences.zh: 皇太后義深鳴鳳，痛切攀龍，亦欲專奉靈輿，躬及園寢，兼盡追摧之道，用終克敬之儀。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager’s righteousness deep as the crying phoenix, pain keen as clinging dragon, also wishes solely to attend the spirit carriage, personally reach the garden tomb, together exhaust the path of mourning, use to finish the rite of respectful completion.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager, grieving as a phoenix, also wished to follow the bier to the tomb.

sentences.zh: 其大行皇帝山陵發引日，朕隨太后親至陵所，付中書門下，宜體至懷。

translations.literal: On the late emperor’s tomb departure day, I with the Empress Dowager personally reach the tomb place; entrust Secretariat and Chancellery to embody utmost feeling.
translations.idiomatic: They would go to the tomb together on departure day—the Secretariat was told to honor that wish.

sentences.zh: 」群臣三表論諫，乃止。

translations.literal: ” The hundred officials three times memorialized remonstrance; then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Three memorials of protest stopped the plan.

sentences.zh: 二月庚寅朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month, gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the first day of the second month.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，制以前知鄜州軍州事、檢校尚書左僕射劉鄩為右金吾衛大將軍，充右街使。

translations.literal: On renchen, edict: former acting Bin military governor, acting Left Vice Director Liu Ye as Right Golden Guard senior general, commissioner of the right street.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Liu Ye, former acting governor of Bin, became Right Golden Guard general and right-street commissioner.

sentences.zh: 檢校左僕射朱漢賓為右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: Acting Left Vice Director Zhu Hanbin as Right Feathered Forest commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hanbin became Right Feathered Forest commander.

sentences.zh: 丙申，群臣告諡於西宮。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the hundred officials announced posthumous title at the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the posthumous title was proclaimed at the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 己亥，敕：「今月十一日，大行皇帝啟攢宮。

translations.literal: On jihai, edict: “On the eleventh of this month, the late emperor opens the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai an edict fixed the eleventh for opening the temporary tomb palace.

sentences.zh: 准故事，坊市禁音樂，至二十日掩玄宮畢，如舊。

translations.literal: Per precedent, markets forbid music until the twentieth when the dark palace is closed—then as before.
translations.idiomatic: Markets would stay silent until the twentieth, when the tomb chamber closed.

sentences.zh: 」庚子，啟攢宮，文武百僚夕臨於西宮。

translations.literal: ” On gengzi, the temporary palace opened; civil and military hundred officials evening attendance at Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the temporary palace opened; officials kept evening vigil.

sentences.zh: 丁未，靈駕發引，濮王已下從，皇帝、太后長樂門外祭畢歸大內。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the spirit carriage departed; Prince of Pu and below followed; emperor and empress dowager after rites at Changle Gate returned to the great inner.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the bier set out with the Prince of Pu and others; emperor and dowager rited at Changle Gate and returned within.

sentences.zh: 己酉，葬昭宗皇帝于和陵。

translations.literal: On jiyou, buried Emperor Zhaozong at He Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Zhaozong was buried at He Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，制乙太常卿王溥為工部尚書。

translations.literal: On gengxu, edict changed Director of Rites Wang Pu to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Wang Pu became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 壬子，制以汝州刺史裴迪為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: On renzi, edict made Runan prefect Pei Di Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Pei Di, prefect of Runan, was made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 泰寧軍節度、檢校司空、兗州刺史、御史大夫葛從周檢校司徒、兼右金吾上將軍致仕，從周病風，不任朝謁故也。

translations.literal: Taining military governor, acting Minister of Works, Yanzhou prefect, Censor Grand Master Ge Congzhou acting Minister of Works, also Right Golden Guard senior general retired—Congzhou had wind illness and could not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou, governor of Taining at Yanzhou, was promoted then retired as Right Golden Guard senior general—wind sickness kept him from court.

sentences.zh: 以左金吾上將軍盧彥威為左威衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Left Golden Guard senior general Lu Yanwei was made Left Weiwu senior general.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanwei moved from Left Golden Guard to Left Weiwu senior general.

sentences.zh: 是月社日，樞密使蔣玄暉宴德王裕已下九王于九曲池，既醉，皆絞殺之，竟不知其瘞所。

translations.literal: That month on the communal-offering day, Privy Councilor Jiang Xuanhui feasted the nine princes including Prince of De Wang Yu at Jiuchiqu Pool; when drunk, all were strangled; in the end their burial place was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: That month on the communal day Jiang Xuanhui feasted nine princes including Prince of De at Jiuchiqu Pool, got them drunk, and strangled them; no one knew where they were buried.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，左僕射裴贄等議遷廟，合遷順宗一室，從之。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Left Vice Director Pei Zan and others deliberated temple move, agreeing to move Shunzong one chamber—approved.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Pei Zan and others agreed to shift Shunzong’s spirit tablet one chamber in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 己未，昭宗皇帝神主祔太廟，禮院奏昭宗廟樂，曰《咸寧之舞》。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Emperor Zhaozong’s spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Temple; Rites Commission memorialized Zhaozong temple music as “Dance of Secure Tranquility.”
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Zhaozong’s tablet entered the Imperial Temple with the hymn “Dance of Secure Tranquility.”

sentences.zh: 三月庚申朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, gengshen.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the first day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，制以前平盧軍節度使、檢校太傅、同平章事、兼青州刺史、上柱國、琅邪郡公、食邑二千五百戶王師範為孟州刺史、河陽三城懷孟節度觀察等使，從全忠奏也。

translations.literal: On renxu, edict: former Pinglu military governor, acting Grand Tutor, co–Grand Councillor, also Qingzhou prefect, Pillar, Duke of Langye with 2,500 households Wang Shifan as Mengzhou prefect, Heyang Three Cities Huai-Meng military governor and observer—on Quanzhong’s memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Wang Shifan was shifted from Qingzhou to Mengzhou and Heyang command at Quanzhong’s request.

sentences.zh: 甲子，制以特進、尚書右僕射、門下侍郎、同平章事、太清宮使、弘文館大學士、延資庫使、諸道鹽鐵轉運使、判度支、上柱國、河東郡開國公、食邑二千戶裴樞可守尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On jiazi, edict: Special Advance, Right Vice Director, Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, Supreme Ultimate Palace Minister, Hongwen Grand Academician, Extended Treasury commissioner, salt-and-iron transport commissioner, budget controller, Pillar, Duke of Hedong with 2,000 households Pei Shu may be acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Pei Shu was made acting Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫、門下侍郎、戶部尚書、同平章事、監修國史、河南縣開國子、食邑五百戶獨孤損可檢校尚書左僕射、同平章事，兼安南都護，充靜海軍節度、安南管內觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Guanglu Grand Master, Vice Director, Households Minister, co–Grand Councillor, national history supervisor, Viscount of Henan with 500 households Dugu Sun may be acting Left Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, also Protector-General of Annan, Jinghai military governor and Annan observer.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Sun was sent acting Left Vice Director and military governor of Jinghai and Annan.

sentences.zh: 以光祿大夫、中書侍郎、同平章事、集賢殿大學士、上柱國、博陵郡開國公、食邑一千五百戶崔遠可守尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Guanglu Grand Master, Central Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, Jixian Grand Academician, Pillar, Duke of Boling with 1,500 households Cui Yuan may be acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan became acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 以正議大夫、中書侍郎、同平章事，判戶部事、上柱國、河東縣男、食邑三百戶柳璨為門下侍郎、兼戶部尚書、同平章事、太清宮使、弘文館大學士、延資庫使、諸道鹽鐵轉運等使。

translations.literal: Correct Opinion Grand Master, Central Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, controller of household affairs, Pillar, Baron of Hedong with 300 households Liu Can as Vice Director, also Households Minister, co–Grand Councillor, Supreme Ultimate Palace Minister, Hongwen Grand Academician, Extended Treasury commissioner, salt-and-iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can took the full chancellorship bundle: Vice Director, Households Minister, Supreme Ultimate Palace, Hongwen, Extended Treasury, and salt-and-iron.

sentences.zh: 以正議大夫、尚書吏部侍郎、上柱國、賜紫金魚袋張文蔚為中書侍郎、同平章事、監修國史、判度支。

translations.literal: Correct Opinion Grand Master, Personnel Vice Minister, Pillar, bearer of purple-gold fish Zhang Wenwei as Central Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, national history supervisor, budget controller.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenwei joined the council as Central Vice Director with historiography and budget.

sentences.zh: 以銀青光祿大夫、行尚書左丞、上柱國、弘農縣伯、食邑七百戶楊涉為中書侍郎、同平章事、集賢殿大學士、判戶部事。

translations.literal: Yinguanglu Grand Master, acting Left Assistant Director, Pillar, Baron of Hongnong with 700 households Yang She as Central Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, Jixian Grand Academician, controller of household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yang She became Central Vice Director with Jixian and household affairs.

sentences.zh: 庚午，敕：「朕以宰臣學士，文武百僚，常拘官局，空逐遊從。

translations.literal: On gengwu, edict: “I consider that Grand Councillors and academicians, civil and military hundred officials, are often bound to office bureaus and vainly chase outings.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu an edict said ministers and officials were chained to their desks and deserved a spring break.

sentences.zh: 今膏澤不愆，豐年有望，當茲韶景，宜示優恩。

translations.literal: Now moisture is not lacking and a rich year is hoped; at this fine season, favor should be shown.
translations.idiomatic: Rain had been steady and harvest looked good—time to grant grace.

sentences.zh: 自今月十二日後至十六日，各令取便選勝追遊。

translations.literal: From the twelfth of this month to the sixteenth, each may take leisure and choose scenic places to roam.
translations.idiomatic: From the twelfth through the sixteenth all might roam as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrust the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: So ordered.

sentences.zh: 」壬申，以檢校司徒、和王傅張廷范為太常卿。

translations.literal: ” On renshen, acting Minister of Works, Prince of He tutor Zhang Tingfan was made Director of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Zhang Tingfan, Quanzhong’s man, was made Director of Rites.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，敕：「翰林學士、戶部侍郎楊注是宰臣楊涉親弟，兄既秉于樞衡，弟故難居宥密，可守本官，罷內職。

translations.literal: On dinghai, edict: “Hanlin academician, Households Vice Minister Yang Zhu is Chancellor Yang She’s younger brother; elder holding the pivot, younger therefore hard to dwell in the secretariat—may keep original office, cease inner duty.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Yang Zhu left the Hanlin because his brother Yang She was chancellor.

translations.literal: closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: (end of edict)

sentences.zh: 四月己丑朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, jichou.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the first day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，敕河南府緱氏縣令宜兼充和陵台令，仍升為赤縣。

translations.literal: On renchen, edict: Henan prefectural Gou county magistrate should also serve as He Mausoleum terrace magistrate and be promoted to red county.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Gou county’s magistrate was also named He Mausoleum terrace magistrate and the county promoted to “red” rank.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，敕曰：「文武二柄，國家大綱，東西兩班，官職同體。

translations.literal: On guisi, edict said: “Civil and military are the two handles, the state’s great cord; eastern and western cohorts, offices share one body.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi a major edict declared civil and military branches equal pillars of the state.

sentences.zh: 咸匡聖運，共列明廷，品秩相對于高卑，祿俸皆均於厚薄。

translations.literal: Together they brace the sagely fortune, together array in the bright court; rank and grade face each other in high and low; salary and stipend are equal in thick and thin.
translations.idiomatic: Both served the throne; ranks might differ but pay should not.

sentences.zh: 不論前代，祗考本朝。

translations.literal: Regardless of former ages, only examine this dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Forget antiquity—look only at Tang practice.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝以中外臣僚，文武參用，或自軍衛而居台省，亦由衣冠而秉節旄，足明于武列文班，不令分清濁優劣。

translations.literal: Taizong used civil and military officials together; some from military guard to terrace and province, some from civil robes to hold banners and axes—clearly in martial arrays and civil rows he did not order clear and turbid, superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had soldiers sit in civil offices and scholars hold commands without ranking “rough” below “refined.”

sentences.zh: 近代浮薄相尚，淩蔑舊章，假偃武以修文，競棄本而逐末。

translations.literal: In recent times frivolity was honored, old statutes despised; falsely resting arms to cultivate letters, competing to abandon the root and chase the branch.
translations.idiomatic: Lately men prized polish, mocked the old ways, pretended to civilize by disarming, and abandoned root for branch.

sentences.zh: 雖藍衫魚簡，當一見而便許升堂；

translations.literal: Though blue robe and fish tally, one meeting permitted ascent to hall;
translations.idiomatic: A blue-gowned clerk with a fish tally might enter the hall at once;

sentences.zh: 縱拖紫腰金，若非類而無令接席。

translations.literal: even dragging purple and girding gold, if not their sort, not permitted to share a mat.
translations.idiomatic: a purple-robed minister of the wrong sort could not share a seat.

sentences.zh: 以是顯揚榮辱，分別重輕，遽失人心，盡隳朝體。

translations.literal: Thus glory and shame were displayed, heavy and light distinguished; suddenly hearts were lost and court body entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: So snobbery split the court and ruined its body.

sentences.zh: 致其今日，實此之由，須議改更，漸期通濟。

translations.literal: Reaching today, truly from this; must discuss reform, gradually expect universal benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Today’s rot came from that—reform was needed for fairness.

sentences.zh: 文武百官，自一品以下，逐月所給料錢並須均勻，數目多少，一般支給。

translations.literal: Civil and military hundred officials from first rank down, monthly stipend money all must be even; amount more or less, one pattern of disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: From first rank down, monthly pay must be equal—same amount for all.

sentences.zh: 兼差使諸道，亦依輪次，既就公平，必期開泰。

translations.literal: Also commissioners to circuits follow rotation in turn; once fairness is reached, surely expect opening and peace.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commissions would rotate fairly too.

sentences.zh: 凡百臣庶，宜體朕懷。

translations.literal: All hundred subjects and commoners should embody my feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Let every subject feel my intent.

sentences.zh: 」和王傅張廷范者，全忠將吏也，以善音律，求為太常卿，全忠薦用之。

translations.literal: Prince of He tutor Zhang Tingfan was Quanzhong’s general and clerk; skilled in music law, he sought to be Director of Rites; Quanzhong recommended and used him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingfan was Quanzhong’s officer, a music man pushed as Director of Rites.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴樞以廷范非樂卿之才，全忠怒，罷樞相位。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Pei Shu considered Tingfan not a music director’s talent; Quanzhong was angry and removed Shu from the council.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu said he was no musician; Quanzhong stripped Shu of office.

sentences.zh: 柳璨希旨，又降此詔斥樞輩，故有白馬之禍。

translations.literal: Liu Can curried favor and again lowered this edict to rebuke Shu’s sort; hence the Baima calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can flattered Quanzhong with this edict attacking Shu’s faction—foreshadowing the Baima slaughter.

sentences.zh: 丙午，前棣州刺史劉仁遇檢校司空，兼兗州刺史、御史大夫，充泰甯軍節度使。

translations.literal: On bingwu, former Bian prefectural governor Liu Renyu acting Minister of Works, also Yanzhou prefect, Censor Grand Master, Taining military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Liu Renyu, former Bin governor, became Taining military governor at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，制左僕射裴樞、新除清海軍節度使獨孤損、河南尹張全義、工部尚書王溥、司空致仕裴贄、刑部尚書張禕，並賜一子八品正員官，以奉山陵之勞也。

translations.literal: On yiwei, edict: Left Vice Director Pei Shu, newly appointed Jinghai military governor Dugu Sun, Henan governor Zhang Quanyi, Minister of Works Wang Pu, retired Minister of Works Pei Zan, Minister of Justice Zhang Yi—all granted one son eighth-rank regular office for mausoleum labor.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei tomb laborers Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, Zhang Quanyi, Wang Pu, Pei Zan, and Zhang Yi each won an eighth-rank post for a son.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「朕以宿麥未登，時陽久亢，慮闕粢盛之備，軫予宵旰之懷。

translations.literal: Edict said: “I consider winter wheat not yet risen, yang long drought, fearing lack of sacrificial grain, deeply felt in my night vigil.
translations.idiomatic: An edict cited drought threatening the harvest and the emperor’s sleepless worry.

sentences.zh: 所宜避正位於宸居，減珍羞于常膳，諒惟眇質，深合罪躬。
