translations.literal: Fitting to avoid the correct seat in the imperial dwelling, reduce delicacies in regular meals; surely my slight substance deeply fits self-blame.
translations.idiomatic: He would leave the main hall and cut his meals in penance.

sentences.zh: 自今月八日已後，不禦正殿，減常膳。

translations.literal: From the eighth of this month afterward, not hold court in the main hall, reduce regular meals.
translations.idiomatic: From the eighth he would not sit the main hall and would eat sparingly.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrust the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: So ordered.

sentences.zh: 」辛丑，侍御史李光庭郗殷象、殿中丞張升崔昭矩、起居舍人盧仁烱盧鼎蘇楷、吏部員外郎崔協、左補闕崔鹹休、右補闕杜承昭羅兗、右拾遺韋彖路德延，並宜賜緋魚袋；

translations.literal: ” On xinchou, attendant censor Li Guangting and Xi Yinxiang, palace director Zhang Sheng and Cui Zhaoju, attendance recorder Lu Renjiong, Lu Ding, Su Kai, Personnel aide Cui Xie, Left Remonstrator Cui Xianxiu, Right Remonstrator Du Chengzhao and Luo Chong, Right Reminder Wei Yan and Lu Deyan—all should be granted crimson fish bags;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou a long list of censors and remonstrators received crimson fish bags for tomb service;

sentences.zh: 兵部郎中韋乾美、比部郎中楊煥，皆賜紫金魚袋：並以奉山陵之勞也。

translations.literal: War Director Wei Qianmei and Comparison Director Yang Huan, both granted purple-gold fish bags: all for mausoleum labor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qianmei and Yang Huan received purple-gold bags for the same reason.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，敕：「朕獲荷丕圖，仰遵慈訓，爰崇徽號，已定禮儀，冀申為子之心，以展奉親之敬。

translations.literal: On renyin, edict: “I have received the great design, look up to follow the compassionate instruction, revere the lofty title, already fixed ritual; hope to extend a son’s heart, to display serving-the-parent respect.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin an edict spoke of honoring the Empress Dowager and the planned investiture.

sentences.zh: 昨所司定今月二十五日行皇太后冊禮。

translations.literal: Yesterday the offices fixed the twenty-fifth of this month for Empress Dowager investiture rites.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture was set for the twenty-fifth.

sentences.zh: 再奉慈旨，以宮殿未停工作，蒸暑不欲勞人，宜改吉辰，固難違命。

translations.literal: Again following the compassionate order: because palace halls have not stopped work and steam heat does not wish to weary people, auspicious day should be changed—solidly hard to disobey the command.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager deferred it—palace work unfinished, summer heat—so the date must move.

sentences.zh: 冊禮俟修大內畢功日，所司以聞。

translations.literal: Investiture rites wait until inner palace work is finished; offices report when ready.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture would follow completion of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 」癸卯，太清宮使柳璨奏修上清宮畢，請改為太清宮，從之。

translations.literal: ” On guimao, Supreme Ultimate Palace Minister Liu Can memorialized Upper Pure Palace repair finished; request change to Supreme Ultimate Palace—approved.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Liu Can reported the Upper Pure Palace repaired and renamed Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 甲辰夜，彗起北河，貫文昌，其長三丈，在西北方。

translations.literal: On jiachen night, comet rose in North River, pierced Wenchang, length three zhang, in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen night a comet three zhang long rose in the northwest through Wenchang.

sentences.zh: 丁未，敕：「設官分職，各有司存，銓衡既任于吏曹，除授甯煩於宰職。

translations.literal: On dingwei, edict: “Setting offices and dividing duties, each has its keeper; evaluation already rests with the Personnel Bureau—appointment should not trouble Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei an edict stripped the council of routine appointments.

sentences.zh: 但所司注擬申到，中書過驗酌量，苟或差舛，難可盡定。

translations.literal: But when responsible offices note and propose reaching the center, the Secretariat passes verification and measure; if there is error, hard to fix entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat would only verify Personnel Bureau lists.

sentences.zh: 近年除授，其徒實繁，占選部之闕員，擇公當之優便，遂致三銓注擬之時，皆曠職務。

translations.literal: In recent years appointments were truly numerous, occupying the Selection Department’s vacant posts, choosing public suitability’s advantages—thus when the three selection bureaus note and propose, all neglect duty.
translations.idiomatic: Lately councilors had hoarded appointments and left the three selection bureaus idle.

sentences.zh: 且以宰相之任，提舉百司，唯務公平無私，方致漸臻有道。

translations.literal: Moreover the Grand Councillor’s task lifts the hundred offices; only if fair and selfless does it gradually reach the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors should govern, not micromanage every post.

sentences.zh: 應天下州府令錄，並委吏部三銓注擬。

translations.literal: All under heaven prefectural magistrates and assistants are entrusted to the Personnel Bureau’s three selections to note and propose.
translations.idiomatic: All county magistrates and aides would be appointed solely by Personnel.

sentences.zh: 自天祐二年四月十一日已後，中書並不除授，或諸薦奏量留，即度可否施行。

translations.literal: From Tianyou year 2 fourth month eleventh day afterward, the Secretariat altogether does not appoint; if memorial recommendations remain by measure, then judge whether to implement.
translations.idiomatic: From the eleventh of the fourth month, Tianyou 2, the Secretariat ceased appointments except on review.

sentences.zh: 庶各司其局，免致紊隳，宰相提綱，永存事體。

translations.literal: So each office keeps its bureau, avoiding disorder; Grand Councillor holds the cord, forever preserving the body of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Each office would keep its lane; chancellors would hold the cord only.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrust the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: So ordered.

sentences.zh: 」辛亥，以彗孛謫見，德音放京畿軍鎮諸司禁囚，常赦不原外，罪無輕重，遞減一等，限三日內疏理聞奏。

translations.literal: On xinhai, because comet and broom star appeared, benevolent edict released capital-region armies, garrisons, and offices’ imprisoned persons; outside those not pardoned by regular amnesty, crimes regardless of light or heavy reduced one grade; within three days memorialize after review.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai a comet prompted amnesty in the capital, most crimes reduced one grade.

sentences.zh: 壬子，敕：「朕以沖幼，克嗣丕基，業業兢兢，勤恭夕惕。

translations.literal: On renzi, edict: “I am young, inheriting the great foundation, diligent and respectful, evening watchful.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the boy emperor blamed himself for the comet.

sentences.zh: 彗星謫見，罪在朕躬。

translations.literal: Comet and reproach star appeared; guilt lies in my person.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s warning was his fault.

sentences.zh: 雖已降赦文，特行恩宥，起今月二十四日後，避正殿，減常膳，以明思過。

translations.literal: Though already lowering amnesty text, specially exercising grace; from the twenty-fourth of this month afterward, avoid the main hall, reduce regular meals, to clarify thinking on faults.
translations.idiomatic: Despite amnesty he would avoid the main hall and cut meals from the twenty-fourth.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrust the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: So ordered.

sentences.zh: 」丙辰，敕：「准向來事例，每貫抽除外，以八百五十文為貫，每陌八十五文。

translations.literal: ” On bingchen, edict: “Per former precedent, each string cash besides deductions uses 850 wen as a string; each mo 85 wen.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen coinage was fixed at eight hundred fifty wen per string and eighty-five per mo.

sentences.zh: 如聞坊市之中，多以八十為陌，更有除折，頓爽舊規。

translations.literal: As heard, in markets many use eighty as mo, with further deductions—suddenly contrary to old rule.
translations.idiomatic: Markets had slipped to eighty per mo.

sentences.zh: 付河南府，市肆交易，並以八十五文為陌，不得更有改移。

translations.literal: Entrust Henan prefecture: market trade all use eighty-five wen as mo, may not further change.
translations.idiomatic: Henan was ordered to enforce eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 」戊午，敕：「東上閣門，西上閣門，比常出入，以東上為先。

translations.literal: ” On wuwu, edict: “Eastern Ascending Gate, Western Ascending Gate—in normal exit, eastern is first.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu gate protocol was corrected.

sentences.zh: 大忌進名，即西上閣門為便。

translations.literal: Great taboo presenting names then Western Ascending Gate is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning audiences used the western gate.

sentences.zh: 比因閹官擅權，乃以陰陽取位，不思南面，但啟西門。

translations.literal: Recently because eunuchs usurped power, they took yin-yang for position, not thinking of facing south but opening the western gate.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs had favored the west for superstition, not south.

sentences.zh: 邇來相承，未議更改，詳其稱謂，似爽舊規。

translations.literal: Lately inherited without discussing change; detailed their titles, seems contrary to old rule.
translations.idiomatic: The custom had lingered wrongly.

sentences.zh: 自今年五月一日後，常朝出入，取東上閣門，或遇奉慰，即開西上閣門，永為定制。

translations.literal: From the first day of the fifth month this year afterward, regular court exit takes Eastern Ascending Gate; if meeting condolence, then open Western Ascending Gate—forever as fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: From May first regular court would use the east gate; condolence, the west.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrust the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: So ordered.

sentences.zh: 」又敕：「朕以上天謫見，避殿責躬，不宜朔會朝正殿。

translations.literal: ” Also edict: “I because heaven’s reproach appeared, avoid hall and blame self, should not hold first-of-month assembly at the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: May Day court at the main hall was canceled for the comet.

sentences.zh: 其五月一日朝會，宜權停。

translations.literal: The fifth month first day court assembly should be temporarily stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The May first levee was suspended.

translations.literal: closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: (end of edict)

sentences.zh: 五月己未朔，以星變不視朝。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, jiwei; because of star change did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, fifth month’s first day, no court for the omen.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「天文變見，合事祈禳，宜於太清宮置黃籙道場，三司支給齋料。

translations.literal: Edict said: “Astronomical change appeared, fitting matter is prayer; should set Yellow Register ritual ground at Supreme Ultimate Palace, three departments supply vegetarian materials.
translations.idiomatic: A Yellow Register Daoist rite was ordered at the Supreme Ultimate Palace.

sentences.zh: 」壬戌，敕：「法駕遷都之日，洛京再建之初，慮懷土有類于新豐，權更名以變於舊制。

translations.literal: ” On renxu, edict: “When the imperial carriage moved the capital, at Luoyang’s rebuilding beginning, fearing attachment to soil like Xinfeng, temporarily changed names to alter old system.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu an edict renamed Luoyang gates after omens, citing fear of homesickness like the Han at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 妖星既出於雍分，高閎難效于秦餘，宜改舊門之名，以壯卜年之永。

translations.literal: The baleful star already came from Yong’s division; high gates hard to imitate Qin’s remainder—old gate names should be changed to strengthen divined years’ endurance.
translations.idiomatic: A comet in Yong’s quarter prompted auspicious new gate names.

sentences.zh: 延喜門改為宣仁門，重明門改為興教門，長樂門改為光政門，光范門曰應天門，乾化門曰乾元門，宣政門曰敷政門，宣政殿曰貞觀殿，日華門曰左延福門，月華門曰右延福門，萬壽門曰萬春門，積慶門曰興善門，含章門曰膺福門，含清門曰延義門，金鑾門曰千秋門，延和門曰章善門，保甯殿曰文思殿。

translations.literal: Yanxi Gate changed to Xuanren Gate, Chongming to Xingjiao, Changle to Guangzheng, Guangfan to Yingtian, Qianhua to Qianyuan, Xuanzheng to Fuzheng, Xuanzheng Hall to Zhenguan Hall, Rihua to Left Yanfu, Yuehua to Right Yanfu, Wanshou to Wanchun, Jiqing to Xingshan, Hanzhang to Yingfu, Hanqing to Yanyi, Jinluan to Qianqiu, Yanhe to Zhangshan, Baoning Hall to Wensi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: A long list renamed gates and halls—Yanxi to Xuanren, Changle to Guangzheng, and so on.

sentences.zh: 其見在門名，有與西京門同名者，並宜復洛京舊門名。

translations.literal: Existing gate names that share names with western capital gates should all restore old Luoyang gate names.
translations.idiomatic: Gates that duplicated Chang’an names reverted to old Luoyang labels.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrust the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: So ordered.

sentences.zh: 」乙酉夜，西北彗星長六七十丈，自軒轅大角及天市西垣，光輝猛怒，其長竟天。

translations.literal: ” On yiyou night, northwest comet length six or seven tens of zhang, from Xuanyuan, Great Horn, and Heavenly Market’s western wall, light fierce and angry, length reaching heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou night a comet sixty or seventy zhang long blazed from the northwest across Xuanyuan and the Market wall.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，有司修皇太后宮畢。

translations.literal: On bingyin, responsible offices finished repairing the Empress Dowager’s palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Empress Dowager’s palace was finished.

sentences.zh: 中書奏：「皇太后慈惠臨人，寬仁馭物，早葉伣天之兆，克彰誕聖之符。

translations.literal: Secretariat memorialized: “The Empress Dowager’s compassion oversees people,lenient benevolence governs affairs; early matched heaven’s leaning omen, fully displayed holy birth’s sign.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat praised her mercy and asked to name her palace Accumulated Goodness.

sentences.zh: 今輪奐新宮，規摹舊典，崇訓既征於信史，積善宜顯於昌期。

translations.literal: Now the revolving splendor of the new palace, model old canon; Chongxun already proved in faithful history, Accumulated Goodness should shine in flourishing period.
translations.idiomatic: The new palace followed old canon; Accumulated Goodness fit a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 太后宮請以積善為名。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager’s palace requests the name Accumulated Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed the name Accumulated Goodness for her palace.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 又以將卜郊禋，預調雅樂，宜乙太常卿張廷范充修樂懸使。

translations.literal: Also because suburban sacrifice will be divined, beforehand tune elegant music; Director of Rites Zhang Tingfan should be music-frame repair commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: With suburban rites coming, Zhang Tingfan was named to repair the ritual music frames.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，荊襄節度使趙匡凝奏為故使成汭立祠宇，從之。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Jingxiang military governor Zhao Kuangning memorialized to establish a shrine for the late commissioner Cheng Yun—approved.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Zhao Kuangning won approval to build a shrine for Cheng Yun.

sentences.zh: 己巳，太清宮使柳璨奏：「近敕改易宮殿門名，竊以玄元皇帝廟，西京曰太清宮，東京曰太微宮，其太清宮請復為太微宮，臣便給入官階。

translations.literal: On jisi, Supreme Ultimate Palace Minister Liu Can memorialized: “Recent edict changed palace and gate names; I consider the Primordial Lord’s temple—in western capital called Supreme Ultimate Palace, eastern capital called Taiwei Palace—the Supreme Ultimate Palace requests restore to Taiwei Palace; your servant then gives entering-office rank.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Liu Can asked to rename the Supreme Ultimate Palace Taiwei again and trade rank for it.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 庚午，敕：「所司定今年十月九日有事郊丘，其修制禮衣祭服宜令宰臣柳璨判，祭器宜令張文蔚、楊涉分判，儀仗車輅宜令太常卿張廷範判。

translations.literal: On gengwu, edict: “Offices fixed this year tenth month ninth day for suburban mound; ritual garments and sacrificial robes should have Grand Councillor Liu Can judge; sacrificial vessels Zhang Wenwei and Yang She divide; ritual guards and chariots Director of Rites Zhang Tingfan judge.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu suburban rites were set for the ninth of the tenth month with Liu Can, Zhang Wenwei, Yang She, and Zhang Tingfan dividing duties.

sentences.zh: 」壬申，制新除靜海軍節度使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校尚書左僕射、同平章事、兼安南都護、河南郡開國侯、食邑一千戶獨孤損可責授朝散大夫、棣州刺史，仍令御史台發遣出京訖聞奏。

translations.literal: ” On renshen, edict: newly appointed Jinghai military governor, Yinguanglu Grand Master, acting Left Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, also Protector-General of Annan, Marquis of Henan with 1,000 households Dugu Sun may be demoted to Court Gentleman for Scattered Honors, Bian prefectural governor, still ordered Censorate dispatch out of capital and memorialize when finished.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Dugu Sun, sent to Jinghai, was demoted to Bian prefect and ordered out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「朕謬將眇質，叨荷丕圖，常懷馭朽之心，每軫泣辜之念。

translations.literal: Edict said: “I wrongly place slight substance, presumptuously bear great design, always cherish steering rotten wood, every bend weeping guilt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict feigned reluctance to punish ministers.

sentences.zh: 諒于黜責，豈易施行。

translations.literal: Considering demotion and blame, how easy to implement.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment was never easy, it said.

sentences.zh: 左僕射裴樞、右僕射崔遠，雖罷機衡，尚居揆路，既處優崇之任，未傷進退之規。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Pei Shu, Right Vice Director Cui Yuan—though removed from the pivot, still occupy the chief path; already in exalted duty, not yet harming advance-retreat rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Pei Shu and Cui Yuan, though off the pivot, still walked the chief corridor.

sentences.zh: 不能秉志安家，但恣流言謗國，頗興物論，難抑朝章。

translations.literal: Unable to hold will and settle home, only indulge spreading slander harming the state; quite arousing public opinion, hard to suppress court statute.
translations.idiomatic: They would not be silent—they slandered the state and had to go.

sentences.zh: 須離八座之榮，尚付六條之政，勉思咎己，無至尤人。

translations.literal: Must leave the eight seats’ glory, still entrusted with six-tiao government; strive to blame self, do not reach to blame others.
translations.idiomatic: They must leave the council but would receive prefectures—blame yourselves, not others.”

sentences.zh: 樞可責授朝散大夫、登州刺史，遠可責授朝散大夫、萊州刺史，便發遣出京。

translations.literal: Shu may be demoted to Court Gentleman for Scattered Honors, Dengzhou prefect; Yuan may be demoted to Court Gentleman for Scattered Honors, Laizhou prefect; immediately dispatch out of capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was demoted to prefect of Deng, Yuan to Laizhou, and both were ordered out of the capital immediately.

sentences.zh: 」兵部郎中韋乾美貶沂州司戶。

translations.literal: ” War Director Wei Qianmei demoted to Yizhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: War Director Wei Qianmei was demoted to registrar of Yi.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，敕中書舍人封渭貶齊州司戶，右補闕鄭輦密州莒縣尉，兵部員外盧協祁州司戶，並員外置。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, edict Secretariat drafter Feng Wei demoted to Qizhou registrar; Right Remonstrator Zheng Nian Mizhou Juxian county aide; War aide Lu Xie Qizhou registrar—all supernumerary posts.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Feng Wei, Zheng Nian, and Lu Xie were demoted to distant posts on supernumerary rolls.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，敕吏部尚書陸扆貶濮州司戶，工部尚書王溥淄州司戶。

translations.literal: On yihai, edict Minister of Personnel Lu Yi demoted to Puzhou registrar; Minister of Works Wang Pu Zizhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Lu Yi and Wang Pu were demoted to registrars of Pu and Zi.

sentences.zh: 司天奏：「旬朔已前，星文變見，仰觀垂象，特軫聖慈。

translations.literal: Astronomical Commission memorialized: “Before the ten-day period, star texts changed and appeared; looking up at the suspended signs, specially bent the sagely compassion.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Commission reported omens had alarmed the throne.

sentences.zh: 自今月八日夜已後，連遇陰雨，測候不得。

translations.literal: From the eighth night of this month afterward, continuously met yin rain; observation could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Since the eighth, rain had blocked observation.

sentences.zh: 至十三日夜一更三點，天色暫晴，景緯分明，妖星不見於碧虛，災沴潛消於天漢者。

translations.literal: To the thirteenth night first watch third point, sky color briefly clear, scenery and constellations distinct—the baleful star not seen in azure void, calamity air secretly dissolved in heavenly river.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth at the first watch the sky cleared—the comet was gone and the omen seemed spent.

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「上天謫見，下土震驚，致夙夜之沈憂，恐生靈之多難。

translations.literal: ” Edict said: “Heaven’s reproach appeared, below earth shocked; causing night-vigil deep worry, fearing the hundred people’s many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thanked heaven: the comet had terrified the realm and the emperor had fasted in fear.

sentences.zh: 不居正殿，盡輟常羞，益務齋虔，以申禳禱。

translations.literal: Not occupying the main hall, entirely stopping regular delicacies, increasing ritual purity, to extend prayer.
translations.idiomatic: He had left the main hall, cut meals, and prayed in earnest.

sentences.zh: 果致玄穹覆祐，孛彗消除，豈罪己之感通，免貽人於災沴。

translations.literal: Indeed reached dark heaven’s covering blessing, broom comet eliminated—how guilt-on-self’s resonance, avoiding leaving the people calamity air.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven answered; the comet vanished—was it penance that spared the people?”

sentences.zh: 式觀陳奏，深慰誠懷。

translations.literal: Observing the submitted memorial, deeply comforted sincere feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial comforted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 」丙子，敕戶部郎中李仁儉貶和王府諮議，起居舍人盧仁烱安州司戶，壽安尉、直弘文館盧晏滄州東光尉。

translations.literal: ” On bingzi, edict Households Director Li Renjian demoted to Prince of He staff counselor; attendance recorder Lu Renjiong Anzhou registrar; Shou’an county aide, direct Hongwen Guan Yan Cangzhou Dongguang aide.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi more officials were demoted, including Li Renjian and Lu Renjiong.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，陳許節度使張全義奏：「得許州留後狀申，自多事以來，許州權為列郡，今特創鼓角樓訖，請復為軍額。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Chenxu military governor Zhang Quanyi memorialized: “Received Xuzhou acting military governor’s report: since many troubles, Xuzhou was temporarily a common prefecture; now specially created drum-and-horn tower finished—request restore military designation.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Zhang Quanyi asked to restore Xuzhou’s military banner now its drum tower was rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 」敕旨依舊置忠武軍牌額。

translations.literal: ” Edict: as before set Zhongwu Army plaque and designation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu Army’s name and plaque were restored.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，宴群臣於崇勳殿，全忠與王鎔、羅紹威置宴也。

translations.literal: On wuyin, banquet for hundred ministers in Chongxun Hall—Quanzhong with Wang Rong and Luo Shaowei set the feast.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Quanzhong, Wang Rong, and Luo Shaowei feasted the court at Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，敕特進、檢校司徒、守太保致仕趙崇可曹州司戶，銀青光祿大夫、兵部侍郎王贊可濮州司戶。

translations.literal: On gengchen, edict Special Advance, acting Minister of Works, acting Grand Guardian retired Zhao Chong may be Caozhou registrar; Yinguanglu Grand Master, Vice Minister of War Wang Zan may be Puzhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Zhao Chong and Wang Zan were demoted to distant registrars.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，敕責授登州刺史裴樞可隴州司戶，責授棣州刺史獨孤損可瓊州司戶，責授萊州刺史崔遠可白州司戶。

translations.literal: On xinsi, edict demoted Dengzhou prefect Pei Shu may be Longzhou registrar; demoted Bian prefect Dugu Sun may be Qiongzhou registrar; demoted Laizhou prefect Cui Yuan may be Baizhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Shu, Sun, and Yuan were pushed farther—Long, Qiong, and Bai.

sentences.zh: 壬午，敕司勳員外韋甄責授和王友，洛陽縣令李光序責授左春坊典設郎。

translations.literal: On renwu, edict Merit aide Wei Zhen demoted to Prince of He companion; Luoyang magistrate Li Guangxu demoted to Left Spring Palace provisioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Wei Zhen and Li Guangxu were demoted within the capital ranks.

sentences.zh: 甲申，秘書監崔仁魯可密州司戶，國子祭酒崔澄陳州司戶，太府少卿裴鍼徐州司戶，衛尉少卿裴紓曹州南華尉，左補闕崔咸休甯陵尉，司封員外薛滈輝州司戶，前鹽鐵推官獨孤憲臨沂尉，秘書少監裴鉥鄆州司戶，長安尉、直史館裴格符離尉，兵部郎中李象鄭州司戶，刑部員外盧薦范縣尉。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Secretariat Director Cui Renlu may be Mizhou registrar; National University Chancellor Cui Cheng Chenzhou registrar; Grand Treasury Vice Director Pei Zhen Xuzhou registrar; Court of Imperial Guards Vice Director Pei Shu Caozhou Nanhua aide; Left Remonstrator Cui Xianxiu Ningling aide; Seals aide Xue Hao Hui prefectural registrar; former salt-and-iron clerk Dugu Xian Linyi aide; Secretariat Vice Director Pei Yue Yanzhou registrar; Chang’an aide, direct Historiography Pei Ge Feiqi aide; War Director Li Xiang Zhengzhou registrar; Justice aide Lu Jian Fan county aide.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen a sweep demoted a dozen more officials connected to the fallen council.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，潁州汝陰縣人彭文妻產三男。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Yingzhou Ruoyin county man Peng Wen’s wife bore three sons.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu a woman in Ruoyin bore triplets.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，敕以翰林學士、尚書職方郎中張策兼充史館修撰，修國史。

translations.literal: On dinghai, edict Hanlin academician, Director of Palace Armories Zhang Ce also Historiography compiler, revise national history.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Zhang Ce was ordered to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 六月戊子朔，敕：「責授隴州司戶裴樞、瓊州司戶獨孤損、白州司戶崔遠、濮州司戶陸扆、淄州司戶王溥、曹州司戶趙崇，濮州司戶王贊等，皆受國恩，咸當重任。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, wuzi; edict: “Demoted Longzhou registrar Pei Shu, Qiongzhou registrar Dugu Sun, Baizhou registrar Cui Yuan, Puzhou registrar Lu Yi, Zizhou registrar Wang Pu, Caozhou registrar Zhao Chong, Puzhou registrar Wang Zan and others—all received state grace, all should have heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi an edict said the exiled ministers had betrayed grace despite high office.

sentences.zh: 罔思罄謁，唯貯奸邪，雖已謫于遐方，尚難寬于國典。

translations.literal: Not thinking to exhaust loyalty, only storing treachery and evil; though already demoted to distant regions, still hard to widen in state canon.
translations.idiomatic: They had stored treachery; exile was not enough.

sentences.zh: 委御史台差人所在州縣各賜自盡。

translations.literal: Entrust Censorate to send men in each prefecture and county where they are to grant self-destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate was to order them to kill themselves wherever they were found.

sentences.zh: 」時樞等七人已至滑州，皆並命于白馬驛，全忠令投屍於河。

translations.literal: ” At that time Shu and seven others had already reached Hua Prefecture; all were killed together at Baima Post; Quanzhong ordered bodies thrown in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Seven of them reached Hua Prefecture and were murdered together at Baima Post; Quanzhong had the bodies thrown into the river.

sentences.zh: 己丑，敕：「君臣之間，進退以禮，矧於求舊，欲保初終，苟自掇于悔尤，亦須行於黜責。

translations.literal: On jichou, edict: “Between lord and minister, advance and retreat by ritual; especially in seeking the old, wishing to preserve the beginning and end—if oneself plucks regret, still must execute demotion and blame.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou an edict preached ritual advance and retreat, then punished another elder.

sentences.zh: 特進、守司空致仕、上柱國、河東縣開國公、食邑二千戶裴贄早以公望，常踐台司，靡聞竭力以匡時，每務養恬而避事。

translations.literal: Special Advance, acting Minister of Works retired, Pillar, Duke of Hedong with 2,000 households Pei Zan early by public repute often tread the terrace departments; not heard to exhaust strength to correct the time, every matter nurturing quiet to avoid affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zan, retired grandee, had never strained to steady the throne and had hid in quiet.

sentences.zh: 洎從請老，不謂無恩，合慎樞機，動循規矩。

translations.literal: When following request for old age, not said without grace; together careful of the pivot, moves should follow rules.
translations.idiomatic: His retirement had been gracious; he should have kept silent.

sentences.zh: 雖雲勇退，乃有後言，自為簿從之酋，頗失人臣之禮。

translations.literal: Though cloud brave retreat, then had later words; self was chief of registry followers, quite lost minister’s ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He boasted of retiring bravely yet gossiped on—unworthy of a minister.

sentences.zh: 謫居郡掾，用正朝綱，可責授青州司戶。

translations.literal: Demoted to occupy prefectural aide, to correct court cord; may be demoted to Qingzhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to registrar of Qing.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中李煦可萊州司戶。

translations.literal: Justice Director Li Xu may be Laizhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xu was sent to Laizhou as registrar.

sentences.zh: 」辛卯，太微宮使柳璨奏：「前使裴樞充宮使日，權奏請玄元觀為太清宮，又別奏在京弘道觀為太清宮，至今未有制置。

translations.literal: ” On xinmao, Taiwei Palace Minister Liu Can memorialized: “When former commissioner Pei Shu served as palace commissioner, he provisionally memorialized requesting Xuan Yuan Abbey as Supreme Ultimate Palace, and separately memorialized Hongdao Abbey in the capital as Supreme Ultimate Palace—until now no fixed disposition.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Liu Can complained Pei Shu had left two competing Supreme Ultimate sites.

sentences.zh: 伏以今年十月九日陛下親事南禋，先謁聖祖廟，弘道觀既未修葺，玄元觀又在北山，若車駕出城，禮非便穩。

translations.literal: Considering this year tenth month ninth day Your Majesty personally performs southern suburban sacrifice, first visiting the sage-ancestor temple; Hongdao Abbey is not yet repaired, Xuan Yuan Abbey is also on North Mountain—if the imperial carriage exits the city, ritual is not convenient and stable.
translations.idiomatic: For the southern suburban rite on the ninth of the tenth month neither Hongdao nor North Mountain Xuan Yuan suited the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 今欲只留北邙山上老君廟一所，其玄元觀請拆入都城，於清化坊內建置太微宮，以備車駕行事。

translations.literal: Now wish only to retain one Lord Lao temple on North Mang mountain; Xuan Yuan Abbey requests dismantle into the capital, build Taiwei Palace in Qinghua ward, to prepare imperial carriage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed one temple on North Mang and moving Xuan Yuan into the city as Taiwei Palace in Qinghua ward.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，敕：「諸道節度、觀察、防禦、刺史等，部內有新除朝官、前資朝官，敕到後三日內發遣赴闕，仍差人監送。

translations.literal: On renchen, edict: “Circuit military governors, observers, defenders, prefects, and others—within their departments newly appointed court officials and former-candidate court officials, within three days after edict arrival dispatch to court, still send men to escort.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen edicts ordered all new court appointees in the provinces to reach the capital within three days under escort.

sentences.zh: 所在州縣不得停住，苟或稽違，必議貶黜。

translations.literal: Where they are, prefectures and counties may not detain; if there is delay, demotion will be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials could not hold them; delay meant demotion.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrust the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: So ordered.

sentences.zh: 」癸巳，敕：「衛尉少卿敬沼是裴贄之甥。

translations.literal: ” On guisi, edict: “Court of Imperial Guards Vice Director Jing Zhao is Pei Zan’s nephew.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Jing Zhao, nephew of Pei Zan, was targeted.

sentences.zh: 常累于舅，或以明經撓文柄，或以私事竊化權。

translations.literal: Often tied to the uncle, or by classics degree obstructed the literary handle, or by private affairs stole transforming power.
translations.idiomatic: He had traded on his uncle’s name to meddle in appointments.

sentences.zh: 贄已左遷，爾又何追！

translations.literal: Zan already demoted left—why do you still pursue!
translations.idiomatic: Zan was gone—why follow him still?”

sentences.zh: 可貶徐州蕭縣尉。

translations.literal: May be demoted to Xuzhou Xiao county aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to aide of Xiao in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 」丙申，敕：「福建每年進橄欖子，比因閹豎出自閩中，牽於嗜好之間，遂成貢奉之典。

translations.literal: ” On bingshen, edict: “Fujian each year presents olive fruit; recently because eunuchs came from Min, dragged into fondness between tastes, thus became tribute canon.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Fujian’s olive tribute was canceled—eunuchs from Min had made it a whim.

sentences.zh: 雖嘉忠藎，伏恐煩勞。

translations.literal: Though praising loyal candor, I fear troubling labor.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute flattered loyalty but burdened the people.

sentences.zh: 今後只供進蠟麵茶，其進橄欖子宜停。

translations.literal: Hereafter only supply wax-noodle tea; presenting olive fruit should stop.
translations.idiomatic: Only wax-noodle tea would be sent thereafter.

sentences.zh: 」戊戌，敕：「密縣令裴練貶登州牟平尉，長水令崔仁略淄州高苑尉，福昌主簿陸珣沂州新泰尉，泥水令獨孤韜范縣尉，並員外置，皆裴樞、崔遠、陸扆宗黨也。

translations.literal: ” On wuxu, edict: “Mizhou magistrate Pei Lian demoted to Dengzhou Mouping aide; Changshui magistrate Cui Renlue Zizhou Gaoyuan aide; Fuchang chief clerk Lu Xun Yizhou Xintai aide; Nishui magistrate Dugu Tao Fan county aide—all supernumerary posts; all Pei Shu, Cui Yuan, Lu Yi clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu more clan members of the murdered ministers were exiled to petty posts.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，湖南馬殷奏，岳州洞庭、青草之側，有古祠四所，先以荒圮，臣復修廟了畢，乞賜名額者。

translations.literal: On renyin, Hunan Ma Yin memorialized: beside Yue Prefecture’s Dongting and Qingcao, four ancient shrines, formerly ruined—I restored the temples finished, begging grant name plaques.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Ma Yin of Hunan asked titles for four shrines he had rebuilt beside Dongting Lake.

sentences.zh: 敕旨黃陵二妃祠曰懿節，洞庭君祠曰利涉侯，青草祠曰安流侯；

translations.literal: Edict: Yellow Mound Two Consorts shrine called Yijie; Dongting Lord shrine called Lisherhou; Qingcao shrine called Anliu Marquis;
translations.idiomatic: They were named Yijie for the Two Consorts, Lisherhou for Dongting’s lord, Anliu Marquis for Qingcao;

sentences.zh: 三閭大夫祠，先以澧朗觀察使雷滿奏，已封昭靈侯，宜依天祐元年九月二十九日敕處分。

translations.literal: Three Gorges Great Officer shrine—formerly Li Lang observation commissioner Lei Man memorialized, already enfeoffed Bright Spirit Marquis—should follow Tianyou year 1 ninth month twenty-ninth day edict disposition.
translations.idiomatic: the Three Gorges officer kept his prior Bright Spirit Marquis title from Lei Man’s memorial.

sentences.zh: 丙午，全忠奏：「得宰相柳璨記事，欲拆北邙山下玄元觀移入都內，於清化坊取舊昭明寺基，建置太微宮，準備十月九日南郊行事。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Quanzhong memorialized: “Received Grand Councillor Liu Can’s record: wishes to dismantle North Mang foot Xuan Yuan Abbey and move into the capital, at Qinghua ward take old Zhaoming Temple base, build Taiwei Palace, prepare tenth month ninth day southern suburban affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Quanzhong reported Liu Can’s plan to move Xuan Yuan Abbey into Qinghua ward for the suburban rite.

sentences.zh: 緣延資庫鹽鐵並無物力，令臣商量者。

translations.literal: Because Extended Treasury salt-and-iron altogether have no material power, ordered your servant to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury had no funds—Quanzhong was asked to pay.

sentences.zh: 臣已牒判六軍諸衛張全義指揮工作訖。

translations.literal: Your servant already dispatched controller of Six Armies Zhang Quanyi to direct work finished.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhang Quanyi finish the work.

sentences.zh: 」優詔嘉之。

translations.literal: ” Favorable edict praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 丁未，敕：「太子賓客柳遜嘗為張浚租庸判官，又王溥監修日奏充判官，授工部侍郎，又與趙崇、裴贄為刎頸之交。

translations.literal: On dingwei, edict: “Crown Prince Mentor Liu Xun once was Zhang Jun’s rent-and-tax clerk; also when Wang Pu supervised revision memorialized him as clerk, appointed Minister of Works; also with Zhao Chong, Pei Zan sworn-neck friendship.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Liu Xun, ally of the fallen, was forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 昨裴樞等得罪之時，合當連坐，尚矜暮齒，且俾懸車，可本官致仕。

translations.literal: Yesterday when Pei Shu and others met guilt, should have been implicated together; still pitying evening years, temporarily permitting suspended carriage—may keep original office and retire.
translations.idiomatic: He should have shared their guilt; only age spared him retirement.

sentences.zh: 」戊申，敕前司勳員外郎、賜緋魚袋李延古責授衛尉寺主簿。

translations.literal: ” On wushen, edict former Merit aide, bearer of crimson fish Li Yangu demoted to Court of Imperial Guards chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Li Yangu was demoted to a minor guards post.

sentences.zh: 七月戊午朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, wuwu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the first day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，賜全忠《迎鑾記功碑文》，立於都內。

translations.literal: On xinyou, granted Quanzhong “Record of Welcoming the Imperial Carriage and Recording Merit” stele text, erected within the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Quanzhong received a merit stele erected in the capital.

sentences.zh: 全忠進助郊禮錢三萬貫。

translations.literal: Quanzhong presented aid for suburban ritual money thirty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: He gave thirty thousand strings cash for the suburban rite.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，再貶柳遜曹州司馬。

translations.literal: On guihai, again demoted Liu Xun to Caozhou aide.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Liu Xun was demoted again to Caozhou aide.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，敕全忠請鑄河中、晉、絳諸縣印，縣名內有「城」字並落下，如密鄭、絳、蒲例，單名為文。

translations.literal: On xinsi, edict Quanzhong requested cast Hezhong, Jin, Jiang prefectural seals; county names with “city” character all drop down, like Mi, Zheng, Jiang, Pu precedent—single name as text.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Quanzhong was allowed new county seals dropping the character “city.”

sentences.zh: 壬午，宰臣柳璨、禮部尚書蘇循充皇太后冊禮使。

translations.literal: On renwu, Grand Councillor Liu Can, Minister of Rites Su Xun filled Empress Dowager investiture ritual commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Liu Can and Su Xun led the Empress Dowager’s investiture.

sentences.zh: 是日，于積善宮行禮畢，帝乘輦赴太后宮稱賀。

translations.literal: That day, at Accumulated Goodness Palace rites finished, emperor rode palanquin to Empress Dowager’s palace to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: That day, at Accumulated Goodness Palace, the boy emperor went to congratulate her.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，太常禮院奏：「每月朔望，皇帝赴積善宮起居，文武百官于宮門進名起居。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Director of Rites memorialized: “Each month new and full moon, emperor goes to Accumulated Goodness Palace for routine audience; civil and military hundred officials at palace gate present names for routine audience.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu monthly visits to the dowager at Accumulated Goodness Palace were fixed.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 八月丁亥朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the first day of the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 戊子，制中書舍人姚洎可尚書戶部侍郎，充元帥府判官，從全忠奏也。

translations.literal: On wuzi, edict Secretariat drafter Yao Ji may be Households Vice Minister, fill marshal’s headquarters judge—on Quanzhong’s memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Yao Ji became Households Vice Minister and judge at Quanzhong’s headquarters.

sentences.zh: 洛苑使奏谷水屯地內嘉禾合穎。

translations.literal: Luoyuan commissioner memorialized Gushui estate land within had auspicious grain double ears.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyuan commissioner reported double-eared grain at Gushui estate.

sentences.zh: 乙未，敕：「偽稱官階人泉州晉江縣應鄉貢明經陳文巨招伏罪款，付河南府決殺。

translations.literal: On yiwei, edict: “False claiming office rank, Quanzhou Jinjiang county presented scholar for classics degree Chen Wenju confessed crimes; entrust Henan prefecture to decide and execute.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei a fake degree-holder in Jinjiang was sent to Henan for execution.

sentences.zh: 庚子，敕：「漢代元勳，鄧禹冠諸侯之上；

translations.literal: On gengzi, edict: “Han dynasty founding ministers, Deng Yu topped the feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an edict ranked Quanzhong beside Han and Jin paragons.

sentences.zh: 晉朝重位，王導居百辟之先。

translations.literal: Jin dynasty heavy position, Wang Dao stood before the hundred ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Like Deng Yu and Wang Dao, merit earned singular honor.

sentences.zh: 皆道著匡扶，功宣寰宇，其於崇寵，迥異等倫。

translations.literal: All the Way displayed in aiding support, achievement proclaimed to the realm; in exalted favor, quite different in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Their service had steadied realms; reward should be unmatched.

sentences.zh: 朕獲以眇躬，重興丕運，凡關制度，必法舊章，實仗勳賢，永安宗社。

translations.literal: I obtained with slight body to again raise great fortune; all concerning institutions must follow old statutes; truly rely on meritorious worthies to forever settle the altars.
translations.idiomatic: The boy throne rose by merit; institutions would follow old forms.

sentences.zh: 副元帥梁王正守太尉、中書令，忠武軍節度使、河南尹張全義亦正守中書令，俱深倚注，鹹正台衡。

translations.literal: Deputy Marshal Prince of Liang correctly holds Grand Preceptor, Central Director; Zhongwu military governor, Henan governor Zhang Quanyi also correctly holds Central Director—both deeply relied upon, all upright as scale beam.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang held Grand Preceptor and Director; Zhang Quanyi held Director—both pillars.

sentences.zh: 其朝廷冊禮、告祀天地宗廟，其司空則差官攝行，太尉、侍中、中書令即宰臣攝行。

translations.literal: Court investiture rites, announcing sacrifice to heaven, earth, and ancestral temple—the Minister of Works then sends an official to act; Grand Preceptor, Palace Attendant, Central Director then Grand Councillors act.
translations.idiomatic: At state rites the Minister of Works or chancellors would stand in by rank.

sentences.zh: 今太尉副元帥任冠籓垣，每遇行禮之時，或不在京國，即事須差攝太尉行事。

translations.literal: Now Grand Preceptor Deputy Marshal’s task crowns the frontier; each time rites are performed, sometimes not in the capital—then affairs require a stand-in as Grand Preceptor to perform.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Liang was away, another must act as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 全義見居闕下，任正中樞，不可更差別官又攝中書令事。

translations.literal: Quanyi now dwells at the gate, task in the center pivot—may not further appoint another to act Central Director affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi was in the capital and would act Director himself.

sentences.zh: 其太尉官，如梁王朝覲在京，便委行事，如卻赴鎮，即依前攝行。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor office—if the Prince of Liang attends court in the capital, then entrust performance; if again goes to garrison, then per before act.
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince of Liang was present he would perform; if in his province, a stand-in would.

sentences.zh: 所合差中書令，便委全義以本官行禮。

translations.literal: What should stand in as Central Director, then entrust Quanyi with original office to perform rites.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi would perform Director rites in his own person.

sentences.zh: 其侍中、司空、司徒即臨時差官。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, Minister of Education then temporarily assign officials.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and the Works and Education ministers would be named ad hoc.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrust the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: So ordered.

sentences.zh: 」壬寅，敕：「前太中大夫、尚書兵部侍郎、賜紫金魚袋司空圖俊造登科，朱紫升籍，既養高以傲代，類移山而釣名。

translations.literal: ” On renyin, edict: “Former Grand Master, War Vice Minister, bearer of purple-gold fish Sikong Tu handsome talent passed degree, vermilion and purple rose in registry; already nurturing height to disdain the age, like moving a mountain to fish for name.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Sikong Tu, lofty scholar who scorned office, was sent home.

sentences.zh: 志樂漱流，心輕食祿。

translations.literal: Will delighted in rinsing streams, heart light on eating salary.
translations.idiomatic: He loved streams more than salary.

sentences.zh: 匪夷匪惠，難居公正之朝；

translations.literal: Neither Yi nor Hui—hard to dwell in the impartial court;
translations.idiomatic: Neither helpful nor gracious—he could not serve an impartial court;

sentences.zh: 載省載思，當徇幽棲之志。

translations.literal: repeatedly reflecting, repeatedly thinking—should follow secluded dwelling’s will.
translations.idiomatic: reflection counseled retreat.

sentences.zh: 宜放還中條山。

translations.literal: Should release to return to Zhongtiao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He was released to Zhongtiao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 」癸卯，敕太常卿張廷範宜充南郊禮儀使。

translations.literal: ” On guimao, edict Director of Rites Zhang Tingfan should be southern suburban ritual commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Zhang Tingfan led the southern suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 丁未，制削奪荊襄節度使趙匡凝在身官爵。

translations.literal: On dingwei, edict stripped Jingxiang military governor Zhao Kuangning of all offices and ranks held in life.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Zhao Kuangning was stripped of every rank.

sentences.zh: 是月乙未，全忠遣大將楊師厚討匡凝，收唐、鄧、復、郢、隨等州，全忠自率親軍赴之。

translations.literal: That month on yiwei, Quanzhong sent great general Yang Shihou to campaign against Kuangning, taking Tang, Deng, Fu, Ying, Sui and other prefectures; Quanzhong himself led personal army to go.
translations.idiomatic: That yiwei Quanzhong sent Yang Shihou against Kuangning and marched himself after taking several prefectures.

sentences.zh: 荊襄之軍，陣于漢水之陰。

translations.literal: Jingxiang’s army arrayed on the Han River’s north bank.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingxiang army lined the north bank of the Han.

sentences.zh: 九月丁巳朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, dingsi.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the first day of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，楊師厚於襄州西六十里陰谷江口伐竹木為浮梁。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Yang Shihou at sixty li west of Xiang Prefecture at Yingu River mouth felled bamboo and wood for a pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Yang Shihou built a pontoon bridge sixty li west of Xiangzhou at Yingu River.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，梁成，引軍渡江。

translations.literal: On guihai, bridge completed, led army across the river.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the bridge was done and the army crossed.

sentences.zh: 甲子，趙匡凝率勁兵二萬，陣于江之湄。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Zhao Kuangning led crack troops twenty thousand, arrayed at the river’s shore.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Zhao Kuangning drew up twenty thousand elite troops on the shore.

sentences.zh: 師厚一戰敗之，遂乘勝躡之，陣於城下。

translations.literal: Shihou one battle defeated him, then taking victory pursued, arrayed below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou routed him in one fight and pressed to the walls.

sentences.zh: 是夜，匡凝挈其孥潰圍遁去。

translations.literal: That night, Kuangning took wife and children, broke encirclement and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That night Kuangning fled with his family through the broken siege.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，師厚入襄陽。

translations.literal: On yichou, Shihou entered Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Shihou entered Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，全忠繼至。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Quanzhong followed and arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Quanzhong arrived in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 壬申，匡凝牙將王建武遣押牙常質以荊南降。

translations.literal: On renshen, Kuangning’s staff officer Wang Jianwu sent escort officer Chang Zhi with Jingnan surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Wang Jianwu sent Chang Zhi to surrender Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 言權知荊南軍府事趙匡明今月十一日棄城上峽，奔蜀川。

translations.literal: Saying acting Jingnan military government Zhao Kuangming on the eleventh of this month abandoned the city, went up the gorges, fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He said Zhao Kuangming had abandoned the city on the eleventh and fled upriver into Shu.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「梁王躬臨貔武，收復荊、襄，拔峴首若轉丸，平荊門如沃雪，連收兩鎮，並走二凶。

translations.literal: Edict: "The Prince of Liang personally led troops at Pi Wu, recovered Jing and Xiang, took Xian shou as if turning a pellet, pacified Jing Gate as if melting snow, seized two circuits in succession, and together drove off two villains.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang led troops at Pi Wu, recovered Jing and Xiang, took Xian shou swiftly, pacified Jing Gate easily, seized two circuits, and drove off two enemies.

sentences.zh: 乃睠勳庸，載深嘉注，宜賜詔獎飾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was mindful of meritorious service and received deep commendation; an edict of reward and decoration should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: His merit drew deep praise; he was to receive an edict of reward.

sentences.zh: 」內出宣旨：「妳婆楊氏可賜號昭儀，妳婆王氏可封郡夫人，第二妳婆王氏先帝已封郡夫人，准楊氏例改封。

translations.literal: " An edict issued from within stated: "Wet-nurse Yang may be granted the title Zhaoyi; wet-nurse Wang may be enfeoffed as Lady of a Commandery; the second wet-nurse Wang, whom the late emperor had already enfeoffed as Lady of a Commandery, should be re-enfeoffed following Yang's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An inner edict said wet-nurse Yang would receive the title Zhaoyi, wet-nurse Wang would become a commandery lady, and the second wet-nurse Wang—already enfeoffed by the late emperor—would be re-enfeoffed like Yang.

sentences.zh: 」中書奏議言：「乳母古無封夫人賜內職之例，近代因循，殊乖典故。

translations.literal: " The Secretariat memorialized: "For wet-nurses antiquity had no precedent of enfeoffing ladies or granting inner-court offices; recent ages have followed custom, which greatly departs from canonical models.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat argued that enfeoffing wet-nurses and granting inner offices had no ancient precedent and violated proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 昔漢順帝以乳母宋氏為山陽君，安帝乳母王氏曰野王君，當時朝議非之。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Shun of Han made wet-nurse Song Lady of Shanyang; Emperor An's wet-nurse Wang was styled Lady of Yewang—court opinion at the time condemned this.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shundi made his wet-nurse Lady of Shanyang and Andi's wet-nurse Lady of Yewang—both were condemned at court.

sentences.zh: 今國祚中興，禮宜求舊。

translations.literal: Now the dynastic fortune is reviving; ritual should seek the old models.
translations.idiomatic: With the dynasty reviving, ritual should return to older models.

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，楊氏望賜號安聖君，王氏曰福聖君，第二王氏曰康聖君。

translations.literal: Your subjects have deliberated: Yang should be granted the title Lady Ansheng; Wang should be styled Lady Fusheng; the second Wang should be styled Lady Kangsheng.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers proposed Lady Ansheng for Yang, Lady Fusheng for Wang, and Lady Kangsheng for the second Wang.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 己巳，敕武成王廟宜改為武明王。

translations.literal: On jisi, an edict ordered the temple of King Wucheng changed to King Wuming.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the temple of King Wucheng was renamed King Wuming.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，敕先擇十月九日有事郊丘，備物之間，有所未辦，宜改用十一月十九日。

translations.literal: On yiyou, an edict stated that the southern suburban rite first set for the ninth day of the tenth month, while preparing the ritual objects, had items still incomplete; it should be changed to the nineteenth day of the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the southern suburban rite set for the tenth month's ninth day was postponed to the eleventh month's nineteenth because preparations were incomplete.

sentences.zh: 十月丙戌朔，制梁王全忠可充諸道兵馬元帥，別開府幕，加食邑通前一萬五千戶，實封一千五百戶。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, bingxu, an order made Liang Wang Quanzhong Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits' Armies and Horses, with a separate commissionerate and staff, and added fief households to a total of fifteen thousand with fifteen hundred actual enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, first of the tenth month, Zhu Quanzhong was made commander-in-chief of all circuits' armies with a separate staff and fifteen thousand fief households, fifteen hundred enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 金州馮行襲奏當道昭信軍額內一字，與元帥全忠諱字同，乃賜號戎昭軍。

translations.literal: Feng Xingxi of Jin Prefecture memorialized that one character in the local Zhaoxin Army designation matched Commander Quanzhong's taboo; the army was therefore renamed Rongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingxi reported a taboo clash in the army name and it was renamed Rongzhao Army.

sentences.zh: 制削奪荊南留後趙匡凝官爵。

translations.literal: An order stripped Acting Governor of Jingnan Zhao Kuangning of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangning of Jingnan was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，敕：「洛城坊曲內，舊有朝臣諸司宅舍，經亂荒榛。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict stated: "Within the wards and lanes of Luoyang city there were formerly mansions of court officials and government offices; after the disorders they lay waste in brambles.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai an edict said old official and government mansions in Luoyang's wards had been ruined in the disorders.

sentences.zh: 張全義葺理已來，皆已耕墾，既供軍賦，即系公田。

translations.literal: Since Zhang Quanyi's restoration, all have been plowed and opened; they already supply military levies and are public fields.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhang Quanyi restored them, the land had been plowed for military levies as public fields.

sentences.zh: 或恐每有披論，認為世業，須煩按驗，遂啟幸門。

translations.literal: Lest there be repeated petitions claiming them as hereditary property, requiring verification and opening the gate to favoritism,
translations.idiomatic: To stop repeated claims of hereditary ownership and favor-seeking petitions,

sentences.zh: 其都內坊曲及畿內已耕植田土，諸色人並不得論認。

translations.literal: within the capital wards and planted fields in the capital region, persons of every status may not petition to claim them.
translations.idiomatic: no one might claim planted fields in the capital wards or nearby region.

sentences.zh: 如要業田，一任買置。

translations.literal: If one needs farmland, one may buy it outright.
translations.idiomatic: Those needing land could buy it.

sentences.zh: 凡論認者，不在給還之限。

translations.literal: All who petition to claim are outside the limit of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Claims were not eligible for return.

sentences.zh: 如有本主元自差人勾當，不在此限。

translations.literal: If the original owner had long sent agents to manage the land, that is outside this restriction.
translations.idiomatic: Land long managed by the original owner's agents was exempt.

sentences.zh: 如荒田無主，即許識認。

translations.literal: If wasteland has no owner, claiming is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ownerless wasteland could be claimed.

sentences.zh: 付河南府。

translations.literal: Entrusted to Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Prefecture was charged with enforcement.

sentences.zh: 」甲午，起居郎蘇楷駁昭宗諡號曰：「帝王禦宇，由理亂以審汙隆；

translations.literal: " On jiawu, Attendant Su Kai rebutted Emperor Zhaozong's posthumous title, saying: "When emperors rule the realm, rise and fall are judged by order and disorder;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Attendant Su Kai challenged Zhaozong's posthumous title: emperors' reputations depend on order versus chaos;

sentences.zh: 宗祀配天，資諡號以定升降。

translations.literal: ancestral sacrifice matching Heaven relies on posthumous titles to fix elevation and descent.
translations.idiomatic: posthumous names fix how they are honored in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 故臣下君上皆不得而私也。

translations.literal: Therefore neither subjects nor rulers may treat this as private.
translations.idiomatic: Neither ruler nor subject may treat this privately.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下順考古道，昭彰至公，既當不諱之朝，寧阻上言之路。

translations.literal: We submit that Your Majesty follows antiquity and makes utmost fairness manifest; now in an age without taboo, how can the path of remonstrance be blocked?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty follows antiquity and fairness; in an age without taboo, remonstrance must be heard.

sentences.zh: 伏以昭宗皇帝睿哲居尊，恭儉垂化，其於善美，孰敢蔽虧。

translations.literal: We submit that Emperor Zhaozong, wise and sagely in dignity, respectful and frugal in transforming the realm, in goodness and beauty who would dare conceal or diminish?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong was wise, respectful, and frugal—who could deny his virtues?

sentences.zh: 然而否運莫興，至理猶鬱，遂致四方多事，萬乘頻遷。

translations.literal: Yet adverse fortune did not rise; supreme principle remained depressed, so the four quarters had many affairs and the Son of Heaven moved his seat repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fortune failed, principle was blocked, the realm was troubled, and the throne moved often.

sentences.zh: 始則閹豎倡狂，受幽辱於東內；

translations.literal: At first eunuchs led madness and he suffered seclusion and insult in the Eastern Inner Palace;
translations.idiomatic: First eunuchs drove him into insult and confinement in the Eastern Palace;

sentences.zh: 終則嬪嬙悖亂，罹夭閼於中闈。

translations.literal: at last palace women rebelled and he met untimely obstruction in the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: then palace women rebelled and he died in the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 其于易名，宜循考行。

translations.literal: As to changing his name, his conduct should be examined.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name should reflect his conduct.

sentences.zh: 有司先定尊諡曰聖穆景文孝皇帝，廟號昭宗，敢言溢美，似異直書。

translations.literal: The responsible offices first fixed the honored posthumous title Sage, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, Filial Emperor, temple name Zhaozong—daring to speak of overflowing praise seems unlike straightforward recording.
translations.idiomatic: Offices had set Sage, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, Filial Emperor with temple name Zhaozong—overpraise unlike honest history.

sentences.zh: 按後漢和、安、順帝，緣非功德，遂改宗稱，以允臣下之請。

translations.literal: According to Later Han, Emperors He, An, and Shun, because merit was lacking, changed their temple designations to satisfy subjects' requests.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han emperors He, An, and Shun changed temple names when merit was lacking, as subjects asked.

sentences.zh: 今郊禋有日，祫祭惟時。

translations.literal: Now the suburban sacrifice has a set day and the collective ancestral rite is timely.
translations.idiomatic: With suburban rites and ancestral worship near,

sentences.zh: 將期允愜列聖之心，更下詳議新廟之稱。

translations.literal: We will expect to satisfy the hearts of the former sages and send down further deliberation on the new temple designation.
translations.idiomatic: the court should satisfy the former emperors and deliberate anew on the temple name.

sentences.zh: 庶使葉先朝罪己之德，表聖主無私之明。

translations.literal: So that the former dynasty's virtue of blaming oneself may be joined and the sage ruler's fairness without partiality may be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: This would honor the late dynasty's self-blame and show the present ruler's impartiality.

sentences.zh: 」楷，禮部尚書循之子，凡劣無藝。

translations.literal: " Kai was son of Minister of Rites Su Xun, vulgar and without talent.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was son of Su Xun, Minister of Rites—a mediocrity.

sentences.zh: 乾甯二年應進士登第後，物論以為濫，昭宗命翰林學士陸扆、秘書監馮渥覆試黜落，永不許入舉場，楷負愧銜怨。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi examination in the second year of Qianning, public opinion held it improper; Zhaozong ordered Hanlin Academician Lu Yi and Director of the Secretariat Feng Wo to re-examine and fail him, never permitting entry to the examination grounds again—Kai bore shame and harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He passed jinshi in Qianning 2 but was failed on re-exam and banned forever—he nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 至是，全忠弑逆君上，柳璨陷害朝臣，乃與起居郎羅袞、起居舍人盧鼎連署駁議。

translations.literal: At this time Quanzhong had murdered his sovereign; Liu Can framed court officials—he then joined Attendant Luo Gun and Attendant-in-Waiting Lu Ding in a linked memorial of rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: Now, with Quanzhong regicide and Liu Can framing ministers, he joined Luo Gun and Lu Ding in a joint rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 楷目不知書，手僅能執筆，其文羅袞作也。

translations.literal: Kai could barely see writing and could only hold a brush; the text was written by Luo Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Kai could barely read; Luo Gun wrote the memorial.

sentences.zh: 時政出賊臣，哀帝不能制。

translations.literal: Government came from treacherous ministers; Emperor Ai could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: Power lay with traitors; Emperor Ai was helpless.

sentences.zh: 太常卿張廷範改諡曰恭靈莊閔孝皇帝，廟號曰襄宗。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Tingfan changed the posthumous title to Respectful, Numinous, Solemn, Mild, Filial Emperor and the temple name to Xiangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingfan changed the title to Respectful, Numinous, Solemn, Mild, Filial Emperor and temple name Xiangzong.

sentences.zh: 全忠雄猜物鑒，自楷駁諡後，深鄙之，既傳代之後，循、楷父子皆斥逐，不令在朝。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was fierce, suspicious, and keen in judging things; after Kai's rebuttal of the posthumous title he deeply despised him—after the succession, father and son Xun and Kai were both expelled and not permitted at court.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong despised Kai after the rebuttal; once power passed, both Xun and Kai were banished from court.

sentences.zh: 丁未，所司改題昭宗神主，輟朝一日，癸丑，敕成德軍宜改為武順，管內槁城縣曰槁平，信都曰堯都，欒城曰欒氏，阜城曰漢阜，臨城為房子，避全忠祖、父名也。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the responsible office retitled Zhaozong's spirit tablet; court was suspended one day. On guichou, an edict ordered Chengde Army renamed Wushun; within its jurisdiction Gaocheng County became Gaoping, Xindu became Yaodu, Luancheng became Luanshi, Fucheng became Hanfu, Lincheng became Fangzi—to avoid the names of Quanzhong's grandfather and father.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Zhaozong's tablet was retitled and court paused a day. On guichou Chengde became Wushun and several counties were renamed for Quanzhong's ancestors' taboos.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯朔，敕潞州潞城縣改為潞子，黎城曰黎亭。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, yimao, an edict ordered Luzhou's Lucheng County changed to Luzhi and Licheng to Liting.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, first of the eleventh month, Lucheng became Luzhi and Licheng Liting.

sentences.zh: 全忠平荊襄後，遂引軍將攻淮南。

translations.literal: After Quanzhong pacified Jing and Xiang he led troops to attack Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Jing and Xiang, Quanzhong marched on Huainan.

sentences.zh: 行次棗陽，阻雨，比至光州，道險塗潦，人馬饑乏。

translations.literal: Stopping at Zaoyang he was blocked by rain; by the time he reached Guang Prefecture the road was perilous and mired, men and horses hungry and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Delayed by rain at Zaoyang, he reached Guang Prefecture with troops exhausted on bad roads.

sentences.zh: 休止十餘日，乃趨固始。

translations.literal: He halted more than ten days, then pressed toward Gushi.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days' rest he advanced on Gushi.

sentences.zh: 進軍距壽州三十里，壽人閉壁不出，左右言師老不可用。

translations.literal: Advancing to within thirty li of Shou Prefecture, the people of Shou shut their walls and would not come out; those beside him said the army was weary and unusable.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from Shou, the city stayed closed; aides said the army was too worn for battle.

sentences.zh: 是月丙辰，全忠自正陽渡淮而北，至汝陰。

translations.literal: On bingchen of that month Quanzhong crossed the Huai north from Zhengyang and reached Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he crossed the Huai north from Zhengyang to Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 全忠深悔此行無益。

translations.literal: Quanzhong deeply regretted that this campaign had been useless.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong deeply regretted the useless campaign.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至大樑。

translations.literal: On dingmao he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived at Daliang on dingmao.

sentences.zh: 時哀帝以此月十九日親祠圓丘，中外百司禮儀法物已備。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ai was to perform the suburban rite at the Round Mound on the nineteenth of this month; ritual objects of the central and outer offices were ready.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai was to sacrifice at the Round Mound on the nineteenth; all ritual gear was ready.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，宰相已下于南郊壇習儀，而裴迪自大樑回，言全忠怒蔣玄暉、張廷范、柳璨等謀延唐祚，而欲郊天改元。

translations.literal: On wuchen, chancellors and below rehearsed at the southern suburban altar, while Pei Di returned from Daliang reporting that Quanzhong was enraged at Jiang Xuanhui, Zhang Tingfan, Liu Can, and others for plotting to extend Tang's fate and for wishing to sacrifice to Heaven and change the reign era.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen ministers rehearsed at the southern altar while Pei Di returned from Daliang saying Quanzhong raged at Jiang Xuanhui, Zhang Tingfan, and Liu Can for prolonging Tang and changing the era at the suburban rite.

sentences.zh: 玄暉、柳璨大懼。

translations.literal: Xuanhui and Liu Can were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui and Liu Can were terrified.

sentences.zh: 庚午，敕曰：「先定此月十九日親禮南郊，雖定吉辰，改卜亦有故事。

translations.literal: On gengwu, an edict stated: "The southern suburban rite first fixed for the nineteenth of this month—though the auspicious day was set, changing the divination also has precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu an edict said the southern rite fixed for the nineteenth could be rescheduled by precedent.

sentences.zh: 宜改取來年正月上辛。

translations.literal: It should be changed to the first xin day of the first month of next year.
translations.idiomatic: It was moved to the first xin day of next year's first month.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrusted to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The offices were charged.

sentences.zh: 」辛巳，制：「回天再造竭忠守正功臣、諸道兵馬元帥、宣武宣義天平護國等軍節度觀察處置、修宮闕制置、度支解縣池場、亳州太清宮等使、開府儀同三司、守太尉、中書令、河中尹、汴滑鄆等州刺史、上柱國、梁王、食邑一萬五千戶、實封一千五百戶硃全忠可授相國，總百揆，其以宣武、宣義、天平、護國、天雄、武順、忠武、佑國、河陽、義武、昭義、保義、戎昭、武定、泰甯、平盧、匡國、鎮國、武甯、忠義、荊南二十一道為魏國，仍進封魏王，依前充諸道兵馬元帥、太尉、中書令、宣武宣義天平護國等軍節度觀察處置等使，加食邑五千戶，實封八千五百戶，入朝不趨，劍履上殿，贊拜不名，兼備九錫之命，仍擇日備禮冊命。

translations.literal: " On xinsi, an order: "Meritorious subject who turned back Heaven and remade the realm, exhausting loyalty and upholding rectitude; Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits' Armies and Horses; Commissioner of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, Huguo, and other armies; Commissioner for Palace Repair; Commissioner for Revenue and Salt Ponds; Commissioner of Taqing Palace in Bozhou; Acting Three Excellencies; Defender Grand Mentor; Grand Preceptor; Zhongshu Director; Governor of Hezhong; Governors of Bian, Hua, Yun, and other prefectures; Supreme Pillar of State; Prince of Liang; fief of fifteen thousand households with fifteen hundred enfeoffments—Zhu Quanzhong may be appointed Chancellor of State, overseeing all affairs. The twenty-one circuits of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, Huguo, Tianxiong, Wushun, Zhongwu, Youguo, Heyang, Yiwu, Zhaoyi, Baoyi, Rongzhao, Wuding, Taining, Pinglu, Kuangguo, Zhenguo, Wuning, Zhongyi, and Jingnan shall form the State of Wei; he is further advanced to Prince of Wei, continuing as before as commander-in-chief, Grand Preceptor, Zhongshu Director, and commissioner of the armies; fief increased by five thousand households with eight thousand five hundred enfeoffments; need not hasten on entering court; may wear sword and shoes in audience; need not be named in congratulation; also granted the Nine Bestowments; a day shall be chosen for full investiture rites."
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Zhu Quanzhong was made chancellor of state and Prince of Wei over twenty-one circuits, with the Nine Bestowments, sword and shoes at court, and increased fiefs—full rites to follow.

sentences.zh: 又制以楊師厚為襄州兵馬留後，左龍武統軍張慎思為武寧軍兵馬留後。

translations.literal: Another order made Yang Shihou acting military commissioner of Xiangzhou and Left Dragon Martial Commander Zhang Shensi acting commissioner of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shihou was made acting commissioner of Xiangzhou and Zhang Shensi of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 壬午，中書門下奏：「相國魏王總百揆，百司合呈納本司印。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Secretariat memorialized: "The Chancellor of State, Prince of Wei, overseeing all affairs—all offices should submit their office seals.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the Secretariat said all offices should surrender seals to the Prince of Wei as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 其中書門下印，堂候王仁珪呈納，中書公事，權追中書省印行遣。

translations.literal: As to the Secretariat seal, Hall Attendant Wang Rengui shall submit it; Secretariat business shall temporarily use the Secretariat of State seal for dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat seal would be submitted by Wang Rengui; business would run on the Secretariat of State seal.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 甲申，敕河南告成縣改為陽邑，蔡州襄城改為苞孚，同州韓城改為韓原，絳州翼城改為澮川，鄆州鄆城改為萬安，慈州文城改為屈邑，澤州晉城改高都，陽城改為濩澤，安州應城改為應陽，洪州豐城改為吳高。

translations.literal: On jiashen, an edict ordered Henan's Gaocheng County changed to Yangyi; Cai Prefecture's Xiangcheng to Baofu; Tong Prefecture's Hancheng to Hanyuan; Jiang Prefecture's Yicheng to Huichuan; Yun Prefecture's Yuncheng to Wan'an; Ci Prefecture's Wencheng to Quyi; Ze Prefecture's Jincheng to Gaodu; Yangcheng to Huoze; An Prefecture's Yingcheng to Yingyang; Hong Prefecture's Fengcheng to Wugao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen many counties were renamed across several prefectures.

sentences.zh: 全忠令判官司馬鄴讓相國總百揆之命。

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered his aide Sima Ye to decline the appointment as chancellor overseeing all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong had Sima Ye decline the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, yiyou.
translations.idiomatic: First day of the twelfth month, yiyou.

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔蔣玄暉齎手詔赴魏國，不許陳讓錫命。

translations.literal: On wuzi, an edict ordered Jiang Xuanhui to carry the emperor's handwritten edict to the State of Wei, not permitting him to decline the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Jiang Xuanhui was sent to Wei with the investiture edict and forbidden to decline.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，制：正議大夫、門下侍郎，兼戶部尚書、同平章事、太微宮使、弘文館大學士、延資庫使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運等使、上柱國、河東縣開國男、食邑三百戶柳璨可光祿大夫、守司空，兼門下侍郎、同平章事、太微宮使、弘文館大學士、延資庫使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運等使，進封河東縣開國伯，通前食邑七百戶，充魏國冊禮使。

translations.literal: On xinmao, an order: Grand Master of Discussion Liu Can, Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Revenue, Associate Director of the Secretariat, Commissioner of Taiwei Palace, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute, Commissioner of the Extended Treasury, Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport for All Circuits, Supreme Pillar of State, Baron of Hedong with three hundred fief households—may become Grand Master of Splendor, Acting Minister of Works, continuing Vice Director, Associate Director, and all commissions; advanced to Earl of Hedong with seven hundred fief households in all; made Commissioner for Wei Investiture Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Liu Can was promoted to acting Minister of Works, made Earl of Hedong, and named commissioner for Wei investiture.

sentences.zh: 制：「相國魏王曾祖贈太傅茂琳追封魏王，諡宣憲；

translations.literal: Order: "The Chancellor of State, Prince of Wei's great-grandfather, posthumously Grand Tutor Maolin, is posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Wei with posthumous title Xuanxian;
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong's great-grandfather Maolin was posthumously made Prince of Wei as Xuanxian;

sentences.zh: 祖贈太師信追封魏王，諡武元；

translations.literal: grandfather, posthumously Grand Preceptor Xin, posthumously Prince of Wei with posthumous title Wuyuan;
translations.idiomatic: grandfather Xin was posthumously Prince of Wei as Wuyuan;

sentences.zh: 父贈尚書令誠追封魏王，諡文明。

translations.literal: father, posthumously Director of the Secretariat Cheng, posthumously Prince of Wei with posthumous title Wenming."
translations.idiomatic: father Cheng was posthumously Prince of Wei as Wenming.

sentences.zh: 敕右常侍王钜、太常卿張廷範、給事中崔沂、工部尚書李克助、祠部郎中知制誥張茂樞、膳部員外知制誥杜曉、吏部郎中李光嗣、駕部郎中趙光胤、戶部郎中崔協、比部郎中楊煥、左常侍孔拯、右諫議蕭頎、左拾遺裴瑑、右拾遺高濟、職方郎中牛希逸、主客郎中蕭蘧等，隨冊禮使柳璨魏國行事。

translations.literal: Edict: Right Regular Attendant Wang Ju, Director Zhang Tingfan, Attendant-in-Waiting Cui Yi, Minister of Works Li Kezhu, Secretariat Drafting Officer Zhang Maoshu, Drafting Attendant Du Xiao, Ministry Director Li Guangsi, Board Director Zhao Guangyin, Ministry Director Cui Xie, Board Director Yang Huan, Left Regular Attendant Kong Zheng, Right Remonstrator Xiao Yi, Left Reminder Pei Yuan, Right Reminder Gao Ji, Board Director Niu Xiyi, Board Director Xiao Su, and others shall accompany Investiture Commissioner Liu Can in Wei state business.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju, Zhang Tingfan, Cui Yi, and many other officials were ordered to accompany Liu Can for the Wei investiture.

sentences.zh: 先是，北院宣徽使王殷使壽州行營，構蔣玄暉于全忠，全忠怒，急歸大樑。

translations.literal: Earlier, Northern Commissionery Commissioner Wang Yin went to the Shou Prefecture camp and framed Jiang Xuanhui to Quanzhong; Quanzhong was enraged and hurried back to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Yin of the Northern Commissionery framed Jiang Xuanhui at Shou; Quanzhong rushed back to Daliang in rage.

sentences.zh: 上令刑部尚書裴迪齎詔慰勞全忠，全忠忿恨，語極不遜，故行相國百揆之命以悅其心。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Minister of Justice Pei Di with an edict to console Quanzhong; Quanzhong was resentful and his words extremely insubordinate—therefore the chancellor appointment was issued to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Di was sent to console him; Quanzhong answered insubordinately, so the chancellorship was offered to appease him.

sentences.zh: 蔣玄暉自至大樑陳訴，全忠怒猶不解。

translations.literal: From the time Jiang Xuanhui reached Daliang to plead his case, Quanzhong's anger was still not resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xuanhui's pleas at Daliang did not calm Quanzhong's anger.

sentences.zh: 帝憂之。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 甲午，上召三宰相議其事，柳璨曰：「人望歸元帥，陛下揖讓釋負，今其時也。

translations.literal: On jiawu the emperor summoned the three chancellors to discuss the matter; Liu Can said: "Popular expectation returns to the commander-in-chief; Your Majesty yielding and laying down the burden—now is the time."
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the three chancellors met; Liu Can said the people wanted the commander-in-chief and the emperor should yield now.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「運祚去唐久矣，幸為元帥所延。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Fortune departed from Tang long ago; fortunately the commander-in-chief has prolonged us.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Tang's fortune was long gone and only the commander-in-chief had sustained them.

sentences.zh: 今日天下，非予之天下，神器大寶，歸於有德，又何疑焉。

translations.literal: Today's realm is not my realm; the sacred vessel and great treasure belong to the virtuous—what doubt is there?"
translations.idiomatic: The realm and throne belonged to the virtuous—there was no doubt.

sentences.zh: 他人傳予意不盡，卿自往大樑，備言此懷。

translations.literal: Others cannot convey my intent fully—you yourself go to Daliang and explain this mind in full."
translations.idiomatic: Others could not convey his mind—Liu Can must go to Daliang himself.

sentences.zh: 」乃賜璨茶、藥，便令進發。

translations.literal: He then bestowed tea and medicine on Can and ordered him to depart at once.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Can tea and medicine and sent him off immediately.

sentences.zh: 乙未，敕：樞密使蔣玄暉宜削在身官爵，送河南府處斬。

translations.literal: On yiwei, an edict: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Jiang Xuanhui should be stripped of all active ranks and sent to Henan Prefecture for execution.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Jiang Xuanhui was stripped of rank and sent to Henan for execution.

sentences.zh: 豐德庫使應頊、尚食使硃建武送河南府決殺。

translations.literal: Fengde Storehouse Commissioner Ying Yi and Food Commissioner Zhu Jianwu were sent to Henan Prefecture for summary execution.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Yi and Zhu Jianwu were sent to Henan for execution.

sentences.zh: 庚子，敕：樞密使及宣徽南院北院並停。

translations.literal: On gengzi, an edict: the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Southern and Northern Commissioneries of the Palace Secretariat were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Bureau of Military Affairs and both Palace Secretariat commissioneries were abolished.

sentences.zh: 其樞密公事，令王殷權知。

translations.literal: Its military affairs were placed under Wang Yin as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin was made acting commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 其兩院人吏，並勒歸中書。

translations.literal: Personnel of both commissioneries were all compelled to return to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Both commissioneries' staff were sent back to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其諸司諸道人，並不得到宣徽院。

translations.literal: Personnel of every office and every Taoist may not enter the Commissionery courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: No office staff or Taoists could enter the commissionery.

sentences.zh: 凡有公事，並於中書論請。

translations.literal: All public business shall be petitioned at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: All business went through the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其延義、千秋兩門，只差小黃門三人勾當，其官健勒歸本軍。

translations.literal: At the Yanyi and Qianqiu gates only three junior eunuchs were assigned; guards were compelled back to their original armies.
translations.idiomatic: Only three junior eunuchs remained at two gates; guards returned to their armies.

sentences.zh: 敕：「魏王堅辭寵命，過示捴謙。

translations.literal: Edict: "The Prince of Wei firmly declines the favor of appointment, overly displaying cumulative humility."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei declined the appointment with excessive humility.

sentences.zh: 朕以國史所書元帥之任，並以天下為名，爰自近年，改為諸道，既非舊制，須在正名。

translations.literal: We note that in the national histories the commander-in-chief's charge is always named for all under Heaven; only in recent years was it changed to "all circuits"—this is not the old system and the correct name must be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Histories named the post for all under Heaven; the recent "all circuits" title must be corrected.

sentences.zh: 宜追制改為天下兵馬元帥，余准詔旨處分。

translations.literal: The prior order should be changed to Commander-in-Chief of Armies and Horses of All under Heaven; the rest follows the edict.
translations.idiomatic: It was changed to commander-in-chief of armies and horses of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」辛丑，敕：「漢宣帝中興，五日一聽朝，歷代通規，永為常式。

translations.literal: " On xinchou, an edict: "When Emperor Xuan of Han revived the dynasty, he held court every five days—a rule transmitted through the ages, forever the constant pattern."
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou an edict cited Han Xuandi holding court every five days as the eternal pattern.

sentences.zh: 近代不循舊儀，輒隳制度，既奸邪之得計，致臨視之失常，須守舊規，以循定制。

translations.literal: Recent ages have not followed the old ritual but have destroyed the system, letting treachery succeed and making imperial audiences abnormal—the old rules must be kept to follow the fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Recent neglect of the rule let traitors win and audiences go wrong—the old rule must be restored.

sentences.zh: 宜每月只許一、五、九日開延英，計九度。

translations.literal: Each month only the first, fifth, and ninth days should open Yanying Hall—nine sessions in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yanying was to open only on the 1st, 5th, and 9th of each month—nine times total.

sentences.zh: 其入閣日，仍于延英日一度指揮；

translations.literal: On days of entering the Hall, one session of command shall still be held on a Yanying day;
translations.idiomatic: Entering-the-Hall days would still hold one Yanying session;

sentences.zh: 如有大段公事，中書門下具榜子奏請開延英，不計日數。

translations.literal: if there is major public business, the Secretariat shall memorialize with a placard requesting Yanying opened, without counting days.
translations.idiomatic: major business could open Yanying by Secretariat memorial regardless of date.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrusted to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The offices were charged.

sentences.zh: 」又敕：「宮嬪女職，本備內任，近年已來，稍失儀制。

translations.literal: " Another edict: "Palace women's offices were originally for inner service; in recent years ritual has gradually been lost."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said palace women's offices had drifted from proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 宮人出內宣命，寀禦參隨視朝，乃失舊規，須為永制。

translations.literal: Palace women issuing edicts from within and maids attending morning audience violate old rules and must be permanently forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women issuing inner edicts and attending court violated old rules and was permanently forbidden.

sentences.zh: 今後每遇延英坐朝日，只令小黃門祗候引從，宮人不得擅出內門，庶循典儀，免至紛雜。

translations.literal: Henceforth on each Yanying audience day only junior eunuchs shall attend and lead; palace women may not leave the inner gate without authority, so that canonical ritual may be followed and confusion avoided."
translations.idiomatic: On Yanying days only junior eunuchs might attend; palace women could not leave the inner gate without authority.

sentences.zh: 」壬寅，戎昭軍奏收復金州，兵火之後，井邑殘破，請移理所於均州，從之。
