translations.literal: On renchen, Rongzhao Army reported recovery of Jin Prefecture; after fire of war the towns were ruined and they requested moving the seat of government to Jun Prefecture—approved.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Rongzhao Army recovered Jin; the seat was moved to Jun Prefecture after war ruined the towns.

sentences.zh: 仍改為武定軍。

translations.literal: It was still renamed Wuding Army.
translations.idiomatic: The army was renamed Wuding.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，汴州別駕蔣仲伸決殺，玄暉季父也。

translations.literal: On yisi, Bian Prefecture Vice Governor Jiang Zhongshen was executed—Xuanhui's uncle.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Jiang Zhongshen, Xuanhui's uncle, was executed at Bian.

sentences.zh: 又敕：「蔣玄暉身居密近，擅弄威權，鬻爵賣官，聚財營第，而苞藏悖逆，稔浸奸邪。

translations.literal: Another edict: "Jiang Xuanhui held a post close to the secret, wielding power on his own, selling offices and amassing wealth to build mansions, while harboring rebellion and steeped in treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict condemned Xuanhui for selling offices, hoarding wealth, and treason.

sentences.zh: 雖都市已處於極刑，而屈法尚慊於眾怒，更示焚棄之典，以懲顯負之蹤。

translations.literal: Though the market execution was already the extreme penalty, bending the law still falls short of public wrath; the rite of burning and abandoning the corpse should further be shown to punish manifest guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Though he was executed, the law still seemed too lenient—his corpse should be burned publicly.

sentences.zh: 宜追削為凶逆百姓，仍委河南府揭屍於都門外，聚眾焚燒。

translations.literal: He should be posthumously demoted to treacherous commoner; Henan Prefecture is charged to expose the corpse outside the capital gate, gather the crowd, and burn it."
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted posthumously to treacherous commoner; Henan would expose and burn his corpse at the gate.

sentences.zh: 」玄暉死後，王殷、趙殷衡等又譖于全忠云：「內人相傳，玄暉私侍積善宮，與柳璨、張廷範為盟誓之交，求興唐祚。

translations.literal: After Xuanhui's death Wang Yin, Zhao Yinheng, and others again slandered him to Quanzhong, saying: "Within the palace it is rumored that Xuanhui privately attended Jishan Palace, with Liu Can and Zhang Tingfan as sworn friends, seeking to revive Tang's fortune."
translations.idiomatic: After his death Wang Yin and Zhao Yinheng told Quanzhong Xuanhui had sworn with Liu Can and Zhang Tingfan to restore Tang.

sentences.zh: 」戊申，全忠令知樞密王殷害皇太后何氏于積善宮，又殺宮人阿秋、阿虔，言通導蔣玄暉。

translations.literal: On wushen, Quanzhong ordered Acting Commissioner Wang Yin to kill Empress Dowager He at Jishan Palace, and also killed palace women Aqiu and Aqian, saying they had guided Jiang Xuanhui.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Wang Yin killed Empress Dowager He at Jishan Palace and two palace women as Xuanhui's accomplices.

sentences.zh: 己酉，敕以太后喪，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: On jiyou, an edict suspended court for three days for the empress dowager's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou court was suspended three days for the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 百官奉慰訖。

translations.literal: The hundred officials finished offering condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Officials finished condolences.

sentences.zh: 又敕曰：「皇太后位承坤德，有愧母儀。

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "The empress dowager bore the earth's virtue yet lacked proper motherly conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said the empress dowager had failed as mother.

sentences.zh: 近者凶逆誅夷，宮闈詞連醜狀，尋自崩變，以謝萬方。

translations.literal: Recently when villains were executed, the inner palace was implicated in shameful matters; she then collapsed of herself to answer all quarters."
translations.idiomatic: After villains were killed, palace scandal implicated her; she died to answer the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕以幼沖，君臨區宇，雖情深號慕，而法難徇私，勉循秦、漢之規，須示追降之典。

translations.literal: We, young upon taking the realm, though deep in grief cannot indulge private feeling and with difficulty follow Qin and Han rules—demotion must be shown."
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor could not indulge grief and followed Qin-Han precedent to demote her.

sentences.zh: 其遣黃門收所上皇太后寶冊，追廢為庶人，宜差官告郊廟。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate officials are sent to take back the empress dowager's submitted seals; she is posthumously deposed to commoner; officers shall announce at the suburban altars."
translations.idiomatic: Her seals were recalled, she was deposed to commoner, and altars were notified.

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，敕：「朕以謬荷丕圖，禮合親謁郊廟，先定來年正月上辛用事。

translations.literal: " On gengxu, an edict: "We wrongly bear the great design and by ritual should personally visit the suburban altars; the first xin day of next year was first fixed for the rite."
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu an edict said the suburban rite set for next year's first xin day followed ritual obligation.

sentences.zh: 今以宮圍內亂，播於醜聲，難以慚恧之容，入於祖宗之廟。

translations.literal: Now with disorder within the palace spreading in shameful report, it is hard to enter the ancestors' temple with a face of shame."
translations.idiomatic: Palace scandal made a shamefaced visit to the ancestors' temple impossible.

sentences.zh: 其明年上辛親謁郊廟宜停。

translations.literal: The personal suburban visit on next year's first xin day should be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Next year's suburban visit was canceled.

sentences.zh: 」壬子，敕積善宮安福殿宜廢。

translations.literal: On renzi, an edict ordered Anfu Hall of Jishan Palace abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Anfu Hall at Jishan Palace was abolished.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，敕光祿大夫、守司空、門下侍郎、平章事、太微宮使、弘文館大學士、延資庫使、諸道鹽鐵轉運使柳璨責授朝議郎，守登州刺史。

translations.literal: On guichou, an edict demoted Grand Master of Splendor, Acting Minister of Works, Vice Director Liu Can to Grand Master of Discussion, Acting Governor of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Liu Can was demoted from acting Minister of Works to Governor of Deng.

sentences.zh: 又敕：「太常卿張廷范、太常少卿裴磵溫鑾、祠部郎中知制誥張茂樞等，蔣玄暉在樞密之時，與柳璨、張廷範共為朋扇，日相往來，假其遊宴之名，別貯傾危之計。

translations.literal: Another edict: "Director Zhang Tingfan, Vice Director Pei Jian, Wen Luan, Drafting Officer Zhang Maoshu, and others—while Jiang Xuanhui was at the Bureau of Military Affairs—formed a faction with Liu Can and Zhang Tingfan, meeting daily, using feasts as pretext while storing designs of peril."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said Zhang Tingfan, Pei Jian, Wen Luan, and Zhang Maoshu had conspired with Liu Can and Xuanhui under cover of feasts.

sentences.zh: 苟安重位，酷陷朝臣，既此陰謀，難寬大辟。

translations.literal: Clinging to high rank, they cruelly framed court officials; such hidden plotting cannot escape capital punishment."
translations.idiomatic: They clung to rank and framed ministers—capital punishment was warranted.

sentences.zh: 柳璨已從別敕處分，廷範可責授萊州司戶。

translations.literal: Liu Can was already handled by separate edict; Tingfan is demoted to Registrar of Laizhou."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can was handled separately; Tingfan became registrar of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 裴磵等常同聚會，固共苞藏，磵可青州北海尉，鑾臨淄尉，茂樞博昌尉，並員外置。

translations.literal: Pei Jian and others often met together and clearly harbored conspiracy—Jian to Assistant Magistrate of Beihai in Qing, Luan of Linzi, Maoshu of Bochang, all supernumerary appointments."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jian went to Beihai, Wen Luan to Linzi, Zhang Maoshu to Bochang—all supernumerary posts.

sentences.zh: 」甲寅，敕：「責授登州刺史柳璨，素矜憸巧，每務回邪。

translations.literal: On jiayin, an edict: "Demoted Governor of Deng Liu Can, always proud of crafty cunning, ever bent on perversity.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Liu Can was condemned for cunning and perversity.

sentences.zh: 幸以庸才，驟居重位，曾無顯效，孤負明恩。

translations.literal: By vulgar talent he suddenly held high rank, never showing clear achievement, betraying bright favor."
translations.idiomatic: A mediocrity in high office, he had shown no merit and betrayed the throne.

sentences.zh: 詭譎多端，苞藏莫測，但結連於兇險，獨陷害于賢良。

translations.literal: Deceitful in many ways, his hiding could not be fathomed, but he joined with the dangerous and alone harmed the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: His deceit joined the dangerous and harmed the worthy alone.

sentences.zh: 罪既貫盈，理須竄殛。

translations.literal: Guilt filled to overflowing; reason demands exile and death."
translations.idiomatic: Guilt was full; exile and death were required.

sentences.zh: 可貶密州司戶，再貶長流崖州百姓，委御史台賜自盡。

translations.literal: He may be demoted to Registrar of Mizhou, again demoted to commoner exiled to Yazhou, entrusted to the Censorate for ordered suicide."
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Mizhou registrar, then exiled to Yazhou as commoner and ordered to kill himself by the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 」是日斬於上東門外。

translations.literal: That day he was beheaded outside the Upper East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded that day outside the Upper East Gate.

sentences.zh: 又敕：「張廷範性唯庸妄，志在回邪，不能保慎寵榮，而乃苞藏兇險。

translations.literal: Another edict: "Zhang Tingfan's nature is only vulgar presumption; his intent is perversity; he could not preserve cautious favor yet harbored dangerous treachery."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said Zhang Tingfan was vulgar, perverse, and treacherous.

sentences.zh: 密交柳璨，深結玄暉，晝議宵行，欺天負地。

translations.literal: Secretly befriending Liu Can, deeply bonding with Xuanhui, plotting by day and acting by night, deceiving Heaven and betraying earth."
translations.idiomatic: He secretly joined Liu Can and Xuanhui, plotting day and night.

sentences.zh: 神祇共怒，罪狀難原。

translations.literal: Spirits and gods share anger; guilt cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Gods and men alike condemned him—no pardon.

sentences.zh: 宜除名，委河南府於都市集眾，以五車分裂。

translations.literal: His name should be erased; Henan Prefecture shall gather the crowd in the market and split him with five carts."
translations.idiomatic: His name was erased; Henan would tear him apart with five carts in the market.

sentences.zh: 溫鑾、裴磵、張茂樞並除名，委于御史台所在賜自盡。

translations.literal: Wen Luan, Pei Jian, and Zhang Maoshu shall all have names erased and be entrusted to the Censorate wherever located for ordered suicide."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Luan, Pei Jian, and Zhang Maoshu were erased and ordered to kill themselves wherever found.

sentences.zh: 柳璨弟瑀、瑊，送河南府決殺。

translations.literal: Liu Can's younger brothers Yu and Jian were sent to Henan Prefecture for summary execution."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can's brothers Yu and Jian were executed at Henan.

sentences.zh: 」天祐三年三年春正月乙卯朔，全忠以四鎮之師七萬，會河北諸軍，屯于深州樂城。

translations.literal: In spring, first month, yimao, first day of Tianyou year three—Quanzhong with seventy thousand troops of four circuits joined Hebei armies and encamped at Lecheng in Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, yimao, Tianyou 3: Quanzhong camped at Lecheng with seventy thousand men from four circuits and Hebei allies.

sentences.zh: 戊午，敕右拾遺柳瑗貶洺州雞澤尉，璨疏屬也。

translations.literal: On wuwu, an edict demoted Right Reminder Liu Yuan to Assistant Magistrate of Jize in Ming Prefecture—a distant kinsman of Can.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Liu Yuan, Liu Can's kinsman, was demoted to Jize magistrate.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，全忠自汴河赴魏州。

translations.literal: On yichou, Quanzhong went from the Bian River to Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Quanzhong went from the Bian River to Wei.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，制：「定亂安國功臣、鎮海鎮東軍節度、浙江東西道觀察處置等使、淮南東面行營招討營田安撫兩浙鹽鐵制置發運等使、開府儀同三司、守侍中、兼中書令、杭越兩州刺史、上柱國、吳王、食邑九千戶、實封五百戶錢鏐，總臨兩鎮，制撫三吳。

translations.literal: On bingyin, an order: "Meritorious subject who settled disorder and pacified the state; Commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong; Commissioner of Zhejiang East and West; Commissioner for Huainan East Campaign, Agriculture, and Two-Zhe Salt; Acting Three Excellencies; Defender Palace Attendant; concurrent Zhongshu Director; Governors of Hang and Yue; Supreme Pillar; Prince of Wu; fief nine thousand households with five hundred enfeoffments—Qian Liu, overseeing both circuits and controlling the Three Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin an order named Qian Liu Prince of Wu, lord of the Two Zhe circuits and the Three Wu.

sentences.zh: 道途阻艱，未行冊命，宜令所司擇日備禮。

translations.literal: Because roads were difficult the investiture had not been performed; the responsible offices should choose a day and prepare the full rites.
translations.idiomatic: Dangerous roads delayed the ceremony—the ministries were to set a date for the rites.

sentences.zh: 」己巳夜，魏博節度使羅紹威殺其衙內親軍八千人。

translations.literal: " On the night of jisi, Weibo Commissioner Luo Shaowei killed eight thousand of his inner guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: That night of jisi Luo Shaowei killed eight thousand inner guards at Weibo.

sentences.zh: 戊午，全忠自內黃入魏州。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Quanzhong entered Wei Prefecture from Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Quanzhong entered Wei from Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 是月，魏博衙外兵五萬自曆亭還，分據紹威貝、博等州，汴軍攻圍之。

translations.literal: That month fifty thousand Weibo outer troops returned from Liting and seized Bei, Bo, and other prefectures held by Shaowei; Bian troops besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: That month fifty thousand Weibo troops seized Shaowei's prefectures; Bian forces besieged them.

sentences.zh: 壬申，敕：「相國總百揆魏王頃辭冊命，宜令所司再行冊禮。

translations.literal: On renshen, an edict: "The Chancellor overseeing all affairs, Prince of Wei, recently declined investiture; the responsible office should again perform investiture rites."
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Wei investiture was ordered again after Quanzhong's refusal.

sentences.zh: 」辛巳，國子監奉：「奉去年十一月五日敕文，應國學每年與諸道等一例解送兩人，今監生郭應圖等六十人連狀論訴。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the Directorate of Education reported: "According to the edict of the fifth day of the eleventh month last year, the Directorate each year should send two candidates like other circuits; now sixty students including Guo Yingtu have jointly petitioned."
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the Directorate reported sixty students petitioned over the annual quota of two candidates.

sentences.zh: 」敕旨：「取士之科，明經極重，每年人數，已有舊規，去夏條疏，蓋防渝濫。

translations.literal: Edict: "The examination for scholars, the Mingjing degree is extremely weighty; annual numbers have fixed rules; last summer's provisions guarded against laxity."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said Mingjing quotas were fixed and last year's rules curbed laxity.

sentences.zh: 今國子監、河南府俱有論奏，所試明經，宜令准常年例解送禮部，放人多少，酌量施行。

translations.literal: Now both the Directorate and Henan have memorialized; the Mingjing candidates tested should be sent to the Ministry of Rites by the usual annual quota, the number admitted to be weighed and implemented."
translations.idiomatic: Mingjing candidates would go to the Ministry of Rites under the usual quota.

sentences.zh: 但不徇囑求，無致僥倖。

translations.literal: But favor-seeking and lucky chance must not be indulged."
translations.idiomatic: Favoritism and luck-seeking were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrusted to the responsible offices."
translations.idiomatic: The offices were charged.
The edict closed.

sentences.zh: 二月甲申朔，魏博節度使羅紹威宜許於本鎮置三代私廟。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month, jiashen, Weibo Commissioner Luo Shaowei was permitted to establish a private temple for three generations in his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Luo Shaowei was allowed a three-generation private temple in Weibo.

sentences.zh: 癸卯。

translations.literal: On guimao.
translations.idiomatic: Guimao day.

sentences.zh: 敕今年禮部所放進士，據依去年人數外，更放兩人。

translations.literal: An edict: this year's jinshi admitted by the Ministry of Rites, beyond last year's quota, shall admit two more.
translations.idiomatic: Two more jinshi were admitted beyond last year's quota.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, jiayin.
translations.idiomatic: First day of the third month, jiayin.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，敕：「河中、昭義管內，俱有慈州，地裏相去不遠，稱謂時聞錯誤，其昭義管內慈州宜改為惠州。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, an edict: "Within the jurisdictions of Hezhong and Zhaoyi both have a Ci Prefecture; the territories are not far apart and names are often confused in speech—the Ci Prefecture within Zhaoyi should be renamed Hui Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Zhaoyi's Ci Prefecture was renamed Hui to avoid confusion with Hezhong's Ci.

sentences.zh: 」壬戌，全忠奏河中判官劉崇子匡圖，今年進士登第，遽列高科，恐涉群議，請禮部落下。

translations.literal: On renxu, Quanzhong memorialized that Hezhong aide Liu Chong's son Kuangtu passed the jinshi this year and was suddenly placed high—fearing public criticism, he requested the Ministry of Rites strike his name.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Quanzhong asked the Ministry of Rites to strike Kuangtu, son of Liu Chong, from the jinshi list.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，制元帥梁王可兼領諸道鹽鐵轉運等使，判度支戶部事，充三司都制置使。

translations.literal: On wuyin, an order made Commander-in-Chief Prince of Liang also oversee Salt and Iron Transport for All Circuits, judge Revenue and Household affairs, and serve as Commissioner-in-Chief of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Prince of Liang took salt, iron, transport, revenue, and the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，敕貶西都留守判官、左諫議大夫鄭賨崖州司戶，尋賜死。

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict demoted Western Capital Acting Governor, Left Remonstrator Zheng Yin to Registrar of Yazhou—soon ordered to death.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Zheng Yin was demoted to Yazhou and soon ordered killed.

sentences.zh: 四月甲申朔，日有蝕之，在胃十二度。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, jiashen, there was an eclipse in the Stomach lodge, twelve degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, first of the fourth month, an eclipse hit Stomach at twelve degrees.

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏博羅紹威奏：「臣當管博州聊城縣、武陽莘縣武水博平高堂等五縣，皆于黃河東岸，其鄉村百姓渡河輸稅不便，與天平軍管界接連，請割屬鄆。

translations.literal: On wushen, Weibo's Luo Shaowei memorialized: "Within my jurisdiction the five counties of Liaocheng in Bo, Wushui in Wuyang, and Bo Ping, Gaotang, etc., all lie east of the Yellow River; village people find crossing to pay tax inconvenient; they adjoin Yun's Tianping circuit—request they be ceded to Yun."
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Luo Shaowei asked five Yellow River counties be ceded to Yun's Tianping.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 五月癸酉朔，追贈故荊南節度使成汭、鄂岳節度使杜洪官爵，仍於本州立祠廟，從全忠奏也。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, guiyou, posthumous restoration of rank was granted to the late Jingnan Commissioner Cheng Run and E-Yue Commissioner Du Hong, with temples in their circuits—following Quanzhong's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Cheng Run and Du Hong were posthumously restored and given temples at Quanzhong's request.

sentences.zh: 丙申，敕：「天祐二年九月二十日于金州置戎昭軍，割均、房二州為屬郡。

translations.literal: On bingchen, an edict: "On the twentieth day of the ninth month of Tianyou year two, Rongzhao Army was established at Jin Prefecture, cutting Jun and Fang as subordinate prefectures."
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen an edict recalled creating Rongzhao Army at Jin from Jun and Fang in Tianyou 2.

sentences.zh: 比因馮行襲葉贊元勳，克宣丕績，用獎濟師之效，遂行割地之權。

translations.literal: Recently because Feng Xingxi assisted the founding merit and proclaimed great achievement, to reward the army's effect the power to cut territory was exercised."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingxi's merit had prompted the territorial cut as reward.

sentences.zh: 今命帥得人，疇庸有秩，其戎昭軍額宜停，其均、房二州卻還山南東道收管。

translations.literal: Now the commandery has a worthy commander and merit has proper rank—the Rongzhao Army designation should be abolished and Jun and Fang returned to Shannan East Circuit."
translations.idiomatic: Rongzhao Army was abolished and Jun and Fang returned to Shannan East.
The edict ended.

sentences.zh: 六月癸未朔，甲申，敕：「襄州近因趙匡凝作帥，請別立忠義軍額，既非往制，固是從權。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, guiwei; on jiashen, an edict: "Xiang Prefecture recently, because Zhao Kuangning became commander, requested a separate Zhongyi Army designation—this was not the old system but a temporary measure."
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen an edict said Zhongyi Army at Xiang, a temporary measure under Zhao Kuangning, should end.

sentences.zh: 忠義軍額宜停廢，依舊為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: The Zhongyi Army designation should be abolished and it should again be Shannan East Circuit Commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi was abolished; Shannan East was restored.

sentences.zh: 」己亥，權右唐州事衛審符奏，州郭凋殘，又不居要路，請移理所于泌陽縣，從之。

translations.literal: On jihai, Acting Tang Prefecture affairs Wei Shenfu memorialized that the prefectural seat was ruined and not on a key route; the seat should move to Biyang County—approved.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Tang's seat moved to Biyang after Shenfu reported ruin and poor location.

sentences.zh: 制以京兆尹、佑國軍節度使韓建為青州節度使，代王重師；

translations.literal: An order made Capital Governor and Youguo Commissioner Han Jian Commissioner of Qing Prefecture, replacing Wang Chongshi;
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian replaced Wang Chongshi as Qing commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以重師代建為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Chongshi replaced Jian as Capital Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Chongshi became capital governor.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，敕：「文武百僚每月一度入閣於貞觀殿。

translations.literal: On renyin, an edict: "Civil and military officials of the hundred offices shall once a month enter the Hall at Zhenguan Hall."
translations.idiomatic: On renyin officials were to enter the Hall monthly at Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 貞觀大殿，朝廷正衙，遇正至之辰，受群臣朝賀。

translations.literal: The great Zhenguan Hall is the court's main hall; on solstice days it receives officials' congratulation."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan was the main hall for solstice congratulations.

sentences.zh: 比來視朔，未正規儀，今後於崇勳殿入閣。

translations.literal: Recently viewing the new moon, ritual was not correct; henceforth entering the Hall shall be at Chongxun Hall."
translations.idiomatic: New-moon audiences had been irregular; entering the Hall would move to Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 付所司。

translations.literal: Entrusted to the responsible offices."
translations.idiomatic: The offices were charged.

sentences.zh: 」左拾遺、充史館修撰裴瑑以堂叔母危疾在濟源，無兄弟侍疾，乞假寧省，從之。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Pei Yuan, serving as History Office compiler, because his uncle's wife had grave illness at Jiyuan and no brother could attend, requested leave to nurse—approved.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yuan was granted leave to nurse his uncle's wife at Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 七月壬子朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, renzi.
translations.idiomatic: First day of the seventh month, renzi.

sentences.zh: 己未，全忠始自魏州歸大樑，魏博六州平定。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Quanzhong at last returned from Wei Prefecture to Daliang; the six Weibo prefectures were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Quanzhong returned to Daliang after pacifying six Weibo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 檢校工部尚書、守宗正卿、嗣邠王震停見任，落下襲封，以請告於外也。

translations.literal: Acting Minister of Works, Acting Director of the Imperial Clan, Heir of Bin Wang Zhen was suspended from current office and stripped of inherited enfeoffment for requesting leave outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, heir of Bin, lost office and enfeoffment for unauthorized leave.

sentences.zh: 辛未，皇妹永明公主薨，罷朝三日。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the emperor's younger sister Princess Yongming died; court was suspended three days.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Princess Yongming died; court paused three days.

sentences.zh: 八月甲辰，全忠復自汴州北渡河，攻滄州。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Quanzhong again crossed the Yellow River north from Bian Prefecture to attack Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Quanzhong crossed north from Bian to attack Cang.

sentences.zh: 乙未，魏博奏割貝州永濟、廣宗，相州臨河、內黃、洹水、斥丘等六縣隸魏州，從之。

translations.literal: On yiyi, Weibo memorialized ceding six counties—Yongji and Guangzong of Bei, Linhe, Neihuang, Huanshui, and Chiqu of Xiang—to Wei Prefecture—approved.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyi six counties were ceded from Bei and Xiang to Wei.

sentences.zh: 九月辛亥朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, xinhai.
translations.idiomatic: First day of the ninth month, xinhai.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，全忠在軍至滄州，軍于長蘆。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Quanzhong in camp reached Cang Prefecture and encamped at Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Quanzhong reached Cang and camped at Changlu.

sentences.zh: 是月積陰霖雨不止，差官宗禜都門。

translations.literal: That month prolonged overcast rain did not stop; officers were sent to sacrifice at the suburban altars and capital gates.
translations.idiomatic: Endless rain that month prompted sacrifices at altars and gates.

sentences.zh: 十月乙未，兩浙錢鏐請於本鎮立三代私廟，從之。

translations.literal: On yiyi of the tenth month, Qian Liu of Two Zhe requested a three-generation private temple in his circuit—approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Qian Liu was allowed a three-generation private temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚戌朔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, gengxu.
translations.idiomatic: First day of the eleventh month, gengxu.

sentences.zh: 丙子，廢牛羊司。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the Cattle and Sheep Office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the Cattle and Sheep Office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 禦廚肉河南府供進，所有進到牛羊，便付河南府收管。

translations.literal: Imperial kitchen meat was supplied by Henan Prefecture; all cattle and sheep delivered were entrusted to Henan for custody.
translations.idiomatic: Kitchen livestock went to Henan Prefecture for custody.

sentences.zh: 十二月己卯朔，淮南偽署宣歙觀察使、檢校司徒王茂章可金紫光祿大夫、檢校太保，從錢鏐奏也。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, jimao, the Huainan pretender's Acting Xuan-She Commissioner, Acting Minister of Works Wang Maozhang was made Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Robe, Acting Grand Mentor—following Qian Liu's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Wang Maozhang of Huainan was promoted at Qian Liu's request.

sentences.zh: 茂章背楊渥，以宣州降錢鏐故也。

translations.literal: Maozhang had turned from Yang Wo and surrendered Xuan Prefecture to Qian Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang had left Yang Wo and surrendered Xuan to Qian Liu.

sentences.zh: 己丑，全忠奏文武兩班一、五、九朝日，元帥府排比廊飧。

translations.literal: On jichou, Quanzhong memorialized that on civil and military audiences on the 1st, 5th, and 9th the commander's office should arrange corridor meals.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Quanzhong asked corridor meals arranged on audience days.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「百官入朝，兩廊賜食，遷都之後，有司官闕供。

translations.literal: Edict: "When officials enter court, food is bestowed in both corridors; after the move of the capital the supplying offices were short."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said corridor food at court had lapsed after the capital move.

sentences.zh: 元帥梁王欲整大綱，復行故事，俾其班列，益認優隆，宜賜詔獎飾。

translations.literal: Commander Prince of Liang wishes to restore great order and old practice so that the ranks may know enhanced favor—an edict of reward should be granted."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang would restore corridor meals—he was to receive praise.

sentences.zh: 」甲辰，河陽節度副使孫乘貶崖州司戶，尋賜自盡。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Heyang Deputy Commissioner Sun Cheng was demoted to Registrar of Yazhou—soon ordered to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Sun Cheng was demoted to Yazhou and ordered to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 閏十二月己酉朔，福建百姓僧道詣闕，請為節度使王審知立德政碑，從之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the intercalary twelfth month, jiyou, Fujian commoners and monks came to court requesting a monument to Commissioner Wang Shenzhi's virtuous government—approved.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Fujian petitioners won a monument to Wang Shenzhi.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，華州鎮國節度觀察處置等使額及興德府名，並宜停廢，復為華州刺史，充本州防禦使，仍隸同州為支郡，所管華、商兩州諸縣，先升次赤，次畿並罷，宜依舊名。

translations.literal: On yichou, the Zhenguo Army designation and Xingde Prefecture name were all to be abolished, restored to Governor of Hua Prefecture with defense of the prefecture, subordinate to Tong as a branch prefecture; Hua and Shang counties formerly raised to secondary capital and capital-region status were abolished and old names restored.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Zhenguo and Xingde were abolished; Hua reverted to a defense prefecture under Tong.

sentences.zh: 西都佑國軍作鎮已來，未有屬郡，其金州、商州宜隸為屬郡。

translations.literal: Since the Western Capital Youguo Army became a commandery it had no subordinates; Jin and Shang prefectures should be made subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Shang were made subordinate to the western capital commandery.

sentences.zh: 京兆府奉先縣本屬馮翊，櫟陽連接下邽，奉先縣宜卻隸同州，櫟陽宜隸華州。

translations.literal: Fengyi's Fengxian County originally belonged to Tong; Liyang adjoined Xia—Fengxian should return to Tong and Liyang to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian returned to Tong; Liyang went to Hua.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，奪西川節度使王建在身官爵。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the active offices and ranks of Xichuan Commissioner Wang Jian were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Wang Jian of Xichuan was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，李克用與幽州之眾同攻潞州，全忠守將丁會以澤、潞降太原，克用以其子嗣昭為留後。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Li Keyong with Youzhou forces jointly attacked Luzhou; Quanzhong's defender Ding Hui surrendered Ze and Lu to Taiyuan; Keyong made his son Jiazhao acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Li Keyong attacked Luzhou; Ding Hui surrendered Ze and Lu; Jiazhao became acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，全忠燒長蘆營旋軍，聞潞州陷故也。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Quanzhong burned the Changlu camp and turned the army—because Luzhou had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Quanzhong burned Changlu and withdrew after Luzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，貶興唐府少尹孫秘長流愛州，尋賜死，孫乘弟也。

translations.literal: On yihai, Acting Governor of Xingde Prefecture Sun Mi was exiled to Aizhou—soon ordered to death; he was Sun Cheng's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Sun Mi, Sun Cheng's brother, was exiled to Aizhou and killed.

sentences.zh: 天祐四年四年春正月戊寅朔。

translations.literal: In spring, first month, wuyin, first day of Tianyou year four.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, wuyin, first day of Tianyou 4.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，全忠自長蘆至大樑，天子遣御史大夫薛貽矩齎詔慰勞。

translations.literal: On renyin, Quanzhong came from Changlu to Daliang; the Son of Heaven sent Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju with an edict to console him.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Quanzhong reached Daliang; Xue Yiju was sent to console him.

sentences.zh: 全忠自弑昭宗之後，岐、蜀、太原，連兵牽制，關西日削。

translations.literal: After Quanzhong murdered Zhaozong, Qi, Shu, and Taiyuan tied him down in continuous warfare and the Guanxi region daily shrank.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhaozong's murder, Qi, Shu, and Taiyuan kept Quanzhong tied down and Guanxi shrank daily.

sentences.zh: 幸羅紹威殺牙軍，全獲魏博六州。

translations.literal: Fortunately Luo Shaowei killed the牙 army and fully gained the six Weibo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei's slaughter of the牙 army gave Quanzhong all six Weibo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 將行篡代，欲威臨河朔，乃再興師臨幽、滄，冀仁恭父子乞盟，則與之相結，以固王鎔、紹威之心。

translations.literal: About to carry out usurpation, wishing to overawe Hebei, he again raised armies against You and Cang, hoping the father and son Ren Gong would beg alliance and bind Wang Rong and Shaowei to him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on You and Cang to intimidate Hebei and bind Ren Gong, Wang Rong, and Shaowei before usurping.

sentences.zh: 而自秋迄冬，攻滄州無功，及聞丁會失守，燒營遽還。

translations.literal: From autumn through winter the attack on Cang achieved nothing; hearing Ding Hui had lost his position, he burned camp and hurried back.
translations.idiomatic: The Cang campaign failed; when Ding Hui fell he burned camp and rushed back.

sentences.zh: 路由魏州，羅紹威知失勢，恐兵襲己，深贊篡奪之謀，他日如王受禪，必罄六州軍賦以助大禮，全忠深感之。

translations.literal: Passing through Wei Prefecture, Luo Shaowei knew he had lost power and feared troops would strike him; he deeply praised the usurpation plot, pledging that when Wang received the Mandate he would exhaust the six prefectures' military levies to aid the great rite—Quanzhong was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei, Shaowei, fearing attack, backed the usurpation and pledged six prefectures' levies for the enthronement—Quanzhong was moved.

sentences.zh: 至大樑，會薛貽矩來，乃以臣禮見全忠。

translations.literal: Reaching Daliang, when Xue Yiju came, he met Quanzhong with subject ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At Daliang Xue Yiju met Quanzhong with subject ritual.

sentences.zh: 貽矩承間密陳禪代之謀，全忠心德之。

translations.literal: Yiju in private secretly stated the abdication plot; Quanzhong was pleased in heart and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yiju privately proposed abdication; Quanzhong was pleased.

sentences.zh: 貽矩還奏曰：「元帥有受代意，陛下深體時事，去茲重負。

translations.literal: Yiju returned and reported: "The commander-in-chief has intent to receive succession; Your Majesty deeply embodies the times and may lay down this heavy burden."
translations.idiomatic: Yiju reported the commander-in-chief would accept succession and the emperor should lay down his burden.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此吾素懷也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "This has long been my mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said that was his long-held wish.

sentences.zh: 」乃降詔元帥以二月行傳禪之禮，全忠偽辭。

translations.literal: " An edict was then sent down that the commander-in-chief should perform the succession rite in the second month; Quanzhong falsely declined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict set abdication for the second month; Quanzhong pretended to decline.

sentences.zh: 二月壬子，詔文武百官以今月七日齊赴元帥府。

translations.literal: On renzi of the second month, an edict ordered civil and military officials to assemble at the commander's office on the seventh of this month.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi officials were ordered to the commander's office on the seventh.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，宰相百官辭，全忠以未斷表為詞。

translations.literal: On guichou, chancellors and officials took leave; Quanzhong used unfinished mourning as pretext.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou ministers took leave; Quanzhong cited unfinished mourning.

sentences.zh: 三月戊寅朔，全忠令大將李思安率兵三萬，合魏博之眾，攻掠幽州。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, wuyin, Quanzhong ordered General Li Si'an to lead thirty thousand troops with Weibo forces to raid You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Li Si'an led thirty thousand with Weibo troops against You.

sentences.zh: 思安頓兵臨其郛，會仁恭子守光率兵赴援，思安乃還。

translations.literal: Si'an halted before the suburbs; when Ren Gong's son Shouguang led troops to rescue, Si'an returned.
translations.idiomatic: Si'an halted at the walls; when Shouguang relieved the city, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔薛貽矩再使大樑，達傳位之旨。

translations.literal: On gengyin, an edict sent Xue Yiju again to Daliang to convey the intent of passing the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Xue Yiju was sent again with the abdication message.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，詔曰：「敕宰臣文武百辟，籓岳庶尹，明聽朕言。

translations.literal: On jiachen, an edict stated: "Edict to chancellors, civil and military officials of the hundred offices, frontier commissioners and prefects—hear Our words clearly.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen an edict addressed all officials and frontier lords.

sentences.zh: 夫大寶之尊，神器之重，儻非德充宇宙，功濟黔黎，著重華納麓之功，彰文命導川之績，允熙帝載，克代天工，則何以統禦萬邦，照臨八極。

translations.literal: The honor of the great treasure and the weight of the sacred vessel—if virtue does not fill the cosmos and merit does not succor the black-haired people, if the weight of accepting the succession at Chonghua and the achievement of guiding rivers like Wenming are not shown, how may one rule the myriad states and shine on the eight extremities?
translations.idiomatic: The throne requires virtue filling heaven and merit saving the people, like the sage emperors of old.

sentences.zh: 元帥梁王，龍顏瑞質，玉理奇文，以英謀睿武定寰瀛，以厚澤深仁撫華夏。

translations.literal: Commander Prince of Liang has a dragon countenance and jade pattern of wondrous script; with heroic plans and keen martial arts he settled the realm within the seas; with deep favor and profound benevolence he comforted the flowering land.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang had a regal bearing and settled the realm with martial prowess and deep benevolence.

sentences.zh: 神功至德，絕後光前，緹油罕紀其鴻勳，謳誦顯歸於至化。

translations.literal: Divine merit and utmost virtue shine after and before; silk and oil rarely record such great achievement—songs of praise clearly return to utmost transformation.
translations.idiomatic: His merit outshone history and songs of praise hailed his rule.

sentences.zh: 二十年之功業，億兆眾之推崇，邇無異言，遠無異望。

translations.literal: Twenty years of achievement and the esteem of hundreds of millions—near, no differing words; far, no differing hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years of achievement won the people's unanimous acclaim.

sentences.zh: 朕惟王聖德，光被八紘，宜順玄穹，膺茲寶命。

translations.literal: We consider the Prince's sage virtue, light covering the eight directions; it is fitting to follow the dark heavens and receive this precious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue covered the realm; he should receive the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 況天文符瑞，雜遝宣明，虞夏昌期，顯於圖籙。

translations.literal: Moreover heavenly signs and auspicious omens were promiscuously declared bright; the flourishing age of Yu and Xia appeared in charts and registers.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly omens and prophecies favored him like Yu and Xia.

sentences.zh: 萬機不可以久曠，天命不可以久違，神祇葉心，歸於有德。

translations.literal: The myriad affairs cannot long be vacant; the Mandate of Heaven cannot long be defied; spirits and gods harmonize in heart and return to the virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: The throne could not stay empty; spirits favored the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 朕敬以天下，傳禪聖君，退居舊籓，以備三恪。

translations.literal: We respectfully yield all under Heaven to the sage lord, retiring to the old fief to prepare the threefold guest honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor yielded the realm and retired as a guest of the new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今敕宰臣張文蔚、楊涉等率文武百僚，備法駕奉迎梁朝，勉厲肅恭，尊戴明主。

translations.literal: Now edict Chancellor Zhang Wenwei, Yang She, and others to lead civil and military officials, prepare the imperial carriage to welcome the Liang court, exerting reverent respect to honor the bright lord.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenwei, Yang She, and others were to welcome the Liang court with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 沖人釋茲重負，永為虞賓，獲奉新朝，慶泰兼極。

translations.literal: The young one lays down this heavy burden, forever a guest of Yu, attaining service in the new court—joy and peace together at the utmost."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would be a guest like Shun—joy in the new court.

sentences.zh: 中外列辟，宜體朕懷。

translations.literal: Central and outer ranks should embody Our mind."
translations.idiomatic: All ranks should heed the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 」乙酉，乃以中書侍郎、平章事張文蔚充冊使，禮部尚書蘇循為副。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Vice Director Zhang Wenwei was made investiture commissioner; Minister of Rites Su Xun was deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Zhang Wenwei led investiture; Su Xun was deputy.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、平章事楊涉押傳國寶使，翰林學士、中書舍人張策為副。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yang She was commissioner for the transmission of the national treasure; Hanlin Academician Zhang Ce was deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Yang She carried the imperial seal; Zhang Ce was deputy.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫薛貽矩為押金寶使，左丞趙光逢為副。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju was commissioner for the golden treasure; Left Vice Director Zhao Guangfeng was deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yiju guarded the golden treasure; Zhao Guangfeng was deputy.

sentences.zh: 甲午，文蔚押文武百僚赴大樑。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Wenwei led civil and military officials to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Wenwei led officials to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 甲子，行事。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the rites were performed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the abdication rites were performed.

sentences.zh: 冊曰：

translations.literal: The investiture document states:
translations.idiomatic: The investiture read:

sentences.zh: 「皇帝若曰：咨爾天下兵馬元帥、相國總百揆梁王，朕每觀上古之書，以堯舜為始者，蓋以禪讓之典垂於無窮。

translations.literal: "The emperor said: Alas for you, Commander-in-Chief of Armies and Horses of All under Heaven, Chancellor overseeing all affairs, Prince of Liang—We each observe books of high antiquity and take Yao and Shun as beginning, because the canon of yielding extends to infinity.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor addressed the Prince of Liang: antiquity shows Yao and Shun began by yielding the throne.

sentences.zh: 故封泰山，禪梁父，略可道者七十二君，則知天下至公，非一姓獨有。

translations.literal: Therefore mounting Tai and yielding at Liangfu—of seventy-two lords who could be spoken of in brief—so one knows all under Heaven is utmost fairness and not possessed by one surname alone.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two rulers who sacrificed show the realm belongs to virtue, not one clan.

sentences.zh: 自古明王聖帝，焦思勞神，惴若納隍，坐以待旦，莫不居之則兢畏，去之則逸安。

translations.literal: Since antiquity bright kings and sage emperors have burned thought and labored spirit, fearful as if falling into a moat, sitting awaiting dawn—none who held it were not wary, none who left it were not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers toiled in office and found ease only in retirement.

sentences.zh: 且軒轅非不明，放勳非不聖，尚欲游于姑射，休彼大庭。

translations.literal: Moreover Xuanyuan was not unenlightened and Yao was not unsage—yet they wished to roam at Guye and rest in the Great Court."
translations.idiomatic: Even Xuanyuan and Yao sought rest from rule.

sentences.zh: 矧乎歷數尋終，期運久謝，屬於孤藐，統禦萬方者哉！

translations.literal: How much more when the sequence nears its end and the allotted span long departed—to belong to the solitary young and rule the myriad directions!
translations.idiomatic: How much less could a youth hold the throne when fate had ended!

sentences.zh: 況自懿祖之後，嬖幸亂朝，禍起有階，政漸無象。

translations.literal: Moreover since the pampered ancestors, favorites disturbed the court; disaster arose by steps and government gradually lost form.
translations.idiomatic: Since mid-Tang, favorites ruined government step by step.

sentences.zh: 天綱幅裂，海水橫流，四紀於茲，群生無庇。

translations.literal: Heaven's net split wide, the sea waters flowed crosswise—four reigns here, the living without shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's net tore, seas flooded—four reigns without shelter for the people.

sentences.zh: 洎乎喪亂，誰其底綏。

translations.literal: Reaching the time of ruin, who could bring peace?
translations.idiomatic: In ruin, who could restore peace?

sentences.zh: 洎于小子，粵以幼年，繼茲衰緒。

translations.literal: Reaching Us, young in years, We succeeded this declining thread.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inherited a failing line in youth.

sentences.zh: 豈茲沖昧，能守洪基？

translations.literal: How could such tender dimness guard the great foundation?
translations.idiomatic: A child could not guard the foundation.

sentences.zh: 惟王明聖在躬，體於上哲。

translations.literal: Only the Prince's sage brightness is in the person, embodying the supreme wise.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Prince embodied supreme wisdom.

sentences.zh: 奮揚神武，戡定區夏，大功二十，光著冊書。

translations.literal: He raised divine martial prowess and quelled the central lands; great achievement for twenty years, light fixed in the records.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years of martial achievement are recorded in history.

sentences.zh: 北越陰山，南逾瘴海，東至碣石，西暨流沙，懷生之倫，罔不悅附。

translations.literal: North beyond Yin Mountain, south beyond malarial seas, east to Jieshi, west to flowing sand—all living kinds none not pleased to attach.
translations.idiomatic: From Yin Mountain to the seas, east to west, all peoples submitted.

sentences.zh: 矧予寡昧，危而獲存。

translations.literal: How much more Our own dimness, peril yet obtaining preservation!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor owed his survival to the Prince.

sentences.zh: 今則上察天文，下觀人願，是土德終極之際，乃金行兆應之辰。

translations.literal: Now above We observe heavenly signs, below human desire—this is the earth virtue's ultimate end and metal's portent responding in season.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and the people showed earth's cycle ending and metal rising.

sentences.zh: 況十載之間，彗星三見，布新除舊，厥有明征，謳歌所歸，屬在睿德。

translations.literal: Moreover within ten years the comet thrice appeared; renewing and removing the old has clear signs; songs of praise return to sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Three comets in ten years showed renewal; praise settled on the Prince.

sentences.zh: 今遣持節、銀青光祿大夫、守中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事張文蔚等，奉皇帝寶綬，敬遜於位。

translations.literal: Now We send Bearer of the Staff, Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Robe, Defender Vice Director Zhang Wenwei and others, bearing the imperial seal and cord, respectfully yielding the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenwei and others bore the seal to yield the throne.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ah!

sentences.zh: 天之歷數在爾躬，允執其中，天祿永終。

translations.literal: Heaven's calendar is upon your person; faithfully hold the center; Heaven's emolument ends forever.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate is yours; hold the center; may fortune endure.

sentences.zh: 王其祗顯大禮，享茲萬國，以肅膺天命。

translations.literal: Prince, respectfully display the great rites, enjoy these myriad states, solemnly receive Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Receive the mandate, perform the great rites, and rule the myriad states.
The investiture concluded.

sentences.zh: 全忠建國，奉帝為濟陰王，遷于曹州，處前刺史氏叔琮之第。

translations.literal: Quanzhong founded his state and made the emperor Prince of Jiyin, moving him to Cao Prefecture to the former prefect's residence of Shi Shuzong.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong made him Prince of Jiyin and moved him to Cao, to Shi Shuzong's old residence.

sentences.zh: 時太原、幽州、鳳翔、西川猶稱天祐正朔。

translations.literal: At that time Taiyuan, Youzhou, Fengxiang, and Xichuan still used the Tianyou reign era.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan, You, Fengxiang, and Shu still kept the Tianyou era.

sentences.zh: 二月二十一日，帝為全忠所害，時年十七，仍諡曰哀皇帝，以王禮葬于濟陰縣之定陶鄉。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the second month the emperor was killed by Quanzhong; he was seventeen; posthumous title Emperor Ai; buried by princely rites at Dingtao in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of the second month Quanzhong killed the seventeen-year-old emperor Ai; he was buried at Dingtao with princely rites.

sentences.zh: 中興之初，方備禮改卜，遇國喪而止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the restoration, suburban rites were prepared and the divination changed, then stopped because of national mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Early restoration had prepared suburban rites, then halted for mourning.

sentences.zh: 明宗時就故陵置園邑，有司請諡曰昭宣光烈孝皇帝，廟號「景宗」。

translations.literal: In Mingzong's time a park was established at the old tomb; the responsible office requested posthumous title Illustrious, Proclaiming, Bright, Fiery, Filial Emperor, temple name "Jingzong."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong later sought temple name Jingzong and a fuller posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 中書覆奏少帝行事，不合稱宗，存諡而已。

translations.literal: The Secretariat re-memorialized that the young emperor's conduct did not fit calling him "zong"; the posthumous title alone was kept.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat said a child emperor should not be called zong—only the posthumous title remained.

sentences.zh: 知禮者亦以宣、景之諡非宜，今只取本諡，載之于紀。

translations.literal: Those who know ritual also held the Xuan and Jing parts of the posthumous title improper; now only the original posthumous title is recorded in the annals."
translations.idiomatic: Ritualists too found parts of the title improper; only the original title is recorded here.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：悲哉！

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historian says: How lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historian writes: How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 土運之將亡也，五常殆盡，百怪斯呈，宇縣瓜分，皇圖瓦解。

translations.literal: When the earth's fortune was about to perish, the five constants were nearly exhausted and a hundred prodigies appeared; the realm was carved up and the imperial design dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: As Tang's earth fortune failed, constants collapsed, omens multiplied, and the realm split apart.

sentences.zh: 昭宗皇帝英猷奮發，志憤陵夷，旁求奇傑之才，欲拯淪胥之運。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong's heroic plans flared up and his will was indignant at decline; he sought extraordinary talents on every side, wishing to rescue a drowning fate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong sought heroes everywhere to save a drowning dynasty.

sentences.zh: 而世途多僻，忠義俱亡，極爵位以待賢豪，罄珍奇而托心腹。

translations.literal: Yet the age's path was mostly perverse and loyalty and righteousness together perished; he exhausted noble rank to await worthies and spent treasures to entrust his inner heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet loyalty died; he heaped rank and treasure on those he trusted.

sentences.zh: 殷勤國士之遇，罕有托孤之賢，豢豐而犬豕轉獰，肉飽而虎狼逾暴。

translations.literal: Earnest as treating a nation's scholar, yet rarely finding one who would entrust orphans; when fodder was plentiful dogs and pigs grew fierce; when meat was full tigers and wolves grew more brutal.
translations.idiomatic: He treated men as national scholars but found no true guardians; fed, his wolves turned fiercer.

sentences.zh: 五侯九伯，無非問鼎之徒；

translations.literal: The Five Marquises and Nine Earls were all men who asked about the cauldrons;
translations.idiomatic: Marquises and earls all coveted the throne;

sentences.zh: 四岳十連，皆畜無君之跡。

translations.literal: the Four Peaks and Ten Links all harbored traces of lacking a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: great lords all acted without a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 雖蕭屏之臣扼腕，岩廊之輔痛心，空銜毀室之悲，寧救喪邦之禍？

translations.literal: Though screen ministers wrung wrists and hall aides grieved at heart, they bore empty grief of a ruined house—how could they rescue the calamity of a lost state?
translations.idiomatic: Ministers grieved but could not save the state.

sentences.zh: 及扶風西幸，洛邑東遷，如寄珠於盜蹠之門，蓄水於尾閭之上，往而不返，夫何言哉！

translations.literal: When he went west to Fufeng and the eastern capital migrated, it was like lodging pearls at a robber's door and storing water on Wei's tail—gone and not returning; what more can be said!
translations.idiomatic: West to Fufeng and eastward migration were like giving pearls to robbers—there was no return.

sentences.zh: 至若川竭山崩，古今同歎；

translations.literal: As for rivers exhausted and mountains collapsed, ancient and modern sigh together;
translations.idiomatic: Rivers dry and mountains fall—ancient and modern alike sigh;

sentences.zh: 虎爭龍戰，興替無常。

translations.literal: tigers contending and dragons battling, rise and fall without constancy.
translations.idiomatic: tiger-and-dragon struggle shifts dynasties without end.

sentences.zh: 縱胠篋之不仁，亦攫金之有道。

translations.literal: Even the unkind who open boxes have a way in seizing gold.
translations.idiomatic: Even thieves seize power by some logic.

sentences.zh: 曹操請刑於椒壺，蓋迫陰謀；

translations.literal: Cao Cao requested punishment at Jiaohu—because he was pressed by hidden plot;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sought punishment at Jiaohu under conspiracy's pressure;

sentences.zh: 馬昭拒命於淩雲，窘於見討。

translations.literal: Sima Zhao refused orders at Lingyun—embarrassed at being attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao defied orders at Lingyun when cornered.

sentences.zh: 誠知醜跡，得以為詞，而全忠所行，止於殘忍。

translations.literal: Truly knowing ugly traces, one may thereby have words—but what Quanzhong carried out stopped at cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier usurpers had excuses; Quanzhong was simply cruel.

sentences.zh: 況自岐遷洛，天子塊然，六軍盡斥于秦人，四面皆環於汴卒。

translations.literal: Moreover from moving from Qi to Luo the Son of Heaven stood alone; the Six Armies was wholly expelled by Qin men; on four sides all were ringed by Bian troops.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang the emperor stood alone, Qin troops held the Six Armies, and Bian soldiers surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 冕旒如寄，纖芥為疑，迎鑾未及於崇朝，剚刃已聞于塗地。

translations.literal: The imperial regalia was like lodged; the slightest matter bred doubt; welcoming the imperial carriage did not reach one morning before blades were heard on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was nominal; doubt was constant; murder came before the emperor could be escorted.

sentences.zh: 立嗣君於南面，斃母后於中闈，黃門與禁旅皆殲，宗室共衣冠並殪。

translations.literal: He established a successor on the south face and killed the empress dowager in the inner quarters; yellow gates and forbidden guards were all destroyed; the imperial clan and officials in caps and robes perished together.
translations.idiomatic: A puppet successor was set up, the empress dowager killed, guards and clan slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 復又盜鐘掩耳，嫁禍於人。

translations.literal: Again he stole the bell and covered his ears, marrying calamity to others.
translations.idiomatic: He stole the bell and blamed others for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 何九六之數窮，偶天人之道盡，目擊斯亂，言之傷心。

translations.literal: Why did the nine-six number reach its end and Heaven and man's way exhaust together—seeing this disorder, to speak of it wounds the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Fate and the way of heaven ended together—the sight wounds the heart.

sentences.zh: 哀帝之時，政由凶族。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ai's time, government came from a vicious clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ai, vicious clans held power.

sentences.zh: 雖揖讓之令，有類于山陽；

translations.literal: Though yielding edicts resembled Shanyang;
translations.idiomatic: Abdication edicts resembled Emperor Xian of Han;

sentences.zh: 而淩逼之權，過逾于侯景。

translations.literal: yet the power of coercion and pressure exceeded Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: but coercion exceeded even Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 人道浸薄，陰騭難征，然以此受終，如何延永！

translations.literal: Human conduct daily thinned and hidden retribution was hard to seek—yet to end thus, how could life be prolonged!
translations.idiomatic: Morality collapsed; ending so, how could the emperor live long?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：勳華受命，揖讓告終。

translations.literal: Praise says: Yao and Shun received the Mandate; yielding announced the end.
translations.idiomatic: Praise: Yao and Shun took the Mandate by yielding.

sentences.zh: 逆取順守，仁道已窮。

translations.literal: Taking by rebellion yet guarding by compliance—the humane way was already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing by force and ruling by pretense exhausted the humane way.

sentences.zh: 暴則短祚，義則延洪。

translations.literal: Violence then short fortune; righteousness then prolonged greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Violence brings short reigns; righteousness long ones.

sentences.zh: 虞賓之禍，非止一宗。

translations.literal: The calamity of the guest of Yu was not limited to one clan.
translations.idiomatic: The guest-of-Yu calamity was not unique to one house.
